name: canvas_apps/lib/CanvasApp.roc
html: ## CanvasApp is what a runner needs from an app, as a type. An app is a model ## you can step with a keyboard and a pointer and ask for a picture, and the ## picture is a list of shapes. Games, a world you fly around, a paint program ## and a movie you can scrub are all one of these, and nothing in this file ## names any of them. ## ## It is a record, not a module found by name. Each app says which value it is ## out loud and hands it to a runner, and a runner is a function of one. import Shapes import Input CanvasApp :: [].{ ## A sound an app can set off: a pitch in hertz and a length in ## milliseconds, which is all either runner needs to make it. Tone : { hertz : U32, milliseconds : U32 } CanvasApp(model) : { # How big a frame is, in the game's own coordinates. size : { width : F64, height : F64 }, # How often it is meant to be stepped. The runner paces to this and # passes a fixed step, so the rules are deterministic: the same keys # at the same ticks play the same game. frames_a_second : U32, init : model, # One step, given what the keyboard looks like now and how long the # step covers. The snapshot is a value, so the browser's event loop # can make one and a test can write one down. The seconds are always # `1 / frames_a_second`: a runner paces to that and passes it, so no game writes # its own sixtieth that might disagree with `frames_a_second`. model_at_next_step : model, Input.Snapshot, F32 -> model, # What to draw. frame_shapes : model -> List(Shapes.Shape), # Which of `tones` the last step set off, as a bit per tone. A game # reports that a sound happened; whether that is a speaker or a widget # in the corner of a web page is the runner's business. The runner # learns how many tones there are from `tones`, never by guessing. sounds : model -> U32, tones : List(CanvasApp.Tone), title : Str, } ## The seconds one step covers, `1 / frames_a_second`, which every runner ## passes to `model_at_next_step`. An app stepped zero times a second never ## moves and its step would be infinite, so a rate of zero crashes. seconds_a_step : CanvasApp.CanvasApp(model) -> F32 seconds_a_step = |canvas_app| if canvas_app.frames_a_second == 0 { crash "CanvasApp.seconds_a_step: an app is stepped at least once a second, never zero times" } else { 1.0 / canvas_app.frames_a_second.to_f32() } # A `model_at_next_step` for an app that needs no seconds: a runner passes # them as ever, and `step` never sees them. A game whose rules count steps # uses it, so real time has no way in. untimed_model_at_next_step : (model, Input.Snapshot -> model) -> (model, Input.Snapshot, F32 -> model) untimed_model_at_next_step = |step| |model, input, _seconds| step(model, input) }

name: canvas_apps/lib/ColorShade.roc
html: ## An opaque color, an `RgbColor`, shaded or blended toward another, channel by ## channel. import Fraction import RgbColor ColorShade :: [].{ ## How a color is shaded: darkened by a fraction of each channel, or ## lightened by one. Shade : [Darkened(Fraction), Lightened(Fraction)] ## A color with each channel shaded, as `shade_channel` shades it. shade_color : RgbColor, ColorShade.Shade -> RgbColor shade_color = |color, shade| RgbColor.from_channels({ red: shade_channel(color.red(), shade), green: shade_channel(color.green(), shade), blue: shade_channel(color.blue(), shade), }) ## The color `fraction` of the way from `from` to `to`, each channel ## rounded to a whole value as `channel_between` rounds it. color_between : { from : RgbColor, to : RgbColor, fraction : Fraction, } -> RgbColor color_between = |{ from, to, fraction }| { blend = |channel_of| channel_between({ from: channel_of(from), to: channel_of(to), fraction, }) RgbColor.from_channels({ red: blend(RgbColor.red), green: blend(RgbColor.green), blue: blend(RgbColor.blue), }) } } ## One channel `fraction` of the way from `from` to `to`, rounded to a whole ## value, half up. channel_between : { from : U8, to : U8, fraction : Fraction, } -> U8 channel_between = |{ from, to, fraction }| { start = from.to_f64() blended = start + (to.to_f64() - start) * fraction.to_f64() rounded = blended.round_to_i64_try() ?? crash "ColorShade.channel_between: a blended channel is a finite number" # A fraction lies from 0 to 1, so the blend lies between two channels. rounded.to_u8_try() ?? crash "ColorShade.channel_between: a blend lies between its two channels" } ## One channel shaded and rounded. Darkened by `f`, it is scaled by the ## whole less `f`; lightened by `f`, by one and `f`, and held at 255 at most. shade_channel : U8, ColorShade.Shade -> U8 shade_channel = |channel, shade| match shade { Darkened(darkening) => { scaled = (channel.to_f64() * darkening.complement().to_f64()).round_to_i64_try() ?? crash "ColorShade.shade_channel: a darkened channel is a finite number" # The scale lies from 0 to 1, so the channel can only fall. scaled.to_u8_try() ?? crash "ColorShade.shade_channel: a darkened channel lies from 0 to its own value" } Lightened(lightening) => { scaled = (channel.to_f64() * (1.0 + lightening.to_f64())).round_to_i64_try() ?? crash "ColorShade.shade_channel: a lightened channel is a finite number" if scaled > 255 { 255 } else { scaled.to_u8_wrap() } } } sample_color : RgbColor sample_color = RgbColor.of(0x804020) expect [ ((128, 0.4), 77), ((64, 0.4), 38), ((32, 0.4), 19), ((255, 0.0), 255), ((0, 0.0), 0), ((200, 1.0), 0), ((255, 1.0), 0), ].all(|((channel, share), want)| shade_channel(channel, Darkened(Fraction.of(share))) == want) # Lightened by a quarter, 203 rounds to 254, 204 lands on 255, and 205 and past # are held there. expect [ ((203, 0.25), 254), ((204, 0.25), 255), ((205, 0.25), 255), ((250, 0.25), 255), ((255, 0.0), 255), ((0, 1.0), 0), ((127, 1.0), 254), ((128, 1.0), 255), ((255, 1.0), 255), ].all(|((channel, share), want)| shade_channel(channel, Lightened(Fraction.of(share))) == want) expect ColorShade.shade_color(sample_color, Darkened(Fraction.of(0.4))) == RgbColor.of(0x4D2613) expect ColorShade.shade_color(sample_color, Lightened(Fraction.of(0.25))) == RgbColor.of(0xA05028) # A channel part way rounds half up, and lands on each end exactly. expect [ ((0, 1, 0.0), 0), ((0, 1, 0.25), 0), ((0, 1, 0.5), 1), ((0, 3, 0.5), 2), ((0, 5, 0.5), 3), ((0, 99, 0.5), 50), ((0, 255, 0.5), 128), ((0, 255, 1.0), 255), ((255, 0, 0.5), 128), ((255, 255, 0.5), 255), ].all( |((from, to, share), want)| { fraction = Fraction.of(share) channel_between({ from, to, fraction }) == want }, ) blend_start : RgbColor blend_start = RgbColor.of(0x8ECAE6) blend_end : RgbColor blend_end = RgbColor.of(0x243A5E) expect ColorShade.color_between({ from: blend_start, to: blend_end, fraction: Fraction.zero, }) == blend_start expect ColorShade.color_between({ from: blend_start, to: blend_end, fraction: Fraction.whole, }) == blend_end expect ColorShade.color_between({ from: blend_start, to: blend_end, fraction: Fraction.of(0.5), }) == RgbColor.of(0x5982A2)

name: canvas_apps/lib/Fraction.roc
html: ## A ratio from 0 to 1: how far through a move, how near dusk, how bright a ## beacon. Only this module can build one, so a value of this type is always ## in range. Anything that can pass 1 has a type of its own. ## ## There are two ways in. `of` takes a ratio that can only be in range, and a ## ratio outside it means the sum that made it is wrong, so `of` crashes. ## `clamp` takes a ratio that can rightly fall outside, such as how far a ## rider has come along a stretch they haven't reached yet. Fraction :: F64.{ ## A ratio that can only be in range, as a fraction. of : F64 -> Fraction of = |ratio| match from_ratio(ratio) { Ok(fraction) => fraction Err(OutOfRange) => crash "Fraction.of: this ratio is outside 0 to 1, so the sum behind it is wrong" } ## The fraction nearest this ratio. clamp : F64 -> Fraction clamp = |ratio| if ratio < 0.0 { zero } else if ratio > 1.0 { whole } else { of(ratio) } to_f64 : Fraction -> F64 to_f64 = |Fraction.(f)| f zero : Fraction zero = Fraction.(0.0) whole : Fraction whole = Fraction.(1.0) ## This fraction of `other`. times : Fraction, Fraction -> Fraction times = |Fraction.(f), Fraction.(other)| Fraction.(f * other) ## What is left of the whole after this fraction: the whole less it. complement : Fraction -> Fraction complement = |Fraction.(f)| Fraction.(1.0 - f) ## The larger of this fraction and `other`. max : Fraction, Fraction -> Fraction max = |Fraction.(f), Fraction.(other)| Fraction.(f.max(other)) is_lt : Fraction, Fraction -> Bool is_lt = |Fraction.(f), Fraction.(other)| f < other is_lte : Fraction, Fraction -> Bool is_lte = |Fraction.(f), Fraction.(other)| f <= other is_gte : Fraction, Fraction -> Bool is_gte = |Fraction.(f), Fraction.(other)| f >= other is_eq : _ } ## This ratio as a fraction. A value that is not a number is out of range. from_ratio : F64 -> Try(Fraction, [OutOfRange]) from_ratio = |ratio| if ratio >= 0.0 and ratio <= 1.0 { Ok(Fraction.(ratio)) } else { Err(OutOfRange) } not_a_number : F64 not_a_number = F64.from_bits(9221120237041090560) infinity : F64 infinity = F64.from_bits(9218868437227405312) negative_zero : F64 negative_zero = F64.from_bits(9223372036854775808) is_fraction : F64 -> Bool is_fraction = |ratio| match from_ratio(ratio) { Ok(_) => True Err(OutOfRange) => False } expect [ (0.0, True), (negative_zero, True), (0.5, True), (1.0, True), (-0.000001, False), (1.000001, False), (not_a_number, False), (infinity, False), ].all(|(ratio, answer)| is_fraction(ratio) == answer) expect [ (-0.5, 0.0), (-0.000001, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0), (0.25, 0.25), (1.0, 1.0), (1.000001, 1.0), (1.5, 1.0), ].all(|(ratio, clamped)| Fraction.clamp(ratio).to_f64() == clamped) # The sums downstream of a clamp can see the sign, so it stays. expect Fraction.clamp(negative_zero).to_f64().to_bits() == negative_zero.to_bits() lesser : Fraction lesser = Fraction.of(0.25) greater : Fraction greater = Fraction.of(0.5) expect lesser < greater expect !(greater < greater) expect !(greater < lesser) expect lesser <= greater expect greater <= greater expect !(greater <= lesser) expect !(lesser >= greater) expect greater >= greater expect greater >= lesser expect greater == greater expect !(lesser == greater)

name: canvas_apps/lib/Shapes.roc
html: ## Shapes is the vocabulary every app's frame is written in. A frame is a list ## of these shapes in the app's own coordinates, and each painter draws the list ## in order. What one app draws is built in that app's own folder. import Brush import Pixels import Point Shapes :: [].{ ## One thing in a frame. A later shape in the list paints over an earlier one. ## A shape is a region and a fill: any of the four regions takes any fill. Shape : [ ## Three corners, which is every triangle and nothing else. Triangle( { first : Point, second : Point, third : Point, fill : Brush.Fill, }, ), ## Four corners in order around the edge. `Shapes.rectangle` makes an ## upright one. Quad( { first : Point, second : Point, third : Point, fourth : Point, fill : Brush.Fill, }, ), ## A circle, `radius` out from `center`. Disc( { center : Point, radius : Pixels, fill : Brush.Fill, }, ), ## An outline of any other number of corners, in order around its edge: a ## traced still, a mountain, the road. Polygon({ corners : List(Point), fill : Brush.Fill }), ## A mark, not a shape: how the shapes after it combine, until the next `Blend`. ## A painter holds this as a mode, so a mark in the list says it directly. ## `Shapes.added_light_shapes` writes the pair of marks around a run of shapes. Blend(Shapes.Mode), ## A mark, not a shape: the space the shapes after it are in, until the next ## `View`. It is a mark for the same reason `Blend` is. `Shapes.shapes_in_space` ## writes the pair of marks around a run of shapes. View(Shapes.Space), ## `cols` by `rows` pixels stretched over the box without smoothing. It carries ## the pixels, not a handle, so there is no second copy of them to keep in step. Image( { x : F64, y : F64, width : F64, height : F64, cols : U64, rows : U64, pixels : List(Brush.Rgba), }, ), ## A line of words in a real typeface. `Font.plotted_shapes` gives a painter that has ## no typefaces the strokes of the same line. Text(Shapes.TextLine), ] ## A line of type. `y` is its baseline, `x` its left end or its middle as `align` ## says, and `size` the height of its em square, as in CSS. The viewer's machine ## chooses the typeface and measures the words, so nothing in Roc knows how wide ## the line came out: `Font.room_for` is the room to leave for it. TextLine : { text : Str, x : F64, y : F64, size : F64, face : Shapes.Face, align : Shapes.Align, color : Brush.Rgba, } ## `Prose` is the viewer's own sans serif, for words. `Code` is a monospace, for ## what a program says. Face : [Prose, Code] Align : [Left, Center] ## `Over` paints over what is there. `Add` adds light to it, which is what a glow ## is. Mode : [Over, Add] ## The space the shapes after a `View` mark are in. `Screen` is the game's own ## pixels, where every frame starts. `World` carries points and numbers rather than a ## Camera, because the mark crosses to JavaScript, which has no such type. As in ## a Camera, the world point `target` lands on the screen point `offset`, turned ## clockwise by `rotation` degrees and scaled by `zoom`. `world_space` is the ## way to make a `World`, because it checks the zoom. Space : [ Screen, World( { target : Point, offset : Point, rotation : F64, zoom : F64, }, ), ] ## A `World` space, its zoom checked. A zoom of zero has no inverse, so a ## painter could not map the screen back into this space, and a zoom that is ## not finite comes only from a bug; either crashes. world_space : { target : Point, offset : Point, rotation : F64, zoom : F64, } -> Shapes.Space world_space = |world| if world.zoom == 0.0 or !world.zoom.is_finite() { crash "Shapes.world_space: a zoom must be finite and not zero" } else { World(world) } ## The shapes lit in `Add` mode, so each adds its light to what is under it, ## and the mode back to `Over` after them. added_light_shapes : List(Shapes.Shape) -> List(Shapes.Shape) added_light_shapes = |shapes| shapes.prepend(Blend(Add)).append(Blend(Over)) ## The shapes in `space`, and the space back to the screen after them. shapes_in_space : Shapes.Space, List(Shapes.Shape) -> List(Shapes.Shape) shapes_in_space = |space, shapes| Shapes.lists_in_space(space, [shapes]) ## The shapes of each of `shape_lists` in turn, in `space`, and the space back ## to the screen after them: what `shapes_in_space` gives for the lists joined, with ## every shape copied once. lists_in_space : Shapes.Space, List(List(Shapes.Shape)) -> List(Shapes.Shape) lists_in_space = | space, shape_lists, | [[View(space)]].concat(shape_lists).append([View(Screen)]).join() ## The region round `corners`, in order, tagged by how many there are: three ## make a `Triangle`, four a `Quad`, and any other number a `Polygon`. Every ## maker that works through a list of corners comes here, so the count ## always matches the tag. region_from_corners : List(Point), Brush.Fill -> Shapes.Shape region_from_corners = |corners, fill| match corners { [first, second, third] => Triangle({ first, second, third, fill }) [first, second, third, fourth] => Quad({ first, second, third, fourth, fill }) _ => Polygon({ corners, fill }) } ## The corners of a straight-edged region, in order round its edge. A disc, ## a picture, a line of type and a mark have no corners to give. region_corners : Shapes.Shape -> Try(List(Point), [NoCorners]) region_corners = |shape| match shape { Triangle(t) => Ok([t.first, t.second, t.third]) Quad(q) => Ok([q.first, q.second, q.third, q.fourth]) Polygon(p) => Ok(p.corners) Disc(_) | Image(_) | Text(_) | Blend(_) | View(_) => Err(NoCorners) } ## An upright box, `width` across and `height` down from `top_left`, as the ## quad it is: clockwise on the screen from its top left corner. rectangle : { top_left : Point, width : Pixels, height : Pixels, fill : Brush.Fill, } -> Shapes.Shape rectangle = |{ top_left, width, height, fill }| { right = top_left.x.plus(width) bottom = top_left.y.plus(height) Quad({ first: top_left, second: { x: right, y: top_left.y }, third: { x: right, y: bottom }, fourth: { x: top_left.x, y: bottom }, fill, }) } ## A line `width` pixels wide between two points, as the quad it is, so no ## painter has to learn a stroke. It has no cap and no join, which suits a ## gridline. A line from a point to itself has no direction to be wide ## across, and crashes. line : { from : Point, to : Point, width : Pixels, }, Brush.Fill -> Shapes.Shape line = |{ from, to, width }, fill| { x0 = from.x.to_f64() y0 = from.y.to_f64() x1 = to.x.to_f64() y1 = to.y.to_f64() dx = x1 - x0 dy = y1 - y0 length = (dx * dx + dy * dy).sqrt() if length == 0.0 { crash "Shapes.line: a line from a point to itself" } else { # The unit normal, half a width each way. half_width = width.to_f64() / 2.0 nx = 0.0 - dy / length * half_width ny = dx / length * half_width Quad({ first: Point.at(x0 + nx, y0 + ny), second: Point.at(x1 + nx, y1 + ny), third: Point.at(x1 - nx, y1 - ny), fourth: Point.at(x0 - nx, y0 - ny), fill, }) } } ## A circle's outline, `line_width` wide around the rim, as `sides` sectors ## of the band between two circles. Neighbouring sectors share their edge ## exactly, so the band has no gap at a corner. A disc under a smaller disc ## makes a ring too, but only on a background of a known flat color. Fewer ## than three sides enclose nothing, and crash. ring_shapes : { center : Point, radius : Pixels, line_width : Pixels, sides : U64, }, Brush.Fill -> List(Shapes.Shape) ring_shapes = |{ center, radius, line_width, sides }, fill| if sides < 3 { crash "Shapes.ring_shapes: a ring needs at least three sides" } else { inner_radius = radius.to_f64() - line_width.to_f64() / 2.0 outer_radius = radius.to_f64() + line_width.to_f64() / 2.0 cx = center.x.to_f64() cy = center.y.to_f64() # The last side ends at angle 0 itself, not at a whole turn, so it # meets the first side's corners exactly. rim_point = |r, k| { angle = F64.tau * (k % sides).to_f64() / sides.to_f64() Point.at(cx + r * angle.cos(), cy + r * angle.sin()) } var $out = List.with_capacity(sides) for k in 0..<sides { sector = Quad({ first: rim_point(outer_radius, k), second: rim_point(outer_radius, k + 1), third: rim_point(inner_radius, k + 1), fourth: rim_point(inner_radius, k), fill, }) $out = $out.append(sector) } $out } ## Every x pulled toward `axis` by `cosine`, so a figure drawn face-on reads as one ## turned away by the angle whose cosine that is. A negative cosine mirrors it as ## well, so a pair beside a path can face each other. A disc keeps its radius, ## because no shape here is an ellipse. A mirror only reverses the order a ## region's corners go round in, which no painter minds. Only a flat fill can ## be squashed: a gradient's geometry would stay where it was while its shape ## moved, so a region with a gradient crashes. squashed_shapes : List(Shapes.Shape), { axis : Pixels, cosine : F64 } -> List(Shapes.Shape) squashed_shapes = |shapes, { axis, cosine: k }| shapes.map( |shape| match shape { Triangle(t) => Triangle({ first: pulled_point(t.first, { axis, cosine: k }), second: pulled_point(t.second, { axis, cosine: k }), third: pulled_point(t.third, { axis, cosine: k }), fill: squashable_fill(t.fill), }) Quad(q) => Quad({ first: pulled_point(q.first, { axis, cosine: k }), second: pulled_point(q.second, { axis, cosine: k }), third: pulled_point(q.third, { axis, cosine: k }), fourth: pulled_point(q.fourth, { axis, cosine: k }), fill: squashable_fill(q.fill), }) Polygon(p) => Polygon({ corners: p.corners.map(|corner| pulled_point(corner, { axis, cosine: k })), fill: squashable_fill(p.fill), }) Disc(d) => Disc({ center: pulled_point(d.center, { axis, cosine: k }), radius: d.radius, fill: squashable_fill(d.fill), }) Blend(m) => Blend(m) View(l) => View(l) # A mirror sends a picture's left edge to its right, and a width is # never negative. Image(i) => { span = pulled_span( { x: i.x, width: i.width }, { axis: axis.to_f64(), cosine: k }, ) Image({ ..i, x: span.x, width: span.width }) } # Type keeps its letterforms, so only its place moves. Text(t) => Text({ ..t, x: axis.to_f64() + (t.x - axis.to_f64()) * k }) }, ) ## A picture `cols` by `rows` pixels, row by row, stretched over the box. A ## pixel list of any other length crashes: a painter would read past its end ## or leave some of it out. image : { x : F64, y : F64, width : F64, height : F64, cols : U64, rows : U64, pixels : List(Brush.Rgba), } -> Shapes.Shape image = |picture| if picture.pixels.len() != picture.cols * picture.rows { crash "Shapes.image: a picture's pixels number its cols times its rows" } else { Image(picture) } ## Light in `color` at the middle, at the colour's own alpha, fading to ## nothing at `radius`. halo : { center : Point, radius : Pixels }, Brush.Rgba -> Shapes.Shape halo = |{ center, radius }, color| Disc({ center, radius, fill: Radial({ inner_color: color, outer_color: { ..color, a: 0.0 }, center, inner_radius: Pixels.zero, outer_radius: radius, }), }) ## A rectangle whose corners are rounded by `corner_radius`, each corner drawn in ## `corner_steps` steps. A radius of zero or no steps gives the plain box, and a ## radius too big for the box is held to half its shorter side. rounded_rect : { top_left : Point, width : Pixels, height : Pixels, corner_radius : Pixels, corner_steps : U64, }, Brush.Fill -> Shapes.Shape rounded_rect = |box, fill| { x = box.top_left.x.to_f64() y = box.top_left.y.to_f64() width = box.width.to_f64() height = box.height.to_f64() corner_steps = box.corner_steps radius = box.corner_radius.to_f64().min((width / 2.0).min(height / 2.0)) if radius <= 0.0 or corner_steps == 0 { Shapes.rectangle({ top_left: box.top_left, width: box.width, height: box.height, fill, }) } else { var $corners = List.with_capacity(4 * (corner_steps + 1)) # Clockwise from the top-left corner, each swept from its own start angle. $corners = quarter_turn_corners( $corners, { center: { x: x + radius, y: y + radius }, radius, start_angle: half_pi * 2.0, steps: corner_steps, }, ) $corners = quarter_turn_corners( $corners, { center: { x: x + width - radius, y: y + radius }, radius, start_angle: -half_pi, steps: corner_steps, }, ) $corners = quarter_turn_corners( $corners, { center: { x: x + width - radius, y: y + height - radius }, radius, start_angle: 0.0, steps: corner_steps, }, ) $corners = quarter_turn_corners( $corners, { center: { x: x + radius, y: y + height - radius }, radius, start_angle: half_pi, steps: corner_steps, }, ) Polygon({ corners: $corners, fill }) } } } ## A squashed shape's fill, which must be flat: a gradient's geometry is in the ## shape's coordinates, and squashing moves the shape but not the gradient. squashable_fill : Brush.Fill -> Brush.Fill squashable_fill = |fill| match fill { Flat(_) => fill Span(_) | Radial(_) | Linear(_) | Ellipse(_) | Glow(_) => crash "Shapes.squashed_shapes: a gradient fill would not move with its shape" } ## A point's x pulled toward `axis` by `cosine`. pulled_point : Point, { axis : Pixels, cosine : F64 } -> Point pulled_point = |{ x, y }, { axis, cosine: k }| { x: Pixels.of(axis.to_f64() + (x.to_f64() - axis.to_f64()) * k), y, } ## A span across x pulled toward `axis` by `cosine`, each edge on its own. A ## mirror sends the left edge to the right, so the span starts at whichever ## edge lands leftmost. pulled_span : { x : F64, width : F64 }, { axis : F64, cosine : F64 } -> { x : F64, width : F64 } pulled_span = |{ x, width }, { axis, cosine: k }| { start_x = axis + (x - axis) * k end_x = axis + (x + width - axis) * k { x: start_x.min(end_x), width: (end_x - start_x).abs() } } half_pi : F64 half_pi = F64.pi / 2.0 ## The corners of a quarter turn about `center`, starting at `start_angle`, ## onto `corners`. quarter_turn_corners : List(Point), { center : { x : F64, y : F64 }, radius : F64, start_angle : F64, steps : U64, } -> List(Point) quarter_turn_corners = |corners, { center, radius, start_angle, steps }| { var $out = corners for k in 0..=steps { a = start_angle + half_pi * k.to_f64() / steps.to_f64() $out = $out.append(Point.at(center.x + radius * a.cos(), center.y + radius * a.sin())) } $out } ## A line of type 100 px from the axis at 0. line_of_type : Shapes.TextLine line_of_type = { text: "Hi", x: 100.0, y: 20.0, size: 16.0, face: Code, align: Center, color: { r: 32.0, g: 32.0, b: 32.0, a: 1.0, }, } expect Shapes.squashed_shapes( [Text(line_of_type)], { axis: Pixels.of(0.0), cosine: 0.5 }, ) == [Text({ ..line_of_type, x: 50.0 })] expect Shapes.squashed_shapes( [Text(line_of_type)], { axis: Pixels.of(0.0), cosine: -1.0 }, ) == [Text({ ..line_of_type, x: -100.0 })] expect Shapes.squashed_shapes( [Text(line_of_type)], { axis: Pixels.of(100.0), cosine: 0.5 }, ) == [Text(line_of_type)] ## The fill the shapes below are drawn in. ink : Brush.Fill ink = Flat({ r: 32.0, g: 32.0, b: 32.0, a: 1.0, }) ## A dot of light, as the shape both brackets hold. dot : Shapes.Shape dot = Disc({ center: Point.at(1.0, 2.0), radius: Pixels.of(3.0), fill: ink, }) expect Shapes.added_light_shapes([dot]) == [Blend(Add), dot, Blend(Over)] expect Shapes.added_light_shapes([]) == [Blend(Add), Blend(Over)] expect Shapes.shapes_in_space(Screen, [dot]) == [View(Screen), dot, View(Screen)] expect Shapes.shapes_in_space(Screen, []) == [View(Screen), View(Screen)] expect Shapes.lists_in_space(Screen, [[dot], [], [ink_dot, dot]]) == [ View(Screen), dot, ink_dot, dot, View(Screen), ] expect Shapes.lists_in_space(Screen, []) == [View(Screen), View(Screen)] ## A second dot, so an order shows. ink_dot : Shapes.Shape ink_dot = Disc({ center: Point.at(5.0, 6.0), radius: Pixels.of(1.0), fill: ink, }) # A small zoom, near the zero it refuses, makes a world space. expect { corner = Point.at(0.0, 0.0) world = { target: corner, offset: corner, rotation: 0.0, zoom: 0.001, } Shapes.world_space(world) == World(world) } # A picture two pixels wide and one high holds two pixels. expect { white = { r: 255.0, g: 255.0, b: 255.0, a: 1.0, } picture = { x: 0.0, y: 0.0, width: 4.0, height: 2.0, cols: 2, rows: 1, pixels: [white, white], } Shapes.image(picture) == Image(picture) } ## Five corners round a house's end: up a wall, the roof's two slopes, down the ## other wall, and back along the floor. house_corners : List(Point) house_corners = [ Point.at(10.0, 1.0), Point.at(10.0, 5.0), Point.at(20.0, 9.0), Point.at(30.0, 5.0), Point.at(30.0, 1.0), ] # A flat polygon and a flat disc are squashed toward the axis with their fills. expect Shapes.squashed_shapes( [Polygon({ corners: house_corners, fill: ink }), dot], { axis: Pixels.of(10.0), cosine: 0.5 }, ) == [ Polygon({ corners: [ Point.at(10.0, 1.0), Point.at(10.0, 5.0), Point.at(15.0, 9.0), Point.at(20.0, 5.0), Point.at(20.0, 1.0), ], fill: ink, }), Disc({ center: Point.at(5.5, 2.0), radius: Pixels.of(3.0), fill: ink, }), ] # A triangle's corners are squashed as a polygon's are. expect Shapes.squashed_shapes( [ Triangle({ first: Point.at(10.0, 1.0), second: Point.at(20.0, 2.0), third: Point.at(30.0, 3.0), fill: ink, }), ], { axis: Pixels.of(10.0), cosine: 0.5 }, ) == [ Triangle({ first: Point.at(10.0, 1.0), second: Point.at(15.0, 2.0), third: Point.at(20.0, 3.0), fill: ink, }), ] # A mirrored rectangle keeps its corners in their order, so its left corners # land on the right: the quad goes round the other way. expect Shapes.squashed_shapes( [ Shapes.rectangle({ top_left: Point.at(20.0, 1.0), width: Pixels.of(10.0), height: Pixels.of(4.0), fill: ink, }), ], { axis: Pixels.of(10.0), cosine: -0.5 }, ) == [ Quad({ first: Point.at(5.0, 1.0), second: Point.at(0.0, 1.0), third: Point.at(0.0, 5.0), fourth: Point.at(5.0, 5.0), fill: ink, }), ] # A rectangle is the quad clockwise on the screen from its top left corner. expect Shapes.rectangle({ top_left: Point.at(2.0, 3.0), width: Pixels.of(4.0), height: Pixels.of(5.0), fill: ink, }) == Quad({ first: Point.at(2.0, 3.0), second: Point.at(6.0, 3.0), third: Point.at(6.0, 8.0), fourth: Point.at(2.0, 8.0), fill: ink, }) # Three corners make a triangle, four a quad, and five a polygon, and each # gives back the corners it was made from. expect { three = house_corners.take_first(3) four = house_corners.take_first(4) tagged = [three, four, house_corners].map(|corners| Shapes.region_from_corners(corners, ink)) match tagged { [ Triangle(_), Quad(_), Polygon(_), ] => tagged.map(Shapes.region_corners) == [ Ok(three), Ok(four), Ok(house_corners), ] _ => False } } # Fewer than three corners enclose nothing, and are still a polygon rather # than a crash. expect { two = house_corners.take_first(2) Shapes.region_from_corners(two, ink) == Polygon({ corners: two, fill: ink }) } # A disc and a mark have no corners. expect [dot, Blend(Add)].map(Shapes.region_corners) == [Err(NoCorners), Err(NoCorners)] # A horizontal line two wide stands one each side of its axis. expect Shapes.line( { from: Point.at(0.0, 0.0), to: Point.at(10.0, 0.0), width: Pixels.of(2.0), }, ink, ) == Quad({ first: Point.at(0.0, 1.0), second: Point.at(10.0, 1.0), third: Point.at(10.0, -1.0), fourth: Point.at(0.0, -1.0), fill: ink, }) # The fewest sides a ring may have make three sectors. expect Shapes.ring_shapes( { center: Point.at(0.0, 0.0), radius: Pixels.of(5.0), line_width: Pixels.of(1.0), sides: 3, }, ink, ).len() == 3 ## A ring sector's corners: outer start, outer end, inner end, inner start. sector_corners : Shapes.Shape -> List(Point) sector_corners = |shape| match shape { Quad(q) => [q.first, q.second, q.third, q.fourth] Triangle(_) | Disc(_) | Polygon(_) | Blend(_) | View(_) | Image(_) | Text(_) => crash "Shapes: a ring's sectors are all quads" } # Each sector starts where the one before it ends, outer corner and inner # corner, all the way round to the first again. Its inner corners sit nearer # the center than its outer ones, by the line's width. expect { sectors = Shapes.ring_shapes( { center: Point.at(3.0, 4.0), radius: Pixels.of(10.0), line_width: Pixels.of(2.0), sides: 7, }, ink, ).map(sector_corners) first = sectors.first() ?? crash "Shapes: a ring of seven sides has sectors" following = sectors.drop_first(1).append(first) shared = sectors.map2( following, |sector, next| sector.get(1) == next.get(0) and sector.get(2) == next.get(3), ) outer = first.get(0) ?? crash "Shapes: a sector has an outer start corner" inner = first.get(3) ?? crash "Shapes: a sector has an inner start corner" sectors.len() == 7 and shared.all(|same| same) and outer.x - inner.x == Pixels.of(2.0) }

name: canvas_apps/lib/WasmApp.roc
html: ## WasmApp turns a CanvasApp into what the canvas apps' wasm platform asks ## for, which is the same for every app. The platform asks for eleven ## functions over a boxed model: box it, step it with the tick's keys, answer ## its shapes, and say which tones went off. `program` takes a CanvasApp and ## names none, so an app's wasm file only names its app. import CanvasApp import Input import Mouse import Shapes WasmApp :: [].{ # Roc reads `game.frame_shapes(m)` as a method call, so each of a game's # functions is bound before it is used, under its own name. # # The seven numbers a tick carries are one Input.Snapshot, flattened: the # wasm edge has no records, so the runner packs and this unpacks. program : CanvasApp.CanvasApp(model) -> { init : {} -> Box(model), model_at_next_step : Box(model), U32, U32, U32, U32, F32, F32, F32 -> Box(model), frame_shapes : Box(model) -> List(Shapes.Shape), release : List(Shapes.Shape) -> {}, sounds : Box(model) -> U32, tone_count : {} -> U32, tone_freq : U32 -> U32, tone_ms : U32 -> U32, width : {} -> U32, height : {} -> U32, fps : {} -> U32, } program = |game| { # The step a tick covers, which is the rate the game asked to be run at. seconds_a_step = CanvasApp.seconds_a_step(game) model_at_next_step = game.model_at_next_step frame_shapes = game.frame_shapes sounds = game.sounds { init: |{}| Box.box(game.init), model_at_next_step: | boxed_model, key_held, key_struck, button_held, button_struck, x, y, wheel, | Box.box( model_at_next_step( Box.unbox(boxed_model), Input.of({ held: key_held, struck: key_struck, mouse: Mouse.of({ held: button_held, struck: button_struck, at: { x, y }, wheel, }), }), seconds_a_step, ), ), frame_shapes: |boxed_model| frame_shapes(Box.unbox(boxed_model)), # The host hands the frame back and Roc drops it. Releasing a # List(Shape) means decrementing each element's inner lists, which # needs the tag union's layout. Roc has that layout and the host # doesn't, so the host returns the frame rather than freeing it. release: |_frame| {}, sounds: |boxed_model| sounds(Box.unbox(boxed_model)), tone_count: |{}| tone_count_of(game.tones), tone_freq: |i| tone_at(game.tones, i).hertz, tone_ms: |i| tone_at(game.tones, i).milliseconds, width: |{}| game.size.width.to_u32_try() ?? crash "WasmApp.program: a width outside a U32's range", height: |{}| game.size.height.to_u32_try() ?? crash "WasmApp.program: a height outside a U32's range", fps: |{}| game.frames_a_second, } } } ## How many tones an app may have: `CanvasApp.sounds` answers a U32, one bit ## for each tone. most_tones : U64 most_tones = 32 ## How many tones `tones` holds, for the host. A tone past `most_tones` has no ## bit in `sounds`, so the app could never set it off, and that crashes. tone_count_of : List(CanvasApp.Tone) -> U32 tone_count_of = |tones| if tones.len() > most_tones { crash "WasmApp.program: an app has ${tones.len().to_str()} tones, and CanvasApp.sounds has a bit for only ${most_tones.to_str()}" } else { tones.len().to_u32_wrap() } expect tone_count_of([]) == 0 expect tone_count_of(List.repeat({ hertz: 440, milliseconds: 80 }, 32)) == 32 # The host asks only for a tone below the count it was given, so one past the # end is a bug on the host's side. tone_at : List(CanvasApp.Tone), U32 -> CanvasApp.Tone tone_at = | tones, i, | tones.get(i.to_u64()) ?? crash "WasmApp.tone_at: the host asked for a tone past the end of the app's tones"

name: canvas_apps/safari/Along.roc
html: ## A place along one segment of the road, in metres from that segment's start, ## which is the only origin an `Along` has. It may lie before the start or past ## the end, as a point on the next segment does when it is measured on this one. ## A place measured from anywhere else, such as the segment's end, is a ## `Distance` named for where it is from, and becomes an `Along` only through ## the segment's length. ## `Along` and `Across` mirror `Angle.Bearing` and `Angle.Turn`: a distance added ## to a place gives a place, and two places give the distance between them, but ## two places can't be added. A place along the road can't be passed as a place ## across it. import Distance Along :: F64.{ metres : F64 -> Along metres = |metres| Along.(metres) to_metres : Along -> F64 to_metres = |Along.(a)| a ## The segment's start. start : Along start = Along.(0.0) ## The place this far from the segment's start. at : Distance -> Along at = |distance| Along.(distance.to_metres()) ## How far this place is from the segment's start. from_start : Along -> Distance from_start = |Along.(a)| Distance.metres(a) ## The place `distance` further along. plus : Along, Distance -> Along plus = |Along.(a), distance| Along.(a + distance.to_metres()) ## The place `distance` back along. minus : Along, Distance -> Along minus = |Along.(a), distance| Along.(a - distance.to_metres()) ## How far this place is ahead of `other`: negative when it is behind. distance_from : Along, Along -> Distance distance_from = |Along.(a), Along.(other)| Distance.metres(a - other) is_gt : Along, Along -> Bool is_gt = |Along.(a), Along.(other)| a > other is_gte : Along, Along -> Bool is_gte = |Along.(a), Along.(other)| a >= other is_lt : Along, Along -> Bool is_lt = |Along.(a), Along.(other)| a < other is_lte : Along, Along -> Bool is_lte = |Along.(a), Along.(other)| a <= other is_eq : _ } ## Just under, at and just over 2.5 m, and how `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` and `==` ## answer against 2.5 m there. expect [ (2.0, [True, True, False, False, False]), (2.5, [False, True, False, True, True]), (3.0, [False, False, True, True, False]), ].all( |(metres, want)| { along = Along.metres(metres) held = Along.metres(2.5) [ along < held, along <= held, along > held, along >= held, along == held, ] == want }, )

name: canvas_apps/safari/Animation.roc
html: ## How an animal plays out on the ride: its timeline. A timeline is a list of ## frames and how to show one, so an animal's whole animation reads in one ## place, and it turns a `Stage`, where the animation has got to, into an ## `Instant`, what the animal shows then. Nothing here plays a timeline but that ## lookup, and nothing here knows when the animation starts: that is ## EncounterPlan's. The instants before and after are the timeline's own, ## because an animal can rest somewhere no frame ever reaches. import Across import Along import Distance import Easing import lib.Fraction import Geom import Steps Animation :: [].{ ## Where an animation has got to: not begun, playing and this many steps in, ## which is the frame it shows, or over this many steps ago. Stage : [Waiting, Playing(Steps), Past(Steps)] ## Where an animal is: a place on its segment, and how high it is off the ## ground. Location : { road_point : Geom.RoadPoint, lift : Distance } ## The location `fraction` of the way from `from` to `to`, in a straight line. location_between : { from : Animation.Location, to : Animation.Location, fraction : Fraction, } -> Animation.Location location_between = |{ from, to, fraction }| { between = |start, end| Easing.lerp({ from: start, to: end, fraction }) { road_point: { along: Along.metres( between(from.road_point.along.to_metres(), to.road_point.along.to_metres()), ), across: Across.metres( between(from.road_point.across.to_metres(), to.road_point.across.to_metres()), ), }, lift: Distance.metres(between(from.lift.to_metres(), to.lift.to_metres())), } } ## An animal at one instant: how it looks, and where it is. Instant(pose) : { pose : pose, location : Animation.Location } ## `instant` as an object on the road: it stands at the instant's location, ## and its kind is the instant's pose. placed_instant : Animation.Instant(pose) -> Geom.Placed({ pose : pose }) placed_instant = |{ pose, location }| { road_point: location.road_point, lift: location.lift, kind: { pose: pose }, } ## A whole animation: the animal at rest before, the frames it plays through, ## one a step, and the animal at rest after. The frames are the animation's ## choreography, a constant list, and `frame_instant` turns a frame into the ## animal then, so playing a frame builds only that frame. Timeline(frame, pose) :: { before : Animation.Instant(pose), frames : List(frame), frame_instant : frame -> Animation.Instant(pose), after : Animation.Instant(pose), }.{ ## The timeline that rests at `before`, plays `frames` one a step, each ## shown by `frame_instant`, then rests at `after`. of : { before : Animation.Instant(pose), frames : List(frame), frame_instant : frame -> Animation.Instant(pose), after : Animation.Instant(pose), } -> Animation.Timeline(frame, pose) of = |parts| Animation.Timeline.(parts) ## The animal at `stage`. instant : Animation.Timeline(frame, pose), Animation.Stage -> Animation.Instant(pose) instant = |Animation.Timeline.(timeline), stage| match stage { Waiting => timeline.before Playing(steps_in) => match timeline.frames.get(steps_in.to_u64()) { Ok(frame) => (timeline.frame_instant)(frame) Err(OutOfBounds) => crash "Animation.Timeline.instant: a stage plays past the last frame, so the span it was staged by disagrees with its timeline" } Past(_) => timeline.after } } } Note : [First, Second, Third, Fourth, BeforeIt, AfterIt] sideways_location : F64 -> Animation.Location sideways_location = |across| { road_point: { along: Along.metres(0.0), across: Across.metres(across) }, lift: Distance.zero, } ## A timeline of four frames, each a note and where it is, as far across as ten ## times its place in the list. four_frames : Animation.Timeline({ note : Note, location : Animation.Location }, Note) four_frames = Animation.Timeline.of({ before: { pose: BeforeIt, location: sideways_location(-1.0) }, frames: [ { note: First, location: sideways_location(0.0) }, { note: Second, location: sideways_location(10.0) }, { note: Third, location: sideways_location(20.0) }, { note: Fourth, location: sideways_location(30.0) }, ], frame_instant: |{ note, location }| { pose: note, location }, after: { pose: AfterIt, location: sideways_location(99.0) }, }) ## The pose and how far across the timeline is at `stage`. four_frames_at : Animation.Stage -> (Note, F64) four_frames_at = |stage| { instant = four_frames.instant(stage) (instant.pose, instant.location.road_point.across.to_metres()) } # Each step in plays the frame of its number, the first and the last included; # before them and past them the timeline rests. expect [ (Waiting, (BeforeIt, -1.0)), (Playing(Steps.zero), (First, 0.0)), (Playing(Steps.of(1)), (Second, 10.0)), (Playing(Steps.of(2)), (Third, 20.0)), (Playing(Steps.of(3)), (Fourth, 30.0)), (Past(Steps.zero), (AfterIt, 99.0)), ].all(|(stage, want)| four_frames_at(stage) == want) start_location : Animation.Location start_location = { road_point: { along: Along.metres(10.0), across: Across.metres(20.0) }, lift: Distance.metres(30.0), } end_location : Animation.Location end_location = { road_point: { along: Along.metres(18.0), across: Across.metres(4.0) }, lift: Distance.metres(46.0), } ## The location's three parts, `fraction` of the way from `start_location` to `end_location`. location_numbers : F64 -> List(F64) location_numbers = |fraction| { location = Animation.location_between({ from: start_location, to: end_location, fraction: Fraction.of(fraction), }) point = location.road_point [point.along.to_metres(), point.across.to_metres(), location.lift.to_metres()] } expect [ (0.0, [10.0, 20.0, 30.0]), (0.25, [12.0, 16.0, 34.0]), (1.0, [18.0, 4.0, 46.0]), ].all(|(fraction, want)| location_numbers(fraction) == want)

name: canvas_apps/safari/Attention.roc
html: ## How strongly something holds the rider's eye, from 0 upward. A look to the ## side at its fullest is 1, and a cat in the road holds the eye harder than ## that, so this is no `Fraction`. import lib.Fraction Attention :: F64.{ ## Attention of this strength. Nothing holds the eye less than not at all, ## so a strength below zero means the sum behind it is wrong. of : F64 -> Attention of = |strength| if strength < 0.0 { crash "Attention.of: this strength is below zero, so the sum behind it is wrong" } else { Attention.(strength) } from_fraction : Fraction -> Attention from_fraction = |fraction| Attention.(fraction.to_f64()) to_f64 : Attention -> F64 to_f64 = |Attention.(a)| a ## Nothing is holding the rider's eye. none : Attention none = Attention.(0.0) ## This fraction of this attention. scaled_by : Attention, Fraction -> Attention scaled_by = |Attention.(a), fraction| Attention.(fraction.to_f64() * a) ## The stronger of this attention and `other`. max : Attention, Attention -> Attention max = |Attention.(a), Attention.(other)| Attention.(a.max(other)) is_eq : _ } expect Attention.none.to_f64() == 0.0 expect Attention.of(1.8).to_f64() == 1.8 expect Attention.of(0.0) == Attention.none expect Attention.from_fraction(Fraction.of(0.5)).to_f64() == 0.5 expect Attention.of(1.8).scaled_by(Fraction.of(0.5)).to_f64() == 0.9 expect Attention.of(0.3).max(Attention.of(1.4)).to_f64() == 1.4 expect Attention.of(1.4).max(Attention.of(0.3)).to_f64() == 1.4

name: canvas_apps/safari/Beacon.roc
html: ## Beacon is the light on top of a radio tower, as the scene draws it: a ## magenta disc 3 m in radius, seen through as far as it is dim. A beacon ## blinks by the ride's clock, each segment's a little apart from the last, and ## a tower halfway along a segment blinks opposite the one at its end. Whatever ## holds a beacon says where its middle is on screen and how many pixels a ## metre spans there. A beacon is worked out each frame from the clock and the ## tower it tops. import Clock import Distance import lib.Point import lib.Fraction import lib.Pixels import Route import Steps import lib.Brush import lib.RgbColor import lib.Shapes ## A tower's beacon at one moment of its blink, by how bright it is. Beacon :: Fraction.{ ## Where on its segment a tower stands: past the segment's end, or halfway ## along it. TowerPlace : [AtEnd, Midway] ## Which tower a beacon tops: the segment it stands on, and its place ## there. Towers aren't kept, so this pair is all that tells one from ## another. TowerKey : { segment : Route.SegmentIndex, place : Beacon.TowerPlace } ## The beacon of the tower at `key`, as it shines at `clock`. at : Beacon.TowerKey, Clock -> Beacon at = |key, clock| Beacon.(beacon_brightness(Beacon.blink_phase(key, clock))) ## The phase at `clock` of the beacon of the tower at `key`: how many steps ## into its blink it is, from 0, where it starts dark, up to a step short of ## one `beacon_period`. It is the steps since the ride's start, plus the ## beacon's head start, wrapped to one blink. blink_phase : Beacon.TowerKey, Clock -> Steps blink_phase = |key, clock| into_blink(clock.steps_since(Clock.start).plus(head_start(key))) ## A beacon blinks once in this many steps of the ride. beacon_period : Steps beacon_period = Steps.of(120) ## How bright the beacon is. brightness : Beacon -> Fraction brightness = |Beacon.(fraction)| fraction ## The beacon's disc, centred on `center` where a metre across spans ## `metre_on_screen`, unless it is too dim or too small to draw. disc : Beacon, { center : Point, metre_on_screen : Pixels, } -> Try(Shapes.Shape, [TooDim, TooSmall]) disc = |Beacon.(fraction), { center, metre_on_screen }| if fraction < dimmest_beacon { Err(TooDim) } else { radius = metre_on_screen.times(beacon_radius.to_metres()) if radius < smallest_beacon_radius { Err(TooSmall) } else { Ok(beacon_disc({ center, radius_on_screen: radius, brightness: fraction })) } } } ## How far into its blink the beacon of the tower at `place` on the segment at ## `segment` is when the ride starts. Each segment's beacon starts a stagger ## further into its blink than the last one's, so neighbouring segments' ## beacons blink apart, and the tower halfway along starts half a blink on ## from the one at the end, so the two blink opposite each other. head_start : Beacon.TowerKey -> Steps head_start = |{ segment, place }| { at_end = into_blink(beacon_stagger.times(segment.to_u32())) match place { AtEnd => at_end Midway => into_blink(at_end.plus(half_period)) } } ## `steps` brought inside one blink: so many steps into a blink, from 0 up to a ## step short of one `beacon_period`. into_blink : Steps -> Steps into_blink = |steps| steps.wrapped_to(Beacon.beacon_period) ## Each segment's beacon starts this many steps further into its blink than the ## last one's. The number shares no factor with the period, so the first ## period's worth of segments' beacons all start at different points of the ## blink. beacon_stagger : Steps beacon_stagger = Steps.of(37) half_period : Steps half_period = Steps.of(Beacon.beacon_period.to_u32() // 2) ## How bright a beacon is `phase` steps into its blink. beacon_brightness : Steps -> Fraction beacon_brightness = |phase| { angle = 2.0 * F64.pi * phase.to_f64() / Beacon.beacon_period.to_f64() Fraction.of((1.0 - angle.cos()) / 2.0) } beacon_radius : Distance beacon_radius = Distance.metres(3.0) beacon_color : RgbColor beacon_color = RgbColor.of(0xFF2FE6) ## The dimmest beacon that is drawn. A dimmer one would tint the sky by less ## than one part in fifty, too little to see; the figure was chosen by eye. dimmest_beacon : Fraction dimmest_beacon = Fraction.of(0.02) ## The smallest beacon radius that is drawn. A disc under a pixel across ## covers no pixel whole, so a far beacon is left out rather than drawn as a ## speck. smallest_beacon_radius : Pixels smallest_beacon_radius = Pixels.of(0.5) ## A beacon's disc, seen through as far as `brightness` says. beacon_disc : { center : Point, radius_on_screen : Pixels, brightness : Fraction, } -> Shapes.Shape beacon_disc = |{ center, radius_on_screen, brightness }| { opaque = Brush.opaque_rgba(beacon_color) Disc({ center, radius: radius_on_screen, fill: Flat({ ..opaque, a: brightness.to_f64() }), }) } ## How far into its blink the beacon past the end of the segment numbered `n` ## is when the ride starts. segment_head_start : U32 -> F64 segment_head_start = |n| { segment = Route.SegmentIndex.number(n) head_start({ segment, place: AtEnd }).to_f64() } ## How far into its blink the beacon halfway along the segment numbered `n` is ## when the ride starts. midway_head_start : U32 -> F64 midway_head_start = |n| { segment = Route.SegmentIndex.number(n) head_start({ segment, place: Midway }).to_f64() } expect segment_head_start(0) == 0.0 expect segment_head_start(1) == 37.0 expect segment_head_start(2) == 74.0 expect segment_head_start(3) == 111.0 expect segment_head_start(4) == 28.0 expect segment_head_start(5) == 65.0 expect segment_head_start(10) == 10.0 expect segment_head_start(60) == 60.0 expect segment_head_start(120) == 0.0 # The midway beacon starts half a blink further on than the one at the end, # wrapped to the blink, and half a blink on from that is back where the one at # the end started. expect [ (midway_head_start(0), 60.0), (midway_head_start(1), 97.0), (midway_head_start(2), 14.0), (midway_head_start(3), 51.0), (midway_head_start(60), 0.0), ].all(|(got, want)| got == want) expect [0, 1, 2, 3, 59, 60, 119].all( |n| { midway = head_start({ segment: Route.SegmentIndex.number(n), place: Midway }) back_again = midway.plus(half_period).wrapped_to(Beacon.beacon_period) back_again.to_f64() == segment_head_start(n) }, ) expect [ (beacon_brightness(Steps.of(0)).to_f64(), 0.0), (beacon_brightness(Steps.of(60)).to_f64(), 1.0), (beacon_brightness(Steps.of(30)).to_f64(), 0.5), (beacon_brightness(Steps.of(90)).to_f64(), 0.5), ].all(|(got, want)| (got - want).abs() <= 0.0000001) ## How bright the first segment's beacon at `place` is at `step` of the ride. first_brightness_at : Beacon.TowerPlace, U32 -> F64 first_brightness_at = |place, step| { beacon = Beacon.at({ segment: Route.SegmentIndex.first, place }, Clock.at_step(step)) beacon.brightness().to_f64() } # A beacon blinks: dark at the start of its blink, full halfway, half a quarter # of the way either side, and dark again a whole blink on. The midway beacon # is full where the one at the end is dark, and dark where it is full. expect [ (first_brightness_at(AtEnd, 0), 0.0), (first_brightness_at(AtEnd, 30), 0.5), (first_brightness_at(AtEnd, 60), 1.0), (first_brightness_at(AtEnd, 90), 0.5), (first_brightness_at(AtEnd, 120), 0.0), (first_brightness_at(Midway, 0), 1.0), (first_brightness_at(Midway, 30), 0.5), (first_brightness_at(Midway, 60), 0.0), (first_brightness_at(Midway, 120), 1.0), ].all(|(got, want)| (got - want).abs() <= 0.0000001) # The phase counts from the tower's own head start: the second segment's beacon # at the end starts 37 steps in, its midway beacon half a blink further, and # each comes back to 0 at a whole blink. expect [ (Route.SegmentIndex.number(1), AtEnd, 0, 37.0), (Route.SegmentIndex.number(1), AtEnd, 83, 0.0), (Route.SegmentIndex.number(1), Midway, 0, 97.0), (Route.SegmentIndex.number(1), Midway, 23, 0.0), (Route.SegmentIndex.first, AtEnd, 5400, 0.0), (Route.SegmentIndex.first, AtEnd, 5519, 119.0), ].all( |(segment, place, step, want)| { Beacon.blink_phase({ segment, place }, Clock.at_step(step)).to_f64() == want }, ) ## The disc of a beacon at `brightness`, centred at (10, 20) where a metre ## spans `metre` pixels. disc_of : F64, F64 -> Try(Shapes.Shape, [TooDim, TooSmall]) disc_of = |brightness, metre| Beacon.(Fraction.of(brightness)).disc({ center: Point.at(10.0, 20.0), metre_on_screen: Pixels.of(metre), }) # A lit beacon's disc is 3 m in radius, magenta, and seen through as # far as it is dim. expect disc_of(0.25, 10.0) == Ok( Disc({ center: Point.at(10.0, 20.0), radius: Pixels.of(30.0), fill: Flat(Brush.with_alpha(beacon_color, 0.25)), }), ) # A beacon dimmer than one part in fifty is not drawn, and one just bright # enough is. expect disc_of(0.0, 10.0) == Err(TooDim) expect disc_of(0.019, 10.0) == Err(TooDim) expect disc_of(0.02, 10.0).is_ok() # A beacon under a pixel across is not drawn, and one just over is. expect disc_of(1.0, 0.16) == Err(TooSmall) expect disc_of(1.0, 0.17).is_ok() # Too dim is told before too small. expect disc_of(0.0, 0.16) == Err(TooDim) # The first segment's beacon, at the start of the ride, is too dark to draw. expect Beacon.at({ segment: Route.SegmentIndex.first, place: AtEnd }, Clock.start).disc({ center: Point.at(10.0, 20.0), metre_on_screen: Pixels.of(10.0), }) == Err(TooDim)

name: canvas_apps/safari/BendAnimal.roc
html: ## At a bend in the road, a safari animal stands on the outside of the bend, ## beyond the guard rail, and its baby stands straight on past the bend, dead ## ahead of a rider coming up to it, off the road the rider turns onto. Both ## face the way the road turns. import Across import Along import Billboard import Distance import EmojiStill import Geom ## The safari animals that stand at a bend. BendAnimal := [Elephant, Giraffe, Zebra, Rhino].{ ## The animal and its baby at `bend`, the bend that ends a segment. bend_billboards : BendAnimal, Geom.Bend -> List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) bend_billboards = |animal, bend| { species = BendAnimal.species_of(animal) bend_along = Along.at(bend.segment_length) { out_on_outside, facing } = match Geom.outer_side(bend.turn) { LeftSide => { out_on_outside: Across.left_of_middle, facing: FacesRight } RightSide => { out_on_outside: Across.right_of_middle, facing: FacesLeft } } adult = Billboard.adult_billboard(species, facing) clear_of_rail = Geom.road_half_width.plus(adult_rail_buffer) across = out_on_outside(clear_of_rail.plus(adult.half_width())) [ { road_point: { along: bend_along, across }, lift: Distance.zero, kind: adult, }, { road_point: { along: bend_along.plus(baby_beyond), across: Across.middle }, lift: Distance.zero, kind: Billboard.young_billboard(species, facing), }, ] } ## The species of a bend's animal. species_of : BendAnimal -> Billboard.Species species_of = |animal| match animal { Elephant => { emoji: EmojiStill.elephant, adult_height: Distance.metres(2.8) } Giraffe => { emoji: EmojiStill.giraffe, adult_height: Distance.metres(4.5) } Zebra => { emoji: EmojiStill.zebra, adult_height: Distance.metres(1.6) } Rhino => { emoji: EmojiStill.rhino, adult_height: Distance.metres(2.2) } } } ## How far beyond the guard rail the grown animal stands. adult_rail_buffer : Distance adult_rail_buffer = Distance.metres(1.5) ## How far the baby stands past the bend, straight on along the segment that ## ends there, in the middle of where its road would run. baby_beyond : Distance baby_beyond = Distance.metres(14.0)

name: canvas_apps/safari/Billboard.roc
html: ## A billboard is an animal that stands in one place and always faces the ## camera: an emoji's still, at a height, facing left or right. import Distance import EmojiStill import Sprite import StillShapes Billboard :: { emoji : EmojiStill, height : Distance, facing : Billboard.Facing, }.{ ## Which way a billboard faces on screen. Facing : [FacesLeft, FacesRight] ## A kind of animal: its emoji, and how tall a grown one stands. Species : { emoji : EmojiStill, adult_height : Distance } ## A grown animal of `species`. adult_billboard : Billboard.Species, Billboard.Facing -> Billboard adult_billboard = |species, facing| Billboard.({ emoji: species.emoji, height: species.adult_height, facing }) ## A young animal of `species`, which stands half as tall as a grown one. young_billboard : Billboard.Species, Billboard.Facing -> Billboard young_billboard = |species, facing| Billboard.( { emoji: species.emoji, height: species.adult_height.divided_by(2.0), facing, }, ) ## Which way the billboard faces. facing : Billboard -> Billboard.Facing facing = |Billboard.(billboard)| billboard.facing scenery_height : Billboard -> Distance scenery_height = |Billboard.(billboard)| billboard.height ## How far a billboard reaches to each side of its middle. An emoji's still ## is square, so this is half its height. half_width : Billboard -> Distance half_width = |Billboard.(billboard)| billboard.height.divided_by(2.0) ## How a billboard looks. An emoji faces left, so a billboard facing right ## is its still mirrored. scenery_sprite : Billboard, Sprite.Setting -> Sprite scenery_sprite = |Billboard.(billboard), setting| { flip = match billboard.facing { FacesLeft => AsDrawn FacesRight => Mirrored } Sprite.from_shapes( StillShapes.standing_still_shapes( setting, { height: billboard.height, still: billboard.emoji.still(), flip }, ), ) } is_eq : _ }

name: canvas_apps/safari/BirdFlight.roc
html: ## A Roc bird's flight: the trees it flies between, and where it is and how it ## looks along the way. A bird sits on its perch, a tree on the left that its ## segment chooses, until its flight starts, then flies diagonally ahead, across ## the road, to the first tree on the far side far enough along, and perches ## there. Its flight ## plays a frame a step at its own pace, and the ride plans its start so that it ## lands as the rider comes within `landing_gap` of the tree it left. import Across import Along import Animation import EncounterPlan import Distance import Easing import lib.Fraction import Steps import Trees ## A bird's flight is the tree it leaves, and the one it flies to. BirdFlight := { from : Trees.RoadsideTree, to : Trees.RoadsideTree }.{ ## Where the wings are in a beat. WingBeat : [WingsUp, WingsDown] ## How the bird looks: sitting; side on as it takes off; seen from behind ## as it flies off; and dropping onto its tree. BirdPose : [ Perched, Side(BirdFlight.WingBeat), Away(BirdFlight.WingBeat), Diving, ] ## Every pose a bird takes, in the order of a flight, each wing beat up ## before down. all_poses : List(BirdFlight.BirdPose) all_poses = [ Perched, Side(WingsUp), Side(WingsDown), Away(WingsUp), Away(WingsDown), Diving, ] ## A bird at one instant: how it looks, and where it is. BirdInstant : Animation.Instant(BirdFlight.BirdPose) ## What the ride plans a flight by: its length, and the gap from the rider ## to the tree it left at which it has landed. flight_span : EncounterPlan.StepSpan flight_span = { length: Steps.of_count(flight_frames.len()), ends_at: landing_gap } ## The flight of a bird perched on the tree at `perch`, among a segment's ## `trees`: to the first tree on the other side of the road far enough along. flight_from : List(Trees.RoadsideTree), Trees.RoadsideTree -> Try(BirdFlight, [NoTreeToFlyTo]) flight_from = |trees, perch| { is_far_enough = |tree| tree.road_point.along >= perch.road_point.along.plus(shortest_hop) is_landing_tree = |tree| is_far_side(tree) and is_far_enough(tree) to = trees.find_first(is_landing_tree) ? |NotFound| NoTreeToFlyTo Ok(BirdFlight.({ from: perch, to })) } ## Where along its segment the ride plans `flight` by: the tree the bird ## leaves. planned_along : BirdFlight -> Along planned_along = |flight| flight.from.road_point.along ## The bird at `stage` of its flight. bird_instant_at : BirdFlight, Animation.Stage -> BirdFlight.BirdInstant bird_instant_at = |flight, stage| flight_timeline(flight).instant(stage) } ## How far short of the tree it left the rider is when the bird lands, so ## that the rider sees the landing before passing the tree. landing_gap : Distance landing_gap = Distance.metres(15.0) ## How far above a straight line the top of its path is, chosen by eye. flight_arc : Distance flight_arc = Distance.metres(5.0) ## The bird flies to a tree at least this far along from the one it left, ## so that its path runs ahead of the rider as well as across the road. The ## length is chosen by eye. shortest_hop : Distance shortest_hop = Distance.metres(25.0) ## How many steps each half of a flap of the wings takes, up or down. frames_a_half_flap : U64 frames_a_half_flap = 2 ## Whether `tree` stands on the far side of the road from where a bird starts: ## on the right, with a positive `across`. A bird starts on the left, because ## its stills are never mirrored and an unmirrored still's beak points toward ## +x, so from the left the bird faces the road, and it flies across to the ## right. is_far_side : Trees.RoadsideTree -> Bool is_far_side = |tree| tree.road_point.across > Across.middle ## The bird as it sits on top of `tree`. sitting_on : Trees.RoadsideTree -> BirdFlight.BirdInstant sitting_on = |tree| { pose: Perched, location: tree_top(tree) } ## How the bird looks through a flight, a frame a step: a flap side on as it ## takes off, seven flaps seen from behind, and a flap's length of diving. The ## seven is chosen by eye. flight_poses : List(BirdFlight.BirdPose) flight_poses = [ flap_poses({ up: Side(WingsUp), down: Side(WingsDown) }), List.repeat(flap_poses({ up: Away(WingsUp), down: Away(WingsDown) }), 7).join(), List.repeat(Diving, 2 * frames_a_half_flap), ].join() ## One frame of any flight before it is put between two trees: how the bird ## looks, and how far through the flight it is. FlightFrame : { pose : BirdFlight.BirdPose, through : Fraction } ## The frames of any flight, one a step: `flight_poses`, each as far through ## the flight as its place in the list, from the start at the first to the end ## at the last. Both the flight's length and its timeline come from this one ## list, so the two can't disagree. flight_frames : List(FlightFrame) flight_frames = { last_frame = (flight_poses.len() - 1).to_f64() flight_poses.map_with_index( |pose, frame| { pose, through: Fraction.of(frame.to_f64() / last_frame) }, ) } ## The whole of a flight: `flight_frames`, on one smooth path that rises in ## the middle, from the tip of the tree it leaves to the tip of the one it ## lands on. flight_timeline : BirdFlight -> Animation.Timeline(FlightFrame, BirdFlight.BirdPose) flight_timeline = |{ from, to }| { ends = { from: tree_top(from), to: tree_top(to) } Animation.Timeline.of({ before: sitting_on(from), frames: flight_frames, frame_instant: |{ pose, through }| { pose, location: flight_location({ from: ends.from, to: ends.to, through }), }, after: sitting_on(to), }) } ## The location on top of `tree`. tree_top : Trees.RoadsideTree -> Animation.Location tree_top = |tree| { road_point: tree.road_point, lift: tree.kind.scenery_height() } ## One flap of the wings: `up` for its first half and `down` for its second. flap_poses : { up : BirdFlight.BirdPose, down : BirdFlight.BirdPose } -> List(BirdFlight.BirdPose) flap_poses = |{ up, down }| { half_up = List.repeat(up, frames_a_half_flap) half_up.concat(List.repeat(down, frames_a_half_flap)) } ## Each bird pose's place in `BirdFlight.all_poses`. The match names every ## pose and wing beat, so a new one doesn't compile until it has a place, and ## the expect below fails until the list holds it there. pose_place : BirdFlight.BirdPose -> U64 pose_place = |pose| match pose { Perched => 0 Side(WingsUp) => 1 Side(WingsDown) => 2 Away(WingsUp) => 3 Away(WingsDown) => 4 Diving => 5 } expect BirdFlight.all_poses.map(pose_place) == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] ## The location `through` a flight between `from` and `to`, easing out and in along ## a straight line, and raised by an arc over it. flight_location : { from : Animation.Location, to : Animation.Location, through : Fraction, } -> Animation.Location flight_location = |{ from, to, through }| { on_line = Animation.location_between({ from, to, fraction: Easing.smoothstep(through) }) share = through.to_f64() # 4t(1 - t) is 0 at both ends and 1 halfway, so the arc tops out at `flight_arc`. above_line = flight_arc.times(4.0 * share * (1.0 - share)) { ..on_line, lift: on_line.lift.plus(above_line) } }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Camera.roc
html: ## The rider's camera: a pinhole at eye height, looking straight ahead. It ## puts a point in the rider's view onto the screen, and a polygon there once ## it is cut at the camera's near plane. import Distance import Lens import lib.Brush import lib.Point import lib.Pixels import lib.RgbColor import lib.Shapes import RiderView Camera :: [].{ ## The camera's height above the ground. eye_height : Distance eye_height = Distance.metres(1.2) ## Where a point in front of the camera lands on the screen, through a ## lens of `focal_length`. project : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead, Pixels -> Point project = |p, focal_length| { slope_right = p.right().ratio_to(p.forward()) slope_up = p.height().minus(eye_height).ratio_to(p.forward()) { x: Lens.x_for_slope({ slope: slope_right, focal_length }), y: Lens.y_for_slope({ slope: slope_up, focal_length }), } } ## How tall something of `height` stands on the screen, `forward` of the ## camera, through a lens of `focal_length`. height_on_screen : { height : Distance, forward : Distance }, Pixels -> Pixels height_on_screen = |{ height, forward }, focal_length| Lens.height_for_slope({ slope: height.ratio_to(forward), focal_length }) ## An upright object on the screen: where its foot is, and how far up the ## screen its top is from there. A tree, a still and a billboard all stand ## this way. Upright : { foot : Point, height_on_screen : Pixels } ## The object standing at `base`, `height` tall, on the screen. upright_on_screen : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead, { height : Distance, focal_length : Pixels, } -> Camera.Upright upright_on_screen = |base, { height, focal_length }| { foot = project(base, focal_length) top = project(base.at_height(base.height().plus(height)), focal_length) { foot, height_on_screen: foot.y.minus(top.y) } } ## Each of `points` put on the screen, in order, through a lens of focal ## length `focal_length`. projected_points : List(RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead), Pixels -> List(Point) projected_points = |points, focal_length| points.map(|p| project(p, focal_length)) ## A polygon of one color, in the rider's view. FlatPolygon : { color : RgbColor, corners : List(RiderView.PointAtHeight) } ## A polygon on screen, cut at the near plane, unless it's wholly behind the ## camera. What is left of a polygon of three corners or more has three or ## more, so fewer is a bug in the code that asked, and it crashes. The cut ## can add a corner or take some away, so a quad can come out a triangle, a ## quad or a polygon of five, and the corners left decide which. clipped_polygon : Camera.FlatPolygon, Pixels -> Try(Shapes.Shape, [BehindCamera]) clipped_polygon = |{ color, corners }, focal_length| { in_front = RiderView.clipped_points(corners) if in_front.is_empty() { Err(BehindCamera) } else if in_front.len() < 3 { crash "Camera.clipped_polygon: a polygon needs at least three corners" } else { Ok( Shapes.region_from_corners( projected_points(in_front, focal_length), Brush.flat(color), ), ) } } } ## `point` past the near plane, which every point in these tests is. ahead : RiderView.PointAtHeight -> RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead ahead = |point| RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(point) ?? crash "a test's point is past the near plane" screen_point : RiderView.PointAtHeight -> Point screen_point = |point| Camera.project(ahead(point), Pixels.of(800.0)) expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(1.2), }).x.to_f64() == 480.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(10.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(1.2), }).x.to_f64() == 1280.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(-5.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(1.2), }).x.to_f64() == 80.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(10.0), forward: Distance.metres(5.0), height: Distance.metres(1.2), }).x.to_f64() == 2080.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(1.2), }).y.to_f64() == 300.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(11.2), }).y.to_f64() == -500.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(6.2), }).y.to_f64() == -100.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(0.2), }).y.to_f64() == 380.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(4.0), height: Distance.metres(3.2), }).y.to_f64() == -100.0 # The same point twice as far off is half as far from the screen's middle. expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(4.0), forward: Distance.metres(4.0), height: Distance.metres(1.2), }).x.to_f64() == 1280.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(4.0), forward: Distance.metres(8.0), height: Distance.metres(1.2), }).x.to_f64() == 880.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(4.0), forward: Distance.metres(16.0), height: Distance.metres(1.2), }).x.to_f64() == 680.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(4.0), height: Distance.metres(5.2), }).y.to_f64() == -500.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(8.0), height: Distance.metres(5.2), }).y.to_f64() == -100.0 expect screen_point({ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(16.0), height: Distance.metres(5.2), }).y.to_f64() == 100.0 expect [ (1.0, 4.0, 800.0, 200.0), (1.0, 8.0, 800.0, 100.0), (2.0, 8.0, 800.0, 200.0), (1.0, 4.0, 400.0, 100.0), ].all( |(height, forward, focal_length, on_screen)| Camera.height_on_screen( { height: Distance.metres(height), forward: Distance.metres(forward) }, Pixels.of(focal_length), ) == Pixels.of(on_screen), ) expect Camera.projected_points( [ { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(1.2), }, { right: Distance.metres(10.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(1.2), }, { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(11.2), }, ].map(ahead), Pixels.of(800.0), ) == [ Point.at(480.0, 300.0), Point.at(1280.0, 300.0), Point.at(480.0, -500.0), ] expect Camera.projected_points([], Pixels.of(800.0)).len() == 0

name: canvas_apps/safari/CatCrossing.roc
html: ## A cat that crosses the road ahead of the rider, by a roadside tree on the ## right of the road. Wherever that tree stands, the cat waits behind it and ## just past it, then walks out into the road, freezes with its head over the ## middle, and leaps clear to the far verge, a frame a step at its own pace. The ## ride plans its start so that it is across as the rider comes within ## `clear_gap` of it. import Across import Along import Animation import Attention import Distance import EncounterPlan import lib.Fraction import Geom import Steps CatCrossing :: { tree : Geom.RoadPoint }.{ ## How the cat holds itself: walking, it is at rest or mid-stride; then ## frozen; then its leap, from the coil through flight and landing to the ## collapse after. CatPose : [Rest, Stride, Frozen, Coil, Flight, Land, Collapse] ## Every pose a cat takes, in the order of a crossing. all_poses : List(CatCrossing.CatPose) all_poses = [Rest, Stride, Frozen, Coil, Flight, Land, Collapse] ## A cat at one instant: how it looks, and where it is. CatInstant : Animation.Instant(CatCrossing.CatPose) ## How tall a cat stands. cat_height : Distance cat_height = Distance.metres(1.7) ## Where the tree the cat crosses by stands. tree : CatCrossing -> Geom.RoadPoint tree = |CatCrossing.(crossing)| crossing.tree ## How far along its segment the cat crosses: just past its tree. along : CatCrossing -> Along along = |crossing| crossing.tree().along.plus(cat_beyond_tree) ## Where across the road the cat starts, behind its tree. start_across : CatCrossing -> Across start_across = |crossing| crossing.tree().across.plus(cat_behind_tree) ## Where across the road every cat ends: on the far verge, its hips on the ## grass. end_across : Across end_across = Across.left_of_middle(Geom.road_half_width.plus(grass_toehold)) .minus(collapsed_hip_reach) ## Where every cat freezes across the road: with its head over the middle. mid_across : Across mid_across = Across.right_of_middle(frozen_head_reach) ## The crossing of a cat by `tree`, on the right of the road. by_tree : { tree : Geom.RoadPoint } -> CatCrossing by_tree = |{ tree: tree_point }| CatCrossing.({ tree: tree_point }) ## What the ride plans a crossing by: its length, and the gap it ends at. crossing_span : EncounterPlan.StepSpan crossing_span = { length: Steps.of_count(crossing_frames.len()), ends_at: clear_gap } ## Where along its segment the ride plans `crossing` by: where the cat ## crosses. planned_along : CatCrossing -> Along planned_along = |crossing| crossing.along() ## How eye-catching a crossing cat is: how hard it holds the rider's eye at ## its strongest. peak_attention : Attention peak_attention = Attention.of(1.8) ## The cat at `stage` of its crossing. cat_instant_at : CatCrossing, Animation.Stage -> CatCrossing.CatInstant cat_instant_at = |crossing, stage| crossing_timeline(crossing).instant(stage) } ## How far ahead of its feet the frozen cat's head is. Its still's head runs ## from 0.02 to 0.49 of its height ahead of them, so this is the head's centre. frozen_head_reach : Distance frozen_head_reach = CatCrossing.cat_height.times(0.25) ## How far behind its feet the collapsed cat's hips lie: about 0.7 of its ## height in its still, with the hind feet themselves nearer 0.6. collapsed_hip_reach : Distance collapsed_hip_reach = CatCrossing.cat_height.times(0.7) ## How far behind its tree, away from the road, the cat starts. cat_behind_tree : Distance cat_behind_tree = Distance.metres(1.5) ## How far past its tree, along the road, the cat crosses. cat_beyond_tree : Distance cat_beyond_tree = Distance.metres(2.0) ## How far onto the far verge's grass the collapsed cat's hips lie. grass_toehold : Distance grass_toehold = Distance.metres(0.3) ## How far short of the cat the rider is when its crossing ends. clear_gap : Distance clear_gap = Distance.metres(3.0) ## How the cat looks walking out: two strides, a frame each step. walking_poses : List(CatCrossing.CatPose) walking_poses = [ Stride, Stride, Stride, Rest, Rest, Stride, Stride, Stride, Rest, Rest, ] ## How many frames the cat stands frozen. frozen_frames : U64 frozen_frames = 24 ## The leap, frame by frame: how the cat looks, how much of the way from the ## middle of the road to the far verge it has come, and how high its feet are. ## These are keyframes set by eye, not measured off the stills, and each shows ## for one step. leap_frames : List(CrossingFrame) leap_frames = [ { pose: Coil, way: Leaping({ way_to_verge: Fraction.zero, lift: Distance.zero }) }, { pose: Flight, way: Leaping({ way_to_verge: Fraction.of(0.4), lift: Distance.metres(0.27) }) }, { pose: Flight, way: Leaping({ way_to_verge: Fraction.of(0.85), lift: Distance.metres(0.17) }), }, { pose: Land, way: Leaping({ way_to_verge: Fraction.whole, lift: Distance.zero }) }, ] ## Where a cat is on its way across in one frame: walking out, this much of ## the way to the middle of the road; standing frozen there; or leaping, this ## much of the way on to the far verge and this high. CrossingWay : [ WalkingOut(Fraction), StandingFrozen, Leaping({ way_to_verge : Fraction, lift : Distance }), ] ## One frame of any crossing before it is put on a road: how the cat looks, and ## where it is on its way across. CrossingFrame : { pose : CatCrossing.CatPose, way : CrossingWay } ## The frames of any crossing, one a step. Both the crossing's length and its ## timeline come from this one list, so the two can't disagree. crossing_frames : List(CrossingFrame) crossing_frames = { walking = walking_poses.map_with_index( |pose, frame| { pose, way: WalkingOut(Fraction.of(frame.to_f64() / walking_poses.len().to_f64())), }, ) frozen = List.repeat({ pose: Frozen, way: StandingFrozen }, frozen_frames) [walking, frozen, leap_frames].join() } ## The whole of a crossing, a frame a step: the cat walks out to the middle ## of the road, freezes there, and leaps clear to the far verge. crossing_timeline : CatCrossing -> Animation.Timeline(CrossingFrame, CatCrossing.CatPose) crossing_timeline = |crossing| { on_road = |across| { road_point: { along: crossing.along(), across }, lift: Distance.zero } start = on_road(crossing.start_across()) middle = on_road(CatCrossing.mid_across) end = on_road(CatCrossing.end_across) location_of = |way| match way { WalkingOut(fraction) => Animation.location_between({ from: start, to: middle, fraction }) StandingFrozen => middle Leaping({ way_to_verge, lift }) => { on_the_way = Animation.location_between({ from: middle, to: end, fraction: way_to_verge, }) { ..on_the_way, lift } } } Animation.Timeline.of({ before: { pose: Rest, location: start }, frames: crossing_frames, frame_instant: |{ pose, way }| { pose, location: location_of(way) }, after: { pose: Collapse, location: end }, }) } the_cat : CatCrossing the_cat = CatCrossing.by_tree({ tree: { along: Along.metres(100.0), across: Across.metres(3.0) } }) ## The same cat by a tree farther from the road. the_cat_by_a_far_tree : CatCrossing the_cat_by_a_far_tree = CatCrossing.by_tree({ tree: { along: Along.metres(100.0), across: Across.metres(8.0) }, }) ## Each cat pose's place in `CatCrossing.all_poses`. The match names every ## pose, so a new one doesn't compile until it has a place, and the expect below ## fails until the list holds it there. pose_place : CatCrossing.CatPose -> U64 pose_place = |pose| match pose { Rest => 0 Stride => 1 Frozen => 2 Coil => 3 Flight => 4 Land => 5 Collapse => 6 } expect CatCrossing.all_poses.map(pose_place) == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] expect the_cat.along().to_metres() == 102.0 expect the_cat.start_across().to_metres() == 4.5 expect the_cat_by_a_far_tree.start_across().to_metres() == 9.5 expect [ (CatCrossing.end_across.to_metres(), -3.49), (CatCrossing.mid_across.distance_from(CatCrossing.end_across).to_metres(), 3.915), ].all(|(got, want)| (got - want).abs() <= 0.000000000001)

name: canvas_apps/safari/Clock.roc
html: ## The ride's clock: which step of the ride this is. It starts at zero and ## moves on by one with every step, so it is always whole. It is one of the ## four things each step carries to the next. import Steps Clock :: U32.{ ## The clock as a ride starts. start : Clock start = Clock.(0) ## The clock at step `number` of a ride. at_step : U32 -> Clock at_step = |number| Clock.(number) ## The clock one step on. next : Clock -> Clock next = |Clock.(n)| Clock.(n + 1) ## How many steps this clock is past `earlier`. It crashes when this clock ## comes before `earlier`. steps_since : Clock, Clock -> Steps steps_since = |Clock.(n), Clock.(earlier)| if n < earlier { crash "Clock.steps_since: this clock comes before the one it counts from" } else { Steps.of(n - earlier) } ## The clock `length` steps on. plus : Clock, Steps -> Clock plus = |Clock.(n), length| Clock.(n + length.to_u32()) ## The clock `length` steps back.
