It crashes when that would go back past ## step 0, where the ride starts. minus : Clock, Steps -> Clock minus = |Clock.(n), length| { back = length.to_u32() if back > n { crash "Clock.minus: the ride starts at step 0, and nothing comes before it" } else { Clock.(n - back) } } is_lt : Clock, Clock -> Bool is_lt = |Clock.(n), Clock.(other)| n < other to_str : Clock -> Str to_str = |Clock.(n)| n.to_str() is_eq : _ } expect Clock.at_step(9).steps_since(Clock.at_step(9)) == Steps.zero expect Clock.at_step(9).steps_since(Clock.at_step(8)) == Steps.one_step expect Clock.at_step(9).steps_since(Clock.start) == Steps.of(9) expect Clock.start.next().steps_since(Clock.start) == Steps.one_step expect Clock.start.plus(Steps.zero) == Clock.start expect Clock.at_step(9).plus(Steps.of(3)) == Clock.at_step(12) expect Clock.at_step(9).minus(Steps.zero) == Clock.at_step(9) expect Clock.at_step(9).minus(Steps.of(3)) == Clock.at_step(6) expect Clock.at_step(9).minus(Steps.of(9)) == Clock.start expect Clock.at_step(8) < Clock.at_step(9) expect !(Clock.at_step(9) < Clock.at_step(9)) expect !(Clock.at_step(10) < Clock.at_step(9))

name: canvas_apps/safari/Coast.roc
html: ## Coast rehearses the rider's next few seconds: it runs the bike's real physics ## with no change of lean or speed, and says where the rider would end up. import Across import Motorcycle import Distance import Geom import Steps Coast :: [].{ ## Where a coast ends up: still on the road at this place across it, or off ## a shoulder after this many steps, counting the step that leaves. Outcome : [EndsAt(Across), Leaves({ side : [Left, Right], after : Steps })] ## How far ahead the rehearsal needs to look: 25 m along the road. A coast ## that runs this far without leaving the road ends there. clear_distance : Distance clear_distance = Distance.metres(25.0) ## Where a coast from `motorcycle` ends up. coast_outcome : Motorcycle -> Coast.Outcome coast_outcome = |motorcycle| coast_end(motorcycle).outcome ## The motorcycle at each step of a coast from `motorcycle`, the last one the ## step that ends it. path_motorcycles : Motorcycle -> List(Motorcycle) path_motorcycles = |motorcycle| { var $motorcycle = motorcycle var $path = [] for _ in 0..<coast_end(motorcycle).steps_run.to_u32() { $motorcycle = coasting_step($motorcycle) $path = $path.append($motorcycle) } $path } } ## Where a coast ends up, and how many steps it runs to get there. CoastEnd : { outcome : Coast.Outcome, steps_run : Steps } ## The coast from `motorcycle`, run a step at a time until it crosses a bound, ## gets `clear_distance` along the road, or runs `longest_coast` steps. coast_end : Motorcycle -> CoastEnd coast_end = |motorcycle| { start = motorcycle.route_place.road_point bounds = coast_bounds(start.across) var $point = start var $steps_run = Steps.zero var $motorcycle = motorcycle while $steps_run < longest_coast and is_coasting({ bounds, start, point: $point }) { $motorcycle = coasting_step($motorcycle) $steps_run = $steps_run.plus(Steps.one_step) $point = $motorcycle.route_place.road_point } outcome = if $point.across < bounds.left { Leaves({ side: Left, after: $steps_run }) } else if $point.across > bounds.right { Leaves({ side: Right, after: $steps_run }) } else { EndsAt($point.across) } { outcome, steps_run: $steps_run } } ## How far across the road a coast may go before it counts as leaving. CoastBounds : { left : Across, right : Across } ## The bounds of a coast that starts at `start_across`: the road's edges, inset ## by `shoulder_margin`, or `start_across` where that is further out. coast_bounds : Across -> CoastBounds coast_bounds = |start_across| { inset_half_width = Geom.road_half_width.minus(shoulder_margin) { left: Across.left_of_middle(inset_half_width).min(start_across), right: Across.right_of_middle(inset_half_width).max(start_across), } } ## Whether a coast from `start` that has reached `point` goes on: it is within ## `bounds`, and short of `clear_distance` along the road. is_coasting : { bounds : CoastBounds, start : Geom.RoadPoint, point : Geom.RoadPoint, } -> Bool is_coasting = |{ bounds, start, point }| point.across >= bounds.left and point.across <= bounds.right and point.along.distance_from(start.along) < Coast.clear_distance ## The motorcycle one step on, holding its lean and speed. coasting_step : Motorcycle -> Motorcycle coasting_step = |motorcycle| motorcycle.motorcycle_at_next_step(motorcycle.steady_controls()) ## How far inside each shoulder the rehearsal puts the road's edge: 5 cm. ## A coast that crosses this inset edge counts as leaving the road, so the ## line the search keeps never grazes the shoulder itself. shoulder_margin : Distance shoulder_margin = Distance.metres(0.05) ## A slow rider who leans can circle on the road and never get clear of where ## they started, so a coast ends after this many steps. longest_coast : Steps longest_coast = Steps.of(2000)

name: canvas_apps/safari/Conifer.roc
html: ## Conifer is a kind of tree. It sets the tree's height, from the ground to its ## tip, and its color, and TreeShapes draws it. import Distance import Sprite import TreeShapes import lib.RgbColor Conifer := [Green, SmallGreen, Red, Gold].{ ## A red tree is twice a small one's height and a gold one three times, ## sizes chosen by eye. scenery_height : Conifer -> Distance scenery_height = |conifer| match conifer { Green => green_height SmallGreen => small_height Red => small_height.times(2.0) Gold => small_height.times(3.0) } ## How a conifer looks. scenery_sprite : Conifer, Sprite.Setting -> Sprite scenery_sprite = |conifer, setting| TreeShapes.tree_sprite( setting, { height: conifer.scenery_height(), foliage_color: foliage_color(conifer) }, ) is_eq : _ } ## A small green tree's height, chosen by eye. small_height : Distance small_height = Distance.metres(4.896) ## A green tree's height, 1.3 times a small one's, a size chosen by eye. green_height : Distance green_height = small_height.times(1.3) green_color : RgbColor green_color = RgbColor.of(0x1C5A22) gold_color : RgbColor gold_color = RgbColor.of(0xCF9A18) red_color : RgbColor red_color = RgbColor.of(0xB23A2A) ## A conifer's foliage color. foliage_color : Conifer -> RgbColor foliage_color = |conifer| match conifer { Green | SmallGreen => green_color Gold => gold_color Red => red_color }

name: canvas_apps/safari/CowHerd.roc
html: ## A herd of cows grazes on the left of the road, in columns that run back ## from it, each cow a little out of line. A bull may stand in front of the ## herd, by the trees. import Across import Along import Billboard import Distance import EmojiStill import Geom import Scatter import Trees CowHerd :: { cow_count : U64, rows_behind_front : U64 }.{ ## Whether a bull leads the herd. Bull : [WithBull, NoBull] ## A herd of `cow_count` cows. `rows_behind_front` is how many rows stand ## behind the front row, nearest the road. Each column has one cow in each ## row, so a column holds one more cow than this. herd : { cow_count : U64, rows_behind_front : U64 } -> CowHerd herd = |shape| CowHerd.(shape) ## The herd's cows behind `herd_along`, column by column from the front, ## led by the bull at `herd_along` if the herd has one. herd_cows : CowHerd, { herd_along : Along, bull : CowHerd.Bull } -> List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) herd_cows = |CowHerd.({ cow_count, rows_behind_front }), { herd_along, bull }| { cows = List.from_iter(U64.until(0, cow_count)) .map(|cow_number| herd_cow({ herd_along, cow_number, rows_behind_front })) match bull { WithBull => [herd_bull(herd_along)].concat(cows) NoBull => cows } } is_eq : _ } cow : Billboard.Species cow = { emoji: EmojiStill.cow, adult_height: Distance.metres(1.4) } bull : Billboard.Species bull = { emoji: EmojiStill.bull, adult_height: cow.adult_height.times(1.15) } ## The gap between the bull's side and the trees. bull_tree_gap : Distance bull_tree_gap = Distance.metres(0.5) ## The bull at `herd_along`, by the trees. herd_bull : Along -> Geom.Placed(Billboard) herd_bull = |herd_along| { bull_billboard = Billboard.adult_billboard(bull, FacesLeft) bull_middle = Trees.near_tree_line.plus(bull_billboard.half_width()) { road_point: { along: herd_along, across: Across.left_of_middle(bull_middle.plus(bull_tree_gap)), }, lift: Distance.zero, kind: bull_billboard, } } ## How far from the middle of the road the herd's front row stands, 10 metres ## off the road's edge. Each herd sets its own. front_row_distance : Distance front_row_distance = Geom.road_half_width.plus(Distance.metres(10.0)) ## How far along the road behind the bull's place the first column's place is, ## chosen by eye. gap_behind_bull : Distance gap_behind_bull = Distance.metres(4.0) ## The distance between the herd's columns, along the road, chosen by eye. column_spacing : Distance column_spacing = Distance.metres(6.0) ## How far along the road each row back is moved from the one in front, chosen ## by eye. A column's place is where its front row stands. row_stagger : Distance row_stagger = Distance.metres(2.0) ## The distance between the herd's rows, away from the road, chosen by eye. row_depth : Distance row_depth = Distance.metres(5.0) ## How far a cow strays from its place along the road, chosen by eye. jitter_along : Distance jitter_along = Distance.metres(1.5) ## How far a cow strays from its place across the road, chosen by eye. jitter_across : Distance jitter_across = Distance.metres(1.2) ## Every fourth cow, starting with cow 1, is a calf. is_calf : U64 -> Bool is_calf = |cow_number| cow_number.rem_by(4) == 1 ## The herd's cow at `cow_number`, counting from 0. The scatter's phases, 2.7 ## along the road and 1.9 across it, are chosen by eye. herd_cow : { herd_along : Along, cow_number : U64, rows_behind_front : U64, } -> Geom.Placed(Billboard) herd_cow = |{ herd_along, cow_number, rows_behind_front }| { cows_per_column = rows_behind_front + 1 column = cow_number.div_trunc_by(cows_per_column).to_f64() row = cow_number.rem_by(cows_per_column).to_f64() herd_front = herd_along.plus(gap_behind_bull) column_place = herd_front.plus(column_spacing.times(column)) in_line = column_place.plus(row_stagger.times(row)) row_place = front_row_distance.plus(row_depth.times(row)) stray = Scatter.stray_of( cow_number, { along_phase: 2.7, across_phase: 1.9, jitter_along, jitter_across, }, ) out_from_road = row_place.plus(stray.across) { road_point: { along: in_line.plus(stray.along), across: Across.left_of_middle(out_from_road), }, lift: Distance.zero, kind: cow_billboard(cow_number), } } ## The billboard for the herd's cow at `cow_number`: young for a calf, grown ## for the rest. cow_billboard : U64 -> Billboard cow_billboard = |cow_number| if is_calf(cow_number) { Billboard.young_billboard(cow, FacesRight) } else { Billboard.adult_billboard(cow, FacesRight) } expect { bull_height = herd_bull(Along.metres(24.0)).kind.scenery_height() (bull_height.to_metres() - 1.61).abs() <= 0.000000000001 } expect [ (0, False), (1, True), (2, False), (4, False), (5, True), (13, True), ].all(|(cow_number, want)| is_calf(cow_number) == want) ## A herd of five cows in columns of two, its last column one cow short. five_cows : CowHerd five_cows = CowHerd.herd({ cow_count: 5, rows_behind_front: 1 }) cows_with_bull : List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) cows_with_bull = five_cows.herd_cows({ herd_along: Along.metres(24.0), bull: WithBull }) cows_without_bull : List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) cows_without_bull = five_cows.herd_cows({ herd_along: Along.metres(24.0), bull: NoBull }) expect cows_with_bull.len() == 6 expect cows_without_bull.len() == 5 # The bull leads, facing left, and the cows follow him in their own order, facing # right. expect cows_with_bull.take_first(1).map(|leader| leader.road_point.along) == [Along.metres(24.0)] expect cows_with_bull.take_first(1).map(|leader| leader.kind) == [Billboard.adult_billboard(bull, FacesLeft)] expect cows_with_bull.drop_first(1) == cows_without_bull expect cows_with_bull.take_first(2).map(|critter| critter.kind.facing()) == [FacesLeft, FacesRight] expect cows_without_bull.all(|member| member.kind.facing() == FacesRight) expect { calf_or_cow = [ Billboard.young_billboard(cow, FacesRight), Billboard.adult_billboard(cow, FacesRight), ] cows_without_bull.all(|member| calf_or_cow.contains(member.kind)) } # Column by column from the front, each cow strays from its place by no more # than the jitter: along the road and across it. expect { places = [ (28.0, -12.0), (30.0, -17.0), (34.0, -12.0), (36.0, -17.0), (40.0, -12.0), ] misses = cows_without_bull.map2( places, |one, (along, across)| ( (one.road_point.along.to_metres() - along).abs(), (one.road_point.across.to_metres() - across).abs(), ), ) within_jitter = misses.all(|(along_miss, across_miss)| along_miss <= 1.5 and across_miss <= 1.2) misses.len() == 5 and within_jitter }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Distance.roc
html: ## A length in metres: how long a segment is, how tall a tree stands, how far ## the rider is from a cat. A length measured toward something can run past it, ## so a gap goes negative once the rider is beyond what it is measured to. import lib.Fraction Distance :: F64.{ metres : F64 -> Distance metres = |metres| Distance.(metres) to_metres : Distance -> F64 to_metres = |Distance.(d)| d ## No length at all. zero : Distance zero = Distance.(0.0) plus : Distance, Distance -> Distance plus = |Distance.(d), Distance.(other)| Distance.(d + other) minus : Distance, Distance -> Distance minus = |Distance.(d), Distance.(other)| Distance.(d - other) times : Distance, F64 -> Distance times = |Distance.(d), factor| Distance.(d * factor) ## This fraction of this length. scaled_by : Distance, Fraction -> Distance scaled_by = |Distance.(d), fraction| Distance.(d * fraction.to_f64()) divided_by : Distance, F64 -> Distance divided_by = |Distance.(d), divisor| Distance.(d / divisor) ## This length measured the other way. opposite : Distance -> Distance opposite = |Distance.(d)| Distance.(0.0 - d) ## How many of `whole` this is, which can pass 1. ratio_to : Distance, Distance -> F64 ratio_to = |Distance.(d), Distance.(whole)| d / whole ## The smaller of this length and `other`. min : Distance, Distance -> Distance min = |Distance.(d), Distance.(other)| Distance.(d.min(other)) ## The larger of this length and `other`. max : Distance, Distance -> Distance max = |Distance.(d), Distance.(other)| Distance.(d.max(other)) is_gt : Distance, Distance -> Bool is_gt = |Distance.(d), Distance.(other)| d > other is_gte : Distance, Distance -> Bool is_gte = |Distance.(d), Distance.(other)| d >= other is_lt : Distance, Distance -> Bool is_lt = |Distance.(d), Distance.(other)| d < other is_lte : Distance, Distance -> Bool is_lte = |Distance.(d), Distance.(other)| d <= other is_eq : _ } ## Just under, at and just over 2.5 m, and how `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` and `==` ## answer against 2.5 m there. expect [ (2.0, [True, True, False, False, False]), (2.5, [False, True, False, True, True]), (3.0, [False, False, True, True, False]), ].all( |(metres, want)| { length = Distance.metres(metres) held = Distance.metres(2.5) [ length < held, length <= held, length > held, length >= held, length == held, ] == want }, )

name: canvas_apps/safari/EarthCurve.roc
html: ## EarthCurve is the earth's curve under the rider: how far the ground drops below ## level as it goes away from the rider, and the horizon where the ground curves ## out of sight, which hides what stands low enough beyond it. import Camera import Distance import lib.Fraction import RiderView EarthCurve :: [].{ ## How far the ground has curved away below level at `point`, which is ## never negative. ground_drop : RiderView.RiderPoint -> Distance ground_drop = |point| { r = point.right.to_metres() f = point.forward.to_metres() Distance.metres((r * r + f * f) / (2.0 * ground_curve_radius.to_metres())) } ## The lowest height at `point`, measured from the rider's level, that the ## rider's eye can see. Within the horizon it is the ground itself. Past it, ## the ground has curved out of sight, and the lowest line of sight is the ## one from the eye that grazes the ground at the horizon. ## ## The ground `s` metres out lies s²/2R below level, for the ground's radius ## R. A line falling k metres per metre from the eye, at height h, touches ## it where h - k s = -s²/2R has one root: k = √(2h/R), at s = √(2hR), which ## is the horizon's distance H. So k is 2h/H, and `d` metres out the ## grazing line stands at h - 2h d/H. At the horizon that is -h, the ## ground's own height there, so the two halves meet. lowest_visible_height : RiderView.RiderPoint -> Distance lowest_visible_height = |point| { reach = distance_from_rider(point).to_metres() horizon = horizon_distance.to_metres() if reach <= horizon { EarthCurve.ground_drop(point).opposite() } else { eye = Camera.eye_height.to_metres() Distance.metres(eye - 2.0 * eye * reach / horizon) } } ## Whether something standing at `point` past the horizon, its top `top` ## above the rider's level, is hidden wholly behind the curve of the ground. ## Within the horizon nothing is: the ground there is all in view. is_below_horizon : { point : RiderView.RiderPoint, top : Distance } -> Bool is_below_horizon = |{ point, top }| { is_past_horizon = distance_from_rider(point) > horizon_distance is_past_horizon and top <= EarthCurve.lowest_visible_height(point) } ## The outline through `points`, each lowered by the earth's curve, cut at ## the horizon. It is empty when all of it lies past the horizon. points_before_horizon : List(RiderView.RiderPoint) -> List(RiderView.PointAtHeight) points_before_horizon = |points| RiderView.points_in_region(points.map(ground_point), region_within(horizon_distance)) } ## The radius the ground curves away over. From the rider's eye it puts ## the horizon 490 metres out. ground_curve_radius : Distance ground_curve_radius = Distance.metres(100000.0) ## How far `point` is from the rider, along the ground. distance_from_rider : RiderView.RiderPoint -> Distance distance_from_rider = |point| RiderView.ground_distance({ from: { right: Distance.zero, forward: Distance.zero }, to: point }) ## How far from the rider the ground curves out of sight. A lowered point ## further out lands lower on screen again, so ground past here would show ## as slivers on the grass. horizon_distance : Distance horizon_distance = { radius = ground_curve_radius.to_metres() Distance.metres((2.0 * radius * Camera.eye_height.to_metres()).sqrt()) } ## A point on the ground, lowered by the earth's curve. ground_point : RiderView.RiderPoint -> RiderView.PointAtHeight ground_point = |point| { right: point.right, forward: point.forward, height: EarthCurve.ground_drop(point).opposite(), } ## The part of the rider's view within `reach` of the rider, measured on the ## ground: a circle round the rider. region_within : Distance -> RiderView.Region(RiderView.PointAtHeight) region_within = |reach| { corner_in_region: |point| if is_within(point, reach) { Ok(point) } else { Err(Outside) }, edge_crossings: |{ from, to }| { point_at = |fraction| RiderView.point_between({ from, to, fraction }) circle_crossings({ from, to, reach }).map(point_at) }, } ## Whether `point` is within `reach` of the rider, measured on the ground. is_within : RiderView.PointAtHeight, Distance -> Bool is_within = |point, reach| { r = point.right.to_metres() f = point.forward.to_metres() r * r + f * f <= reach.to_metres() * reach.to_metres() } ## How far along the edge from `from` to `to` it crosses the circle at `reach` ## round the rider, as fractions of the edge strictly between its ends, ## nearest `from` first. ## ## The point a share t of the way along is `from` plus t steps, and it is on ## the circle where its squared distance equals the squared reach, a quadratic ## in t. circle_crossings : { from : RiderView.PointAtHeight, to : RiderView.PointAtHeight, reach : Distance, } -> List(Fraction) circle_crossings = |{ from, to, reach }| { start_right = from.right.to_metres() start_forward = from.forward.to_metres() step_right = to.right.to_metres() - start_right step_forward = to.forward.to_metres() - start_forward step_squared = step_right * step_right + step_forward * step_forward outward = start_right * step_right + start_forward * step_forward reach_squared = reach.to_metres() * reach.to_metres() start_past_reach = start_right * start_right + start_forward * start_forward - reach_squared discriminant = outward * outward - step_squared * start_past_reach if step_squared == 0.0 or discriminant <= 0.0 { [] } else { root = discriminant.sqrt() entering = (0.0 - outward - root) / step_squared leaving = (0.0 - outward + root) / step_squared [entering, leaving].keep_if(|share| share > 0.0 and share < 1.0).map(Fraction.of) } } expect EarthCurve.ground_drop({ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(0.0), }).to_metres() == 0.0 expect EarthCurve.ground_drop({ right: Distance.metres(3.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), }).to_metres() == 0.000545 expect EarthCurve.ground_drop({ right: Distance.metres(-5.0), forward: Distance.metres(40.0), }).to_metres() == 0.008125 expect EarthCurve.ground_drop({ right: Distance.metres(12.5), forward: Distance.metres(100.0), }).to_metres() == 0.05078125 ## A point `forward` metres straight ahead of the rider. straight_ahead : F64 -> RiderView.RiderPoint straight_ahead = |forward| { right: Distance.zero, forward: Distance.metres(forward) } # The horizon is 490 m out. Within it the lowest height in view is the # ground's: 400 m out it has dropped 0.8 m. At the horizon the grazing line # meets the ground, 1.2 m down, the eye's height below level. 1000 m out the # grazing line stands 3.699 m below level. expect [ (400.0, -0.8), (horizon_distance.to_metres(), -1.2), (1000.0, -3.698979485566356), ].all( |(forward, lowest)| (EarthCurve.lowest_visible_height(straight_ahead(forward)).to_metres() - lowest).abs() <= 0.000000001, ) # 1000 m out, a top 3.6 m below level shows over the horizon, and one 3.8 m below # is hidden. Within the horizon nothing is hidden, even a top down on the ground. expect !EarthCurve.is_below_horizon({ point: straight_ahead(1000.0), top: Distance.metres(-3.6) }) expect EarthCurve.is_below_horizon({ point: straight_ahead(1000.0), top: Distance.metres(-3.8) }) expect !EarthCurve.is_below_horizon({ point: straight_ahead(400.0), top: Distance.metres(-0.8) }) ## A point on the level of the rider, `right` and `forward` in metres. level_at : F64, F64 -> RiderView.PointAtHeight level_at = |right, forward| { right: Distance.metres(right), forward: Distance.metres(forward), height: Distance.zero, } ## Whether a point is within a nanometre of `right` and `forward`, in metres. is_level_near : RiderView.PointAtHeight, (F64, F64) -> Bool is_level_near = |point, (right, forward)| { right_miss = (point.right.to_metres() - right).abs() forward_miss = (point.forward.to_metres() - forward).abs() right_miss <= 0.000000001 and forward_miss <= 0.000000001 } ## Whether each point is near its want. are_near : List(RiderView.PointAtHeight), List((F64, F64)) -> Bool are_near = |got_points, wants| { is_each_near = got_points.map2(wants, is_level_near).all(|is_close| is_close) got_points.len() == wants.len() and is_each_near } ## The polygon cut to what lies within 10 m of the rider. points_within_ten_metres : List(RiderView.PointAtHeight) -> List(RiderView.PointAtHeight) points_within_ten_metres = |polygon_points| { reach = region_within(Distance.metres(10.0)) RiderView.points_in_region(polygon_points, reach) } # A square that reaches past 10 m of the rider keeps two corners, then where its # right side leaves the circle, then where its left side comes back in. expect { square = [ level_at(-6.0, 0.0), level_at(6.0, 0.0), level_at(6.0, 12.0), level_at(-6.0, 12.0), ] are_near( points_within_ten_metres(square), [ (-6.0, 0.0), (6.0, 0.0), (6.0, 8.0), (-6.0, 8.0), ], ) } # An edge with both ends past reach that passes through the circle adds where # it enters and where it leaves. expect { triangle = [ level_at(-20.0, 6.0), level_at(20.0, 6.0), level_at(0.0, 30.0), ] are_near(points_within_ten_metres(triangle), [(-8.0, 6.0), (8.0, 6.0)]) } # A polygon wholly past reach leaves nothing. expect { far_triangle = [ level_at(20.0, 20.0), level_at(30.0, 20.0), level_at(30.0, 30.0), ] points_within_ten_metres(far_triangle).is_empty() } # A point on the ground keeps its right and forward, and sits the drop below level. expect ground_point({ right: Distance.metres(3.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0) }) == { right: Distance.metres(3.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(-0.000545), }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Encounter.roc
html: ## An encounter is what the rider meets on one segment of the road: a cat ## crossing, a bird's flight, or nothing, a quiet road. A segment has one, so ## that the rider has one experience at a time, and most of the road is quiet, ## so that an encounter stands out. import Along import Animation import BirdFlight import CatCrossing import Clock import EncounterPlan Encounter := [CatCrosses(CatCrossing), BirdHere(BirdFlight), QuietRoad].{ ## What the ride plans `encounter` by: its animation's span, and where along ## its segment its animal is, or none on a quiet road. encounter_span : Encounter -> Try( { span : EncounterPlan.StepSpan, planned_along : Along }, [QuietRoad], ) encounter_span = |encounter| match encounter { CatCrosses(crossing) => Ok({ span: CatCrossing.crossing_span, planned_along: crossing.planned_along() }) BirdHere(flight) => Ok({ span: BirdFlight.flight_span, planned_along: flight.planned_along() }) QuietRoad => Err(QuietRoad) } ## Where `encounter`'s animation, started by `plan`, has got to with the ## ride's clock at `now`, as long as its span lasts. A quiet road has nothing ## to wait for, so it stays `Waiting`. encounter_stage : Encounter, { plan : EncounterPlan, now : Clock } -> Animation.Stage encounter_stage = |encounter, { plan, now }| match encounter.encounter_span() { Ok({ span, .. }) => plan.stage_at({ now, length: span.length }) Err(QuietRoad) => Waiting } }

name: canvas_apps/safari/EncounterPlan.roc
html: ## The ride's plan for the encounter on the rider's segment: when its animation ## starts, and so where it has got to. An encounter's animation runs on its own ## clock, a frame a step from the step it starts at, and never looks at the ## rider. The ride picks that step once, when the rider first comes within ## reach, from how the rider is coming then, so that the animation ends as the ## rider arrives. The plan and the ride's clock say where the animation has ## got to as an `Animation.Stage`, which the animal's timeline turns into what ## it shows. The plan is kept from one step to the next, one of the four things ## the ride remembers. import Animation import Clock import Distance import Speed import Steps ## When the encounter on the rider's segment starts: not planned yet, or at a ## step of the ride's clock. The ride keeps one, and forgets it at each new ## segment, since only the encounter on the rider's own segment is ever live. EncounterPlan := [Unplanned, StartsAt(Clock)].{ is_eq : _ ## How many steps an animation plays for, a frame a step, and the gap from ## the rider to the animal it ends at. StepSpan : { length : Steps, ends_at : Distance } ## How far from the animal an animation is planned for a rider at `speed`: ## the gap it ends at, and the road the rider covers while it plays. A ## faster rider has it planned farther off. planning_gap : EncounterPlan.StepSpan, Speed -> Distance planning_gap = |span, speed| span.ends_at.plus(speed.distance_in(span.length)) ## How the rider comes at the encounter on their segment: `gap` short of ## its animal at `speed`, for an animation `span` long, or none on a quiet ## road. Approach : [ Approaching( { span : EncounterPlan.StepSpan, gap : Distance, speed : Speed, }, ), QuietRoad, ] ## The plan a step after `plan`, for a rider who has just come onto a new ## segment or stayed on the same one, coming at its encounter by ## `approach` with the ride's clock at `now`. A new segment forgets the ## plan. A plan once made is kept, and an unplanned encounter is planned by ## `plan_for`. plan_at_next_step : EncounterPlan, { segment_change : [SameSegment, NewSegment], approach : EncounterPlan.Approach, now : Clock, } -> EncounterPlan plan_at_next_step = |plan, { segment_change, approach, now }| { kept_plan = match segment_change { SameSegment => plan NewSegment => Unplanned } match kept_plan { StartsAt(_) => kept_plan Unplanned => match approach { Approaching({ span, gap, speed }) => plan_for(span, { gap, speed, now }) QuietRoad => Unplanned } } } ## Where an animation `span` long has got to, for a rider `gap` short of its ## animal, coming at a steady `speed` from `gap_at_start` at step 0 of the ## ride's clock. It is planned by `plan_for`, on the first step that such a ## rider comes within reach. The ride's rider is not steady, so on the ride ## the same animation may start on another step. steady_approach_stage : EncounterPlan.StepSpan, { gap_at_start : Distance, speed : Speed, gap : Distance, } -> Animation.Stage steady_approach_stage = |span, { gap_at_start, speed, gap }| { now = Clock.start.plus(speed.steps_to_cover(gap_at_start.minus(gap))) var $step = Clock.start var $plan = Unplanned while $plan == Unplanned and !(now < $step) { $plan = plan_for( span, { gap: gap_at_start.minus(speed.distance_in($step.steps_since(Clock.start))), speed, now: $step, }, ) $step = $step.next() } $plan.stage_at({ now, length: span.length }) } ## Where an animation `length` steps long, started by `plan`, has got to with ## the ride's clock at `now`. An unplanned animation is still waiting. stage_at : EncounterPlan, { now : Clock, length : Steps } -> Animation.Stage stage_at = |plan, { now, length }| match plan { Unplanned => Waiting StartsAt(first_step) => { end = first_step.plus(length) if now < first_step { Waiting } else if now < end { Playing(now.steps_since(first_step)) } else { Past(now.steps_since(end)) } } } } ## The start of an animation that is to end as the rider comes within ## `ends_at`, planned at `now` from how the rider comes then: `gap` from the ## animal, at `speed`. It starts now on the first step that a rider keeping ## their speed would arrive within its length, so a faster rider has it ## start farther off. Till then, and while the rider is at rest, it isn't ## planned. The plan looks at the rider's speed that once: after it, the ## animal doesn't care what the rider does. ## ## Planning on the step itself keeps the guess short, an animation's length ## ahead. A plan from farther off would take the speed to be steady for ## longer, and a rider speeding up meanwhile would arrive before the end. plan_for : EncounterPlan.StepSpan, { gap : Distance, speed : Speed, now : Clock, } -> EncounterPlan plan_for = |span, { gap, speed, now }| if speed == Speed.at_rest { Unplanned } else if gap <= EncounterPlan.planning_gap(span, speed) { StartsAt(now) } else { Unplanned } ## A span of 10 steps that ends 3 m short of the animal. ten_step_span : EncounterPlan.StepSpan ten_step_span = { length: Steps.of(10), ends_at: Distance.metres(3.0) } ## The start a rider `metres_off` the animal, going `metres_a_step`, plans at ## step 100. planned_at : { metres_off : F64, metres_a_step : F64 } -> EncounterPlan planned_at = |{ metres_off, metres_a_step }| plan_for( ten_step_span, { gap: Distance.metres(metres_off), speed: Speed.metres_a_step(metres_a_step), now: Clock.at_step(100), }, ) # At 1 m a step the rider is 10 steps from the end 13 m off: the animation # starts there and nearer, and not farther off. At 2 m a step that is 23 m off. expect planned_at({ metres_off: 13.0, metres_a_step: 1.0 }) == StartsAt(Clock.at_step(100)) expect planned_at({ metres_off: 13.1, metres_a_step: 1.0 }) == Unplanned expect planned_at({ metres_off: 8.0, metres_a_step: 1.0 }) == StartsAt(Clock.at_step(100)) expect planned_at({ metres_off: 23.0, metres_a_step: 2.0 }) == StartsAt(Clock.at_step(100)) expect planned_at({ metres_off: 23.1, metres_a_step: 2.0 }) == Unplanned # A rider at rest plans nothing, however near. expect planned_at({ metres_off: 2.0, metres_a_step: 0.0 }) == Unplanned # At 2.5 m a step the plan is made 3 + 2.5 × 10 = 28 m off. expect EncounterPlan.planning_gap(ten_step_span, Speed.metres_a_step(2.5)) == Distance.metres(28.0) expect planned_at({ metres_off: 28.0, metres_a_step: 2.5 }) == StartsAt(Clock.at_step(100)) ## A rider 8 m off the animal at 1 m a step, whom `plan_for` plans for at ## step 100. near_approach : EncounterPlan.Approach near_approach = Approaching({ span: ten_step_span, gap: Distance.metres(8.0), speed: Speed.metres_a_step(1.0), }) ## The plan a step after `plan`, at step 100, for a rider on the same segment ## with `approach`. plan_on_same_segment : EncounterPlan, EncounterPlan.Approach -> EncounterPlan plan_on_same_segment = |plan, approach| EncounterPlan.plan_at_next_step( plan, { segment_change: SameSegment, approach, now: Clock.at_step(100), }, ) ## The plan a step after `plan`, at step 100, for a rider just come onto a new ## segment with `approach`. plan_on_new_segment : EncounterPlan, EncounterPlan.Approach -> EncounterPlan plan_on_new_segment = |plan, approach| EncounterPlan.plan_at_next_step( plan, { segment_change: NewSegment, approach, now: Clock.at_step(100), }, ) ## A plan made at step 40. made_plan : EncounterPlan made_plan = StartsAt(Clock.at_step(40)) # A plan once made is kept on its segment, and forgotten at a new one, where # the new encounter is planned afresh. expect plan_on_same_segment(made_plan, near_approach) == made_plan expect plan_on_same_segment(made_plan, QuietRoad) == made_plan expect plan_on_new_segment(made_plan, near_approach) == StartsAt(Clock.at_step(100)) expect plan_on_new_segment(made_plan, QuietRoad) == Unplanned expect plan_on_same_segment(Unplanned, near_approach) == StartsAt(Clock.at_step(100)) expect plan_on_same_segment(Unplanned, QuietRoad) == Unplanned ## The stage at step `now` of a 10-step animation that `plan` starts. ten_step_stage : EncounterPlan, U32 -> Animation.Stage ten_step_stage = |plan, now| plan.stage_at({ now: Clock.at_step(now), length: Steps.of(10) }) ## The stage at step `now` of a 10-step animation starting at step 50. stage_now : U32 -> Animation.Stage stage_now = |now| ten_step_stage(StartsAt(Clock.at_step(50)), now) expect stage_now(49) == Waiting expect stage_now(50) == Playing(Steps.zero) expect stage_now(59) == Playing(Steps.of(9)) expect stage_now(60) == Past(Steps.zero) expect stage_now(65) == Past(Steps.of(5)) # An unplanned animation waits at every step, before, through and after where a # plan would have played it. expect [0, 50, 59, 60, 65].all(|now| ten_step_stage(Unplanned, now) == Waiting)

name: canvas_apps/safari/EncounterPoses.roc
html: ## EncounterPoses says where each animal on the road in view stands, and how it ## is posed, at one instant of the ride. It reads only the ride's planned ## encounter, never a camera: the encounter on the rider's own segment is where ## its animation has got to, one on a segment ahead hasn't begun, and one on the ## segment behind ended before the rider left it, so it has no pose. A segment ## holds one encounter at most, a cat's or a bird's. The poses are worked out ## each frame from the encounter plan and the clock, on the road ahead of the ## rider. import Animation import Geom import Bird import Cat import RoadAhead import SegmentFromRider EncounterPoses :: [].{ ## An animal on a segment in view: where that segment lies from the rider, ## and where on it the animal stands and how it is posed. PlacedAnimal(kind) : { from_rider : SegmentFromRider, animal : Geom.Placed(kind) } ## The cats on `road`, with the encounter on the rider's segment at ## `encounter_stage`, in the order of `RoadAhead.segments_in_view`. cat_poses : RoadAhead.RoadView, Animation.Stage -> List(EncounterPoses.PlacedAnimal(Cat)) cat_poses = |road, encounter_stage| RoadAhead.segments_in_view(road).keep_oks( |in_view| segment_cat({ in_view, encounter_stage }), ) ## The birds on `road`, with the encounter on the rider's segment at ## `encounter_stage`, in the order of `RoadAhead.segments_in_view`. bird_poses : RoadAhead.RoadView, Animation.Stage -> List(EncounterPoses.PlacedAnimal(Bird)) bird_poses = |road, encounter_stage| RoadAhead.segments_in_view(road).keep_oks( |in_view| segment_bird({ in_view, encounter_stage }), ) } ## The cat on a segment in view, if it has one that isn't over. segment_cat : { in_view : RoadAhead.SegmentInView, encounter_stage : Animation.Stage, } -> Try(EncounterPoses.PlacedAnimal(Cat), [NoPose]) segment_cat = |{ in_view, encounter_stage }| match in_view.segment.encounter { CatCrosses(crossing) => posed_in_view( in_view.from_rider, { rider_stage: encounter_stage, animal_instant_at: |stage| crossing.cat_instant_at(stage), }, ) BirdHere(_) | QuietRoad => Err(NoPose) } ## The bird on a segment in view, if it has one that isn't over. segment_bird : { in_view : RoadAhead.SegmentInView, encounter_stage : Animation.Stage, } -> Try(EncounterPoses.PlacedAnimal(Bird), [NoPose]) segment_bird = |{ in_view, encounter_stage }| match in_view.segment.encounter { BirdHere(flight) => posed_in_view( in_view.from_rider, { rider_stage: encounter_stage, animal_instant_at: |stage| flight.bird_instant_at(stage), }, ) CatCrosses(_) | QuietRoad => Err(NoPose) } ## The animal on the segment in view at `from_rider`, shown by ## `animal_instant_at`, with the encounter on the rider's own segment at ## `rider_stage`: one ahead hasn't begun, and one behind is over, so it has no ## pose. posed_in_view : SegmentFromRider, { rider_stage : Animation.Stage, animal_instant_at : Animation.Stage -> Animation.Instant(pose), } -> Try(EncounterPoses.PlacedAnimal({ pose : pose }), [NoPose]) posed_in_view = |from_rider, { rider_stage, animal_instant_at }| { posed = |stage| Ok({ from_rider, animal: Animation.placed_instant(animal_instant_at(stage)) }) match from_rider { Ahead(position) => if position == SegmentFromRider.Position.first { posed(rider_stage) } else { posed(Waiting) } JustBehind => Err(NoPose) } }

name: canvas_apps/safari/EncounterReaction.roc
html: ## What a segment's encounter does to the rider. The rider reacts only to the ## encounter on their own segment, and this is the one place that knows which ## encounters ask anything of them. A cat in the road stops the rider opening ## the throttle, without braking, and draws their eye. A bird asks nothing. The ## pigs' gaze is no encounter, and is Gaze's. import Acceleration import Animation import Attention import CatCrossing import Easing import Encounter import lib.Fraction import Steps import ThrottleLimit EncounterReaction :: [].{ ## What `encounter`, at `stage`, asks of the throttle of a rider on its ## segment: while a cat crosses, the rider eases off, holding the ## acceleration at none, which stops them speeding up and never brakes. encounter_throttle : Encounter, Animation.Stage -> ThrottleLimit encounter_throttle = |encounter, stage| match encounter { CatCrosses(_) => match stage { Playing(_) => AtMost(Acceleration.steady) Waiting | Past(_) => NoLimit } BirdHere(_) | QuietRoad => NoLimit } ## How hard `encounter`, at `stage`, holds the eye of a rider on its ## segment. encounter_attention : Encounter, Animation.Stage -> Attention encounter_attention = |encounter, stage| match encounter { CatCrosses(_) => cat_attention(stage) BirdHere(_) | QuietRoad => Attention.none } } ## How hard a crossing cat holds the rider's eye at `stage`: rising to the ## cat's peak as it crosses, then fading once it is across. cat_attention : Animation.Stage -> Attention cat_attention = |stage| match stage { Waiting => Attention.none Playing(steps_in) => { progress = Fraction.of(steps_in.ratio_to(CatCrossing.crossing_span.length)) CatCrossing.peak_attention.scaled_by(Easing.smoothstep(progress)) } Past(steps_past) => { faded = Fraction.clamp(steps_past.ratio_to(attention_fade)) CatCrossing.peak_attention.scaled_by(Easing.smoothstep(faded).complement()) } } ## Over how many steps the rider's eye lets a cat go, from when the crossing ## ends: 83 steps, chosen by eye, about 80 metres past the cat at a metre a step. attention_fade : Steps attention_fade = Steps.of(83) ## How hard the cat holds the eye at `stage`. attention_at : Animation.Stage -> F64 attention_at = |stage| cat_attention(stage).to_f64() expect attention_at(Waiting) == 0.0 expect attention_at(Playing(Steps.zero)) == 0.0 expect attention_at(Playing(Steps.of(19))) == 0.9 expect attention_at(Past(Steps.zero)) == 1.8 expect attention_at(Past(Steps.of(42))) > 0.0 expect attention_at(Past(Steps.of(42))) < 1.8 expect attention_at(Past(Steps.of(83))) == 0.0 expect attention_at(Past(Steps.of(200))) == 0.0

name: canvas_apps/safari/FrameView.roc
html: ## FrameView works out what the camera shows at one instant of the ride: the ## backdrop, the ride's shapes in paint order, and the roll, from the camera it ## places for the rider. import Angle import Clock import lib.Fraction import Grass import GroundPatch import GroundSighting import Pipeline import lib.Pixels import RideInstant import RoadAhead import RiderCamera import Route import Scene import Screen import Sky import Skyline import Sun import TruckBrakeLights import TruckHeadlights import lib.Pixels import lib.Shapes ## What the camera shows at one instant of the ride, worked out from the ## instant RideInstant keeps: the backdrop, the ride's layers, and the roll the ## camera is held at. `FrameView.ride_shape_lists` puts the layers in paint ## order. It is nominal, not opaque: other modules read its fields, and the ## frame widget builds a view of some of the layers to draw them alone. FrameView := { ## The sky, the sun and the grass, which everything else is painted over. backdrop : FrameView.Backdrop, ## The mountains, darkened with the sky. mountain_shapes : List(Shapes.Shape), ## The road itself and its ponds. ground_patch_shapes : List(Shapes.Shape), ## The things on and beside the road. scene : Scene, ## The camera's roll. The camera turns one way, so the whole frame, backdrop ## and shapes, turns the other way by the same angle, about the screen's ## centre. roll : Angle.Lean, }.{ ## What the ride is drawn over: the sky, the sun and the grass. Backdrop : { ## The sky's colors, at the top of the frame and at the horizon. sky_colors : Sky.Colors, ## Where the sun stands in the sky, if it is in view. sun_sighting : Sun.Sighting, ## How dark the sky is, which dims the grass. darkness : Fraction, } ## The frame at `instant`. The camera is worked out once, for the shapes, ## the sun and the roll. frame_view_at : Route, RideInstant -> FrameView frame_view_at = |route, instant| { camera = FrameView.camera_at(route, instant) road = RoadAhead.RoadView.ahead_of(route, camera.route_place.segment_index) sighting_camera = camera.sighting_camera() darkness = Sky.darkness_at(instant.clock) { backdrop: { sky_colors: Sky.colors_at(instant.clock), sun_sighting: Sun.sun_in_view(camera.aim(route), instant.clock), darkness, }, mountain_shapes: FrameView.skyline_shapes(camera.aim(route), instant.clock), ground_patch_shapes: FrameView.ground_shapes( road, { camera: sighting_camera, darkness }, ), scene: Scene.scene_in_view( road, { camera: sighting_camera, facts: FrameView.ride_facts(route, instant) }, ), roll: camera.roll, } } ## The ride's shapes in paint order, in the lists they are made in: the ## skyline, the ground, then each thing beside the road, far to near. ride_shape_lists : FrameView -> List(List(Shapes.Shape)) ride_shape_lists = |view| [view.mountain_shapes, view.ground_patch_shapes].concat(Scene.scene_shape_lists(view.scene)) ## The camera the frame at `instant` is seen through. It is public for ## FramePartsBench, which times the camera alone. camera_at : Route, RideInstant -> RiderCamera camera_at = |route, instant| RiderCamera.of( instant.rider, { route, encounter_stage: RideInstant.encounter_stage(route, instant) }, ) ## The backdrop's shapes in paint order: the sky, the sun, then the grass, ## which covers whatever of the sun has set. backdrop_shapes : FrameView.Backdrop -> List(Shapes.Shape) backdrop_shapes = |backdrop| [ [Sky.sky_shape(backdrop.sky_colors)], Sun.sun_shapes(backdrop.sun_sighting), [Grass.grass_shape(backdrop.darkness)], ].join() ## The whole frame turned by the camera's roll. ## ## The whole frame leans, backdrop and all, so the world banks into a turn: ## everything is drawn in one space, which turns about the middle of the ## screen by the roll, the other way round. leaned_shapes : FrameView -> List(Shapes.Shape) leaned_shapes = |view| framed_shapes(view, Screen.leaned_by(view.roll)) ## `ride_shape_lists`, already in paint order, over `backdrop`, all in ## `space`. painted_shapes : { backdrop : FrameView.Backdrop, ride_shape_lists : List(List(Shapes.Shape)), space : Shapes.Space, } -> List(Shapes.Shape) painted_shapes = |painted| { backdrop = FrameView.backdrop_shapes(painted.backdrop) Shapes.lists_in_space(painted.space, [backdrop].concat(painted.ride_shape_lists)) } ## What the sightings read from `instant` on `route` beyond the road: where ## the encounter on the rider's segment has got to, where the truck is and ## which of its lights are on, and the clock. It is public for ## FramePartsBench, which times each kind beside the road alone. ride_facts : Route, RideInstant -> Scene.RideFacts ride_facts = |route, instant| { encounter_stage: RideInstant.encounter_stage(route, instant), truck: { route_position: instant.truck.route_position, lights: { headlights: TruckHeadlights.at(Sky.darkness_at(instant.clock)), brake_lights: TruckBrakeLights.at(instant.truck.pace), }, }, clock: instant.clock, } ## The skyline seen along `aim` at `clock`, darkened as far as the sky is. It ## is public for FramePartsBench, which times the skyline alone. skyline_shapes : { heading : Angle.Bearing, focal_length : Pixels }, Clock -> List(Shapes.Shape) skyline_shapes = |aim, clock| { sky_darkness = Sky.darkness_at(clock) Skyline.skyline_shapes(aim, { darkness: sky_darkness }) } ## The road's ground that `camera` sees of `road`, under a sky `darkness` ## dark: the road itself and its ponds. It is public for FramePartsBench, ## which times the ground alone. ground_shapes : RoadAhead.RoadView, { camera : Pipeline.SightingCamera, darkness : Fraction, } -> List(Shapes.Shape) ground_shapes = |road, { camera, darkness }| { lens_and_light = { focal_length: camera.focal_length, darkness } GroundSighting.patches_in_view(road, camera.vantage).keep_oks( |patch| GroundPatch.patch_shape(patch, lens_and_light), ) } } ## The whole frame in `space`, in paint order: the backdrop, then the ## ride's shapes, which start with the mountains. framed_shapes : FrameView, Shapes.Space -> List(Shapes.Shape) framed_shapes = |view, space| FrameView.painted_shapes({ backdrop: view.backdrop, ride_shape_lists: FrameView.ride_shape_lists(view), space, })

name: canvas_apps/safari/Gawking.roc
html: ## Gawking is what a pig by the road does to the rider's speed. A rider who ## notices a pig that catches the eye slows for it, and stays slow to the end ## of the segment. The noticing and the look are the eyes', and Gaze's. import Distance import Gaze import Motorcycle import Segment import Speed import ThrottleLimit import VehicleLimits Gawking :: [].{ ## Whether the rider is gawking: whether they have noticed this segment's ## pig. is_gawking : Motorcycle, Segment -> Bool is_gawking = |motorcycle, segment| match Gaze.noticed_pig(motorcycle, segment) { Noticed(_) => True NothingNoticed => False } ## The brake for a gawking rider, who aims to be down to `gawk_speed` by ## the settle distance before the pig. The noticing lasts to the end of ## the segment, so the brake holds the rider down until the next one. gawk_brake : Motorcycle, Segment -> ThrottleLimit gawk_brake = |motorcycle, segment| match Gaze.noticed_pig(motorcycle, segment) { Noticed(pig) => { gap = pig.road_point.along.distance_from(motorcycle.route_place.road_point.along) room = gap.minus(gawk_settle_distance) AtMost( VehicleLimits.braking_to( motorcycle.speed, { target: gawk_speed, within: room.max(gawk_least_distance) }, ), ) } NothingNoticed => NoLimit } } ## The speed a gawking rider brakes down to. gawk_speed : Speed gawk_speed = Speed.metres_a_step(0.2) ## How far short of the pig a gawking rider aims to reach `gawk_speed`. gawk_settle_distance : Distance gawk_settle_distance = Distance.metres(25.0) ## The shortest distance the brake for a pig is worked out over. Past the ## settle distance the rider is still coming down to `gawk_speed`, so the ## brake keeps working at this distance's strength. Throttle's bend limit ## has a different guard, which lets go at its commit point: a rider who ## reaches a bend has no more road to brake on, and a rider who reaches ## the pig has the rest of the segment. gawk_least_distance : Distance gawk_least_distance = Distance.metres(1.0)

name: canvas_apps/safari/Gaze.roc
html: ## What the rider notices, and where the rider looks. A pig by the road catches ## the rider's eye, and once the rider is near enough to notice it the gaze ## swivels toward it. The pig passes out of sight to the side while it is still ## ahead, and the gaze turns back to the road. ## ## Two words keep the eyes and the throttle apart. A look is what the eyes do, ## and it ends once the pig is too far round. Gawking is what the speed does, ## and it lasts to the end of the segment; it is Gawking's, which reads the ## noticing from here. import Along import Angle import Billboard import Distance import Geom import Motorcycle import Segment Gaze :: [].{ ## How far short of a pig the rider notices it, measured along the road. ## The look and the gawking both start here. notice_distance : Distance notice_distance = Distance.metres(150.0) ## The pig on `segment` that catches the rider's eye: the standout pig of a herd ## the rider finds distracting. A herd the rider passes by catches no eye. eye_catching_pig : Segment -> [CatchesEye(Geom.Placed(Billboard)), NoPigCatchesEye] eye_catching_pig = |segment| match segment.segment_standout_pig() { Standout({ pig, interest: Distracting }) => CatchesEye(pig) Standout({ interest: Unnoticed, .. }) | NoPigs => NoPigCatchesEye } ## The pig the rider has noticed on this segment, if any. The noticing ## starts where an eye-catching pig is `notice_distance` ahead and asks only ## where the motorcycle is, so it lasts past the pig to the end of the ## segment. noticed_pig : Motorcycle, Segment -> [Noticed(Geom.Placed(Billboard)), NothingNoticed] noticed_pig = |motorcycle, segment| { rider_along = motorcycle.route_place.road_point.along match eye_catching_pig(segment) { CatchesEye(pig) if is_past_notice(rider_along, pig) => Noticed(pig) CatchesEye(_) | NoPigCatchesEye => NothingNoticed } } ## Where the rider wants to look: at the pig in sight, this far from the ## way the motorcycle points, or at the road. GazeTarget : [OnPig(Angle.Turn), OnRoad] ## How far from the way the motorcycle points the rider will look. A pig ## this far round, or further, is out of sight. look_release_angle : Angle.Turn look_release_angle = Angle.Turn.degrees(35.0) ## Where the rider wants to look: at a distracting pig that is near enough ## to notice and less than the release angle from the way the motorcycle ## points, or else at the road. desired_gaze : Motorcycle, Segment -> Gaze.GazeTarget desired_gaze = |motorcycle, segment| match Gaze.noticed_pig(motorcycle, segment) { Noticed(pig) => { rider_point = motorcycle.route_place.road_point turn = turn_to({ rider_point, yaw: motorcycle.yaw }, pig) if turn.abs() < look_release_angle { OnPig(turn) } else { OnRoad } } NothingNoticed => OnRoad } } ## Whether a motorcycle at `rider_along` has reached the place where `pig` is ## noticed. is_past_notice : Along, Geom.Placed(Billboard) -> Bool is_past_notice = |rider_along, pig| rider_along >= pig.road_point.along.minus(Gaze.notice_distance) ## How far `pig` stands from the way a motorcycle at `rider_point` points, its ## `yaw`. turn_to : { rider_point : Geom.RoadPoint, yaw : Angle.Turn }, Geom.Placed(Billboard) -> Angle.Turn turn_to = |{ rider_point, yaw }, pig| Angle.Turn.radians( F64.atan2({ x: pig.road_point.along.distance_from(rider_point.along).to_metres(), y: pig.road_point.across.distance_from(rider_point.across).to_metres(), }), ).minus(yaw)

name: canvas_apps/safari/Geom.roc
html: ## The geometry of the road. The road is a line of straight segments, and a point ## on it is measured within one segment: metres along it from its start, and ## metres across it from the middle of the road. This module carries a point ## round a bend into the segment before or after it. RoadAhead turns a point on ## the road into a point in the rider's view (`RiderView`). import Across import Along import Angle import Distance Geom :: [].{ ## A point on one segment of the road. RoadPoint : { along : Along, across : Across } ## An object on one segment of the road, `lift` off the ground, and what ## kind of object it is. A tree is placed once for the whole ride, a cow ## from its herd whenever something asks for it, and a cat, a tower or the ## truck anew for each frame. ## `Pipeline.sighting_of` turns it into a `Pipeline.Sighted` for a frame. Placed(kind) : { road_point : Geom.RoadPoint, lift : Distance, kind : kind, } ## Where the camera stands on the current segment, and which way it faces. Vantage : { along : Along, across : Across, yaw : Angle.Turn, } ## The bend from one segment into the next: the length of the segment ## before it, and the turn it makes, positive to the right. Bend : { segment_length : Distance, turn : Angle.Turn } ## How far the road reaches from its middle to either edge. The road is ## twice this wide. road_half_width : Distance road_half_width = Distance.metres(2.0) ## The road's left edge. left_edge : Across left_edge = Across.left_of_middle(road_half_width) ## The road's right edge. right_edge : Across right_edge = Across.right_of_middle(road_half_width) ## The side of the road on the outside of a bend, where its guard rail runs. OuterSide : [LeftSide, RightSide] ## The outside of a bend that turns `bend_turn`: the left side when the ## road turns right, the right side when it turns left. outer_side : Angle.Turn -> Geom.OuterSide outer_side = |bend_turn| if bend_turn.is_right() { LeftSide } else { RightSide } ## A point on the segment after `bend`, measured on the segment before it: ## turned by the bend, then moved to where the segment after starts. point_in_segment_before : Geom.RoadPoint, Geom.Bend -> Geom.RoadPoint point_in_segment_before = |point, bend| Geom.point_before_worked_bend(point, Geom.worked_bend(bend)) ## A point on the segment before `bend`, measured on the segment after it. ## This is `point_in_segment_before` undone. point_in_segment_after : Geom.RoadPoint, Geom.Bend -> Geom.RoadPoint point_in_segment_after = |point, bend| Geom.point_after_worked_bend(point, Geom.worked_bend(bend)) ## A bend with what carrying a point across it needs worked out once: where ## the segment after it starts, measured on the segment before, and the ## cosine and sine of its turn. The road ahead keeps its bends this way, so ## the many points of a frame don't each work them out again. WorkedBend : { start_after : Geom.RoadPoint, cos_turn : F64, sin_turn : F64, } ## `bend`, worked out. worked_bend : Geom.Bend -> Geom.WorkedBend worked_bend = |bend| { cos_turn = bend.turn.to_radians().cos() sin_turn = bend.turn.to_radians().sin() { start_after: start_after(bend, { cos_turn, sin_turn }), cos_turn, sin_turn, } } ## `point`, on the segment after a bend already worked out, measured on the ## segment before it instead: turned by the bend, and moved to where the ## segment after starts. point_before_worked_bend : Geom.RoadPoint, Geom.WorkedBend -> Geom.RoadPoint point_before_worked_bend = |point, { start_after: start, cos_turn, sin_turn }| { along = point.along.to_metres() across = point.across.to_metres() { along: start.along.plus(Distance.metres(cos_turn * along - sin_turn * across)), across: start.across.plus(Distance.metres(sin_turn * along + cos_turn * across)), } } ## What `point_in_segment_after` gives, for a bend already worked out. point_after_worked_bend : Geom.RoadPoint, Geom.WorkedBend -> Geom.RoadPoint point_after_worked_bend = |point, { start_after: start, cos_turn, sin_turn }| { past_start = point.along.distance_from(start.along).to_metres() aside = point.across.distance_from(start.across).to_metres() { along: Along.metres(cos_turn * past_start + sin_turn * aside), across: Across.metres((0.0 - sin_turn) * past_start + cos_turn * aside), } } ## How far along the segment before `bend` a rider on the middle of the road ## comes onto the next segment's road: its edge meets the middle here. commit_along : Geom.Bend -> Along commit_along = |bend| { exit_tan = bend.turn.abs().to_radians().tan() Along.at(bend.segment_length.minus(Geom.road_half_width.divided_by(exit_tan))) } } ## The middle of the road where the segment after `bend` starts, measured on ## the segment before it. The two segments share the corner on the inside of ## the bend, so this lies past the end of the segment before, and toward the ## turn. ## The cosine and sine of the bend's turn are `cos_turn` and `sin_turn`. start_after : Geom.Bend, { cos_turn : F64, sin_turn : F64 } -> Geom.RoadPoint start_after = |bend, { cos_turn, sin_turn }| { half_width = Geom.road_half_width.to_metres() toward_turn = half_width * (1.0 - cos_turn) { along: Along.metres(bend.segment_length.to_metres() + half_width * sin_turn.abs()), across: if bend.turn.is_right() { Across.metres(toward_turn) } else { Across.metres(0.0 - toward_turn) }, } } expect Geom.outer_side(Angle.Turn.degrees(50.0)) == LeftSide expect Geom.outer_side(Angle.Turn.degrees(-70.0)) == RightSide ## A bend of `degrees` out of a 300 metre segment. bend_of : F64 -> Geom.Bend bend_of = |degrees| { segment_length: Distance.metres(300.0), turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(degrees) } ## Whether two road points are within a nanometre of each other. is_near : Geom.RoadPoint, Geom.RoadPoint -> Bool is_near = |got, want| { along_miss = got.along.distance_from(want.along).to_metres().abs() across_miss = got.across.distance_from(want.across).to_metres().abs() along_miss <= 0.000000001 and across_miss <= 0.000000001 } # A point carried round a bend one way and back lands where it started, both # ways round. expect [50.0, -70.0, 15.0, -15.0].all( |degrees| { start = { along: Along.metres(12.0), across: Across.metres(1.0) } bend = bend_of(degrees) on_next = Geom.point_in_segment_after(start, bend) on_previous = Geom.point_in_segment_before(start, bend) is_near(Geom.point_in_segment_before(on_next, bend), start) and is_near(Geom.point_in_segment_after(on_previous, bend), start) }, ) # The two segments share the corner on the inside of the bend: the right edge # for a right turn, the left edge for a left turn. expect [ (50.0, Geom.right_edge), (-70.0, Geom.left_edge), (15.0, Geom.right_edge), ].all( |(degrees, inner_edge)| { end_before = { along: Along.metres(300.0), across: inner_edge } next_start = { along: Along.start, across: inner_edge } is_near(Geom.point_in_segment_before(next_start, bend_of(degrees)), end_before) }, ) # The middle of the road where the segment after starts is past the end of the # segment before and toward the turn. expect { middle_at_start = { along: Along.start, across: Across.middle } is_near( Geom.point_in_segment_before(middle_at_start, bend_of(90.0)), { along: Along.metres(302.0), across: Across.metres(2.0) }, ) } # The commit point is where the middle of the road reaches the next road's edge: # short of it a rider there is off that road, and just past it on. expect [50.0, -70.0, 15.0, -80.0].all( |degrees| { bend = bend_of(degrees) commit = Geom.commit_along(bend) from_next_middle = |along| { on_next = Geom.point_in_segment_after({ along, across: Across.middle }, bend) on_next.across.distance_from_middle().to_metres() } (from_next_middle(commit) - 2.0).abs() <= 0.000000001 and from_next_middle(commit.minus(Distance.metres(0.01))) > 2.0 and from_next_middle(commit.plus(Distance.metres(0.01))) < 2.0 }, )

name: canvas_apps/safari/Grass.roc
html: ## The grass, from just above the horizon down past the foot of the screen. ## It is one colour, dimmed as the sky darkens, and nothing else in the ride ## draws grass: the grass is whatever the rest of the frame doesn't paint over. import lib.Fraction import lib.Pixels import Screen import Sky import lib.Brush import lib.RgbColor import lib.Shapes Grass :: [].{ ## The grass's colour by day, which the rolling land in front of the ## mountains takes too. grass_color : RgbColor grass_color = RgbColor.of(0x4A8F43) ## The grass's colour under a sky `darkness` dark. grass_color_at : Fraction -> RgbColor grass_color_at = |darkness| Sky.color_at_darkness(Grass.grass_color, darkness) ## The grass starts a pixel above the horizon, so no seam shows between ## the two under the roll. grass_top_y : Pixels grass_top_y = Screen.horizon_y.minus(Pixels.of(1.0)) ## The grass under a sky `darkness` dark: a rectangle from `grass_top_y` ## down to `roll_margin` below the screen, and `roll_margin` past each side. grass_shape : Fraction -> Shapes.Shape grass_shape = |darkness| Screen.margin_rect( { top: grass_top_y, bottom: Screen.height.plus(Screen.roll_margin) }, Brush.flat(Grass.grass_color_at(darkness)), ) }

name: canvas_apps/safari/GroundSighting.roc
html: ## GroundSighting finds the ground under everything else in a frame, as ## patches: the road, in chunks along each segment in view; the paved corner ## where one segment bends into the next; and the pond beside a segment that ## ends at one. It is never depth sorted, because the ground is painted first, ## under everything. The patches are worked out each frame from where the ## rider's camera stands and the route. import Along import Distance import RoadAhead import Geom import RiderView import GroundPatch import BendInView import Pond import lib.RgbColor GroundSighting :: [].{ ## The ground in view, in paint order: each segment in view in the order of ## `RoadAhead.segments_in_view`. patches_in_view : RoadAhead.RoadView, Geom.Vantage -> List(GroundPatch) patches_in_view = |road, vantage| RoadAhead.segments_in_view(road).join_map( |in_view| ground_patches(road, { vantage, in_view }), ) } ## How many chunks the edges of the road along a segment `length` long are ## laid in: at least one. chunk_count : Distance -> U32 chunk_count = |length| { chunks = length.ratio_to(road_chunk_length).ceiling_to_i64_try() ?? crash "GroundSighting.chunk_count: a segment's length is finite" chunks.max(1).to_u32_wrap() } ## The road along a segment in view, as one patch: across its start, up its ## right edge to the end of each chunk, then back down its left edge. It is ## one patch, not a patch a chunk, because a canvas smooths each patch's ## edges on its own, and where two patches meet the grass under them shows ## through as a pale seam. road_along : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, in_view : RoadAhead.SegmentInView, } -> GroundPatch road_along = |road, { vantage, in_view }| { from_rider = in_view.from_rider segment_length = in_view.segment.length segment_chunk_count = chunk_count(segment_length) corner = |chunk_number, across| { along = chunk_end(segment_length, chunk_number) RoadAhead.rider_point_at(road, { vantage, from_rider, road_point: { along, across } }) } up_right_edge = List.from_iter(U32.until(0, segment_chunk_count + 1)) .map(|number| corner(number, Geom.right_edge)) down_left_edge = List.from_iter(U32.until(0, segment_chunk_count)) .map(|k| corner(segment_chunk_count - k, Geom.left_edge)) road_patch([corner(0, Geom.left_edge)].concat(up_right_edge).concat(down_left_edge)) } road_color : RgbColor road_color = RgbColor.of(0x34353C) ## The road's edges are laid in chunks no longer than this. Chunks at most ## 25 m long keep the chord cut at the horizon below a pixel. road_chunk_length : Distance road_chunk_length = Distance.metres(25.0) ## A bend's paving starts this far before the end of the segment that ## bends. lead_in_length : Distance lead_in_length = Distance.metres(40.0) ## Where chunk `chunk_number` of the road along a segment `segment_length` long ## ends, the chunks counted from 1. Chunk 0 ends where the segment starts. chunk_end : Distance, U32 -> Along chunk_end = |segment_length, chunk_number| { segment_chunk_count = chunk_count(segment_length) Along.at(segment_length.times(chunk_number.to_f64()).divided_by(segment_chunk_count.to_f64())) } ## A patch of road with these corners. road_patch : List(RiderView.RiderPoint) -> GroundPatch road_patch = |corners| GroundPatch.of(corners, road_color) ## The ground of a segment in view: its road, the bend into the next segment ## if the road in view goes on, and its pond if it ends at one. The segment ## just behind lays no road along it, and its bend's paving stands for it, ## because that paving lays the last `lead_in_length` of its road. The cut at the ## near plane does not make this rule: just past a bend, the end of the road ## behind reaches in front of the camera and would draw. Road further back on ## it would show at a bend sharper than a right angle, and the route has none. ground_patches : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, in_view : RoadAhead.SegmentInView, } -> List(GroundPatch) ground_patches = |road, { vantage, in_view }| { along_segment = match in_view.from_rider { Ahead(_) => [road_along(road, { vantage, in_view })] JustBehind => [] } bend = match BendInView.bend_after(road, in_view) { Ok(bend_in_view) => [bend_paving(road, { vantage, bend_in_view })] Err(RoadEndsInView) => [] } [ along_segment, bend, pond_patches(road, { vantage, in_view }), ].join() } ## A bend's paving, as one patch: the last `lead_in_length` of the road before ## the bend, the corner it cuts out to where the two outer edges meet, and the ## first chunk of the road after it. It runs up the left edge and back down the ## right, and the outer edge takes in the apex. ## ## The road along each segment ends inside the paving, so where they meet is ## road over road, and no seam shows. The paving takes in the first chunk after ## the bend for that reason, though that road is laid anyway, and it ends where ## that chunk ends, so its edges there are the road's own. bend_paving : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, bend_in_view : BendInView, } -> GroundPatch bend_paving = |road, { vantage, bend_in_view }| { length_before = bend_in_view.length_before() before = |along, across| bend_in_view.rider_point_before({ road, vantage, road_point: { along, across } }) after = |along, across| bend_in_view.rider_point_after({ road, vantage, road_point: { along, across } }) lead_start = Along.at(length_before.minus(lead_in_length)) end = Along.at(length_before) lead_end = chunk_end(bend_in_view.length_after(road), 1) { end_before, apex, start_after } = bend_in_view.outer_corner_in_view({ road, vantage }) left = Geom.left_edge right = Geom.right_edge corners = match Geom.outer_side(bend_in_view.turn()) { LeftSide => [ before(lead_start, left), end_before, apex, start_after, after(lead_end, left), after(lead_end, right), before(end, right), before(lead_start, right), ] RightSide => [ before(lead_start, left), before(end, left), after(lead_end, left), after(lead_end, right), start_after, apex, end_before, before(lead_start, right), ] } road_patch(corners) } ## The pond past the end of a segment in view: its bank, then its water. A ## segment that ends at no pond has none. pond_patches : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, in_view : RoadAhead.SegmentInView, } -> List(GroundPatch) pond_patches = |road, { vantage, in_view }| { rider_point = |road_point| RoadAhead.rider_point_at(road, { vantage, from_rider: in_view.from_rider, road_point }) match in_view.segment.segment_ending() { Bends({ bend, bend_life: DuckPond }) => Pond.pond_outlines(bend).map( |outline| GroundPatch.of(outline.corners.map(rider_point), outline.color), ) Bends({ bend_life: Animal(_), .. }) | Bends({ bend_life: Quiet, .. }) | RouteEnds => [] } } expect [ (25.0, 1), (25.1, 2), (50.0, 2), (49.9, 2), (1.0, 1), (0.0, 1), (500.0, 20), (320.0, 13), (1200.0, 48), ].all(|(length, want)| chunk_count(Distance.metres(length)).to_i64() == want)

name: canvas_apps/safari/GuardRail.roc
html: ## A guard rail: a metal bar half a metre up, on thin posts, along a path ## on the ground. Each stretch of bar between two points of the path, and ## each post, is a flat quad, which the depth sort places among the frame's ## other things. import lib.Pixels import DepthSort import Distance import lib.Fraction import RiderView import Sky import Sprite import Rendered import lib.RgbColor import Camera import lib.Shapes GuardRail :: [].{ ## A quad of the rail: its corners and its colour. Its low edge runs along ## the path from start to end, and its high edge runs above it. RailQuad : { corners : { low_start : RiderView.PointAtHeight, low_end : RiderView.PointAtHeight, high_end : RiderView.PointAtHeight, high_start : RiderView.PointAtHeight, }, color : RgbColor, } ## The rail along `path_points`: the bars, then the posts. quads_along : List(RiderView.RiderPoint) -> List(GuardRail.RailQuad) quads_along = |path_points| bars(path_points).concat(posts(path_points)) ## A quad as the frame draws it, at its own depth, unless it's wholly ## behind the camera. A rail quad has no kind for `Pipeline` to ask, so it ## renders itself. quad_rendering : GuardRail.RailQuad, Sprite.LensAndLight -> Try(Rendered, [BehindCamera]) quad_rendering = |quad, { focal_length, darkness }| { dimmed_quad = { ..quad, color: Sky.color_at_darkness(quad.color, darkness) } quad_shape(dimmed_quad, focal_length).map_ok( |shape| Rendered.of(quad_depth(quad), Sprite.from_shapes([shape])), ) } } ## How far ahead a quad is, for the depth sort: the mean of its corners' ## distances, taken round the quad from its low start. It is negative for a ## quad behind the rider. quad_depth : GuardRail.RailQuad -> Distance quad_depth = |quad| { { low_start, low_end, high_end, high_start } = quad.corners DepthSort.mean_depth([low_start, low_end, high_end, high_start].map(|corner| corner.forward)) } ## A quad on screen, cut at the camera's near plane, unless it's wholly ## behind the camera. quad_shape : GuardRail.RailQuad, Pixels -> Try(Shapes.Shape, [BehindCamera]) quad_shape = |quad, focal_length| { { low_start, low_end, high_end, high_start } = quad.corners corners = [low_start, low_end, high_end, high_start] Camera.clipped_polygon({ color: quad.color, corners }, focal_length) } bar_middle_height : Distance bar_middle_height = Distance.metres(0.5) bar_thickness : Distance bar_thickness = Distance.metres(0.1) post_width : Distance post_width = Distance.metres(0.02) bar_color : RgbColor bar_color = RgbColor.of(0xC2C7CF) post_color : RgbColor post_color = RgbColor.of(0x9AA0A8) bar_top : Distance bar_top = bar_middle_height.plus(bar_thickness.divided_by(2.0)) bar_bottom : Distance bar_bottom = bar_middle_height.minus(bar_thickness.divided_by(2.0)) post_half_width : Distance post_half_width = post_width.divided_by(2.0) ## A stretch of bar between each two neighbouring points of `path_points`. bars : List(RiderView.RiderPoint) -> List(GuardRail.RailQuad) bars = |path_points| path_points.map2(path_points.drop_first(1), |from, to| bar({ from, to })) ## A post at each point of `path_points`, turned to face along the path from ## the point before it to the point after it. A post at an end of the ## path takes its own point in place of the one it lacks. posts : List(RiderView.RiderPoint) -> List(GuardRail.RailQuad) posts = |path_points| { before = path_points.take_first(1).concat(path_points.drop_last(1)) after = path_points.drop_first(1).concat(path_points.take_last(1)) before.map3( path_points, after, |previous, at, next| post(at, { previous, next }), ) } ## A point of the path, at `height` above the ground. point_at_height : RiderView.RiderPoint, Distance -> RiderView.PointAtHeight point_at_height = |point, height| { right: point.right, forward: point.forward, height } ## The bar from `from` to `to`, bottom edge first. bar : { from : RiderView.RiderPoint, to : RiderView.RiderPoint } -> GuardRail.RailQuad bar = |{ from, to }| { corners: { low_start: point_at_height(from, bar_bottom), low_end: point_at_height(to, bar_bottom), high_end: point_at_height(to, bar_top), high_start: point_at_height(from, bar_top), }, color: bar_color, } ## The post at `at`, half its width to each side of it along the path from ## `previous` to `next`, from the ground to the top of the bar. Two points ## at one place give no direction, and the post then has no width. post : RiderView.RiderPoint, { previous : RiderView.RiderPoint, next : RiderView.RiderPoint, } -> GuardRail.RailQuad post = |at, { previous, next }| { rightward = next.right.minus(previous.right).to_metres() forward = next.forward.minus(previous.forward).to_metres() length = RiderView.ground_distance({ from: previous, to: next }).to_metres() run = if length.to_bits() == 0 { 1.0 } else { length } half_right = post_half_width.times(rightward / run) half_forward = post_half_width.times(forward / run) back = { right: at.right.minus(half_right), forward: at.forward.minus(half_forward) } front = { right: at.right.plus(half_right), forward: at.forward.plus(half_forward) } { corners: { low_start: point_at_height(back, Distance.zero), low_end: point_at_height(front, Distance.zero), high_end: point_at_height(front, bar_top), high_start: point_at_height(back, bar_top), }, color: post_color, } } first_post : List(RiderView.RiderPoint) -> GuardRail.RailQuad first_post = |route_points| posts(route_points).first() ?? crash "a route of two points has posts" straight_points : List(RiderView.RiderPoint) straight_points = [ { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0) }, { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(20.0) }, { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(30.0) }, ] straight_quads : List(GuardRail.RailQuad) straight_quads = GuardRail.quads_along(straight_points) first_bar : GuardRail.RailQuad first_bar = straight_quads.first() ?? crash "a straight route has a rail" expect straight_quads.len() == 5 expect bars(straight_points).len() == 2 expect posts(straight_points).len() == 3 expect straight_quads.map(|quad| quad.color.to_i64()) == [0xC2C7CF, 0xC2C7CF, 0x9AA0A8, 0x9AA0A8, 0x9AA0A8] expect straight_quads.map(|quad| quad_depth(quad).to_metres()) == [15.0, 25.0, 10.0, 20.0, 30.0] behind_bar : GuardRail.RailQuad behind_bar = bar({ from: { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(-20.0) }, to: { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(-10.0) }, }) # A quad stands at its own depth, and one wholly behind the camera isn't drawn. expect { first_bar_depth = GuardRail.quad_rendering(first_bar, by_day).map_ok( |rendering| rendering.depth().to_metres(), ) first_bar_depth == Ok(15.0) } expect GuardRail.quad_rendering(behind_bar, by_day).is_err() ## The test lens, by day. by_day : Sprite.LensAndLight by_day = { focal_length: Pixels.of(500.0), darkness: Fraction.zero } # The first bar runs from one post to the next, between the bar's two heights. expect first_bar.corners.low_start.forward.to_metres() == 10.0 expect first_bar.corners.low_end.forward.to_metres() == 20.0 expect first_bar.corners.high_end.forward.to_metres() == 20.0 expect first_bar.corners.high_start.forward.to_metres() == 10.0 expect first_bar.corners.low_start.height.to_metres() == 0.45 expect first_bar.corners.low_end.height.to_metres() == 0.45 expect first_bar.corners.high_end.height.to_metres() == 0.55 expect first_bar.corners.high_start.height.to_metres() == 0.55 # A post is square to the path, and stands from the ground to the bar's top. straight_post : GuardRail.RailQuad straight_post = first_post(straight_points) expect straight_post.corners.low_start.forward.to_metres() == 9.99 expect straight_post.corners.low_end.forward.to_metres() == 10.01 expect straight_post.corners.high_end.forward.to_metres() == 10.01 expect straight_post.corners.high_start.forward.to_metres() == 9.99 expect straight_post.corners.low_start.height.to_metres() == 0.0 expect straight_post.corners.high_end.height.to_metres() == 0.55 expect straight_post.corners.low_start.right.to_metres() == 0.0 expect straight_post.corners.low_end.right.to_metres() == 0.0 diagonal_post : GuardRail.RailQuad diagonal_post = first_post([ { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0) }, { right: Distance.metres(30.0), forward: Distance.metres(50.0) }, ]) expect diagonal_post.corners.low_start.right.to_metres() == -0.006 expect diagonal_post.corners.low_end.right.to_metres() == 0.006 expect diagonal_post.corners.low_start.forward.to_metres() == 9.992 expect diagonal_post.corners.low_end.forward.to_metres() == 10.008 doubled_points : List(RiderView.RiderPoint) doubled_points = [ { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0) }, { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0) }, ] doubled_post : GuardRail.RailQuad doubled_post = first_post(doubled_points) # A path that goes nowhere keeps its posts, each with no width. expect GuardRail.quads_along(doubled_points).len() == 3 expect doubled_post.corners.low_start.right.to_metres() == 0.0 expect doubled_post.corners.low_end.right.to_metres() == 0.0 expect doubled_post.corners.low_start.forward.to_metres() == 10.0 expect doubled_post.corners.low_end.forward.to_metres() == 10.0 expect doubled_post.corners.high_end.height.to_metres() == 0.55 expect bars([{ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0) }]).len() == 0

name: canvas_apps/safari/LeanSearch.roc
html: ## How far the rider leans. A bisection over leans near the current one ## finds the lean whose coast ends nearest the road's middle. import Across import Angle import Coast import Motorcycle LeanSearch :: [].{ ## Where the search aims a coast to end: the road's middle. aimed_across : Across aimed_across = Across.middle ## Which way the next try should lean, from where this try's coast went: ## off the left shoulder means more right, off the right means more left, ## and a coast that stays on the road compares its end with ## `aimed_across`. A coast that ends exactly there means lean left. lean_correction : Coast.Outcome -> [MoreRight, MoreLeft] lean_correction = |outcome| match outcome { Leaves({ side: Left, .. }) => MoreRight Leaves({ side: Right, .. }) => MoreLeft EndsAt(end_across) => if end_across < LeanSearch.aimed_across { MoreRight } else { MoreLeft } } ## How many times the search halves its bounds. They start 2° wide, a ## degree either side of the lean, so 12 halvings narrow them to about ## 0.0005°. lean_search_round_count : U8 lean_search_round_count = 12 ## The leans a try searches between. LeanBounds : { low : Angle.Lean, high : Angle.Lean } ## The lean halfway between `bounds`, which a try tries. middle_lean : LeanSearch.LeanBounds -> Angle.Lean middle_lean = |{ low, high }| low.halfway_to(high) ## The motorcycle a try coasts: `motorcycle`, the one the search started ## from, with the lean halfway between `bounds`. tried_motorcycle : Motorcycle, LeanSearch.LeanBounds -> Motorcycle tried_motorcycle = |motorcycle, bounds| motorcycle.with_lean(LeanSearch.middle_lean(bounds)) ## One try of the search: the bounds it tried between, and where the coast ## with the lean halfway between them went. LeanTry : { bounds : LeanSearch.LeanBounds, outcome : Coast.Outcome } ## The tries of the bisection over the leans one step can reach from the ## motorcycle's own, in the order tried.
