Each try's bounds are the half of the one ## before it that its coast pointed to. search_tries : Motorcycle -> List(LeanSearch.LeanTry) search_tries = |motorcycle| { var $bounds = first_bounds(motorcycle) var $tries = [] for _ in 0..<lean_search_round_count { tried = lean_try(motorcycle, $bounds) $tries = $tries.append(tried) $bounds = bounds_after(tried) } $tries } ## The lean for the next step, whose coast ends nearest the road's middle: ## halfway between the bounds the last try narrowed to. best_lean : Motorcycle -> Angle.Lean best_lean = |motorcycle| { var $bounds = first_bounds(motorcycle) for _ in 0..<lean_search_round_count { $bounds = bounds_after(lean_try(motorcycle, $bounds)) } LeanSearch.middle_lean($bounds) } } ## The bounds of the search's first try: the leans one step can reach from the ## motorcycle's own. first_bounds : Motorcycle -> LeanSearch.LeanBounds first_bounds = |motorcycle| { low: motorcycle.lean.minus(max_lean_change), high: motorcycle.lean.plus(max_lean_change), } ## The most the lean changes in one step. max_lean_change : Angle.LeanChange max_lean_change = Angle.LeanChange.degrees(1.0) ## The try between `bounds`: where the coast of the tried motorcycle goes. lean_try : Motorcycle, LeanSearch.LeanBounds -> LeanSearch.LeanTry lean_try = |motorcycle, bounds| { bounds, outcome: Coast.coast_outcome(LeanSearch.tried_motorcycle(motorcycle, bounds)), } ## The half of a try's bounds its coast points to. bounds_after : LeanSearch.LeanTry -> LeanSearch.LeanBounds bounds_after = |{ bounds, outcome }| { mid = LeanSearch.middle_lean(bounds) match LeanSearch.lean_correction(outcome) { MoreRight => { low: mid, high: bounds.high } MoreLeft => { low: bounds.low, high: mid } } } ## A coast that ends `metres` across the road. ending_at : F64 -> Coast.Outcome ending_at = |metres| EndsAt(Across.metres(metres)) expect LeanSearch.lean_correction(ending_at(-0.1)) == MoreRight expect LeanSearch.lean_correction(ending_at(0.1)) == MoreLeft expect LeanSearch.lean_correction(ending_at(0.0)) == MoreLeft ## Bounds a degree either side of upright. upright_bounds : LeanSearch.LeanBounds upright_bounds = { low: Angle.Lean.degrees(-1.0), high: Angle.Lean.degrees(1.0) } # A try halves its bounds, keeping the half its coast points to. expect LeanSearch.middle_lean(upright_bounds) == Angle.Lean.degrees(0.0) expect bounds_after({ bounds: upright_bounds, outcome: ending_at(-0.1) }) == { low: Angle.Lean.degrees(0.0), high: Angle.Lean.degrees(1.0) } expect bounds_after({ bounds: upright_bounds, outcome: ending_at(0.1) }) == { low: Angle.Lean.degrees(-1.0), high: Angle.Lean.degrees(0.0) } ## The lean the search picks for a motorcycle at the start of the segment, in ## radians. searched_lean : F64, F64 -> F64 searched_lean = |across, lean_radians| LeanSearch.best_lean({ ..Motorcycle.initial, route_place: { ..Motorcycle.initial.route_place, road_point: { ..Motorcycle.initial.route_place.road_point, across: Across.metres(across), }, }, lean: Angle.Lean.radians(lean_radians), }).to_radians() ## The search's tries for the motorcycle the ride starts with. initial_tries : List(LeanSearch.LeanTry) initial_tries = LeanSearch.search_tries(Motorcycle.initial) # The search makes its rounds of tries, the first between the leans one step can # reach, and each after it between the half of the one before that its coast # pointed to. expect initial_tries.len() == LeanSearch.lean_search_round_count.to_u64() expect initial_tries.first().map_ok(|first| first.bounds) == Ok(first_bounds(Motorcycle.initial)) expect initial_tries .map2(initial_tries.drop_first(1), |before, after| after.bounds == bounds_after(before)) .all(|is_followed| is_followed) # The lean the search picks is the middle of the half its last try pointed to. expect { picked = initial_tries.last().map_ok(|last| LeanSearch.middle_lean(bounds_after(last))) picked == Ok(LeanSearch.best_lean(Motorcycle.initial)) } # An upright rider right of the middle leans left, and one left of it leans # right. expect searched_lean(1.0, 0.0) < 0.0 expect searched_lean(-1.0, 0.0) > 0.0 # A lean held to the right stays further right than an upright rider's. expect { held = searched_lean(0.0, 0.5) centred = searched_lean(0.0, 0.0) held > centred }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Motorcycle.roc
html: ## The motorcycle the rider sits on: where it is on the route, which way it ## points, how fast it goes and how far it leans, and the physics that moves it ## a step. The lean steers the motorcycle, and it moves along the middle of the ## step's turn, in its segment's frame. It is kept from one step to the next, ## as part of the `Rider`. import Acceleration import Along import Angle import Distance import Geom import RoutePlace import Speed import VehicleLimits ## The motorcycle at one step. `route_place` places it on the route, and `yaw` ## is its turn from its segment's axis. `lean` is how far it tips. Nominal, not ## opaque: other modules read its fields. Motorcycle := { route_place : RoutePlace, yaw : Angle.Turn, speed : Speed, lean : Angle.Lean, }.{ initial : Motorcycle initial = { route_place: RoutePlace.route_start, yaw: Angle.straight_ahead, speed: VehicleLimits.starting_speed, lean: Angle.upright, } ## What the rider sets for a step: the lean the motorcycle takes, and how ## hard it accelerates. Controls : { lean : Angle.Lean, acceleration : Acceleration } ## The motorcycle one step on, at the lean its controls set and the speed ## their acceleration gives, held to the top speed. motorcycle_at_next_step : Motorcycle, Motorcycle.Controls -> Motorcycle motorcycle_at_next_step = |motorcycle, { lean, acceleration }| { speed = allowed_speed(motorcycle.speed.accelerated_by(acceleration)) step_length = speed.step_length() turn = lean.steer(turn_per_lean) mid = motorcycle.yaw.plus(turn.times(0.5)).to_radians() place = motorcycle.route_place { route_place: { ..place, road_point: { along: place.road_point.along.plus(step_length.times(mid.cos())), across: place.road_point.across.plus(step_length.times(mid.sin())), }, }, yaw: motorcycle.yaw.plus(turn), speed, lean, } } ## The controls that keep this motorcycle's lean and speed as they are. steady_controls : Motorcycle -> Motorcycle.Controls steady_controls = |motorcycle| { lean: motorcycle.lean, acceleration: Acceleration.steady } with_lean : Motorcycle, Angle.Lean -> Motorcycle with_lean = |motorcycle, lean| { ..motorcycle, lean } ## This motorcycle carried over `bend`, the bend out of its segment, when ## that puts it on the next segment's road: placed on that segment and turned ## to its axis. Short of that, it stays where it is. cross_bend_if_on_road : Motorcycle, Geom.Bend -> Motorcycle cross_bend_if_on_road = |motorcycle, bend| { on_next = motorcycle.route_place.route_place_past_bend(bend) if on_next.is_on_road() { { ..motorcycle, route_place: on_next, yaw: motorcycle.yaw.minus(bend.turn), } } else { motorcycle } } ## This motorcycle stopped dead at `at` on its segment. stopped_at : Motorcycle, Along -> Motorcycle stopped_at = |motorcycle, at| { place = motorcycle.route_place { ..motorcycle, route_place: { ..place, road_point: { ..place.road_point, along: at } }, speed: Speed.at_rest, } } ## Whether this motorcycle has come to `at` on its segment, or gone past. has_reached : Motorcycle, Along -> Bool has_reached = |motorcycle, at| motorcycle.route_place.road_point.along >= at is_eq : _ } ## How far the motorcycle turns in a step for each radian of lean. This is an ## honest cheat, chosen by eye: a real bike's turn at a given lean depends on ## its speed, and here it doesn't. The ride never asks for more, because the ## lean search picks each step's lean by coasting this same physics, so the ## rider leans for the turn the bike really makes at any speed. turn_per_lean : F64 turn_per_lean = 0.1 ## The speed the rider may reach: `next_speed`, held to the top speed. allowed_speed : Speed -> Speed allowed_speed = |next_speed| next_speed.min(VehicleLimits.top_speed) ## The speed the clamp allows for `next_speed` metres a step. clamped_speed : F64 -> F64 clamped_speed = |next_speed| allowed_speed(Speed.metres_a_step(next_speed)).to_metres_a_step() # Up to the top speed the speed is as asked, and past it it is held there. expect clamped_speed(1.0) == 1.0 expect clamped_speed(0.1) == 0.1 expect clamped_speed(2.5) == 2.5 expect clamped_speed(3.0) == 2.5 expect clamped_speed(0.0) == 0.0 ## A motorcycle well along a segment, leaning a little to the right. riding : Motorcycle riding = { route_place: { ..RoutePlace.route_start, road_point: { along: Along.metres(120.5), across: RoutePlace.route_start.road_point.across.plus(Distance.metres(2.25)), }, }, yaw: Angle.Turn.radians(0.375), speed: Speed.metres_a_step(0.8), lean: Angle.Lean.radians(0.125), } # The first two steps change the lean and the speed a little from the step # before, and the third keeps them. first_step : Motorcycle first_step = riding.motorcycle_at_next_step({ lean: Angle.Lean.radians(0.175), acceleration: Acceleration.metres_a_step_each_step(0.01), }) second_step : Motorcycle second_step = first_step.motorcycle_at_next_step({ lean: Angle.Lean.radians(0.155), acceleration: Acceleration.metres_a_step_each_step(0.005), }) third_step : Motorcycle third_step = second_step.motorcycle_at_next_step(second_step.steady_controls()) expect [ (first_step.yaw.to_radians(), 0.3925), (first_step.speed.to_metres_a_step(), 0.81), (first_step.lean.to_radians(), 0.175), (second_step.yaw.to_radians(), 0.40800000000000003), (second_step.speed.to_metres_a_step(), 0.8150000000000001), (second_step.lean.to_radians(), 0.155), (third_step.yaw.to_radians(), 0.42350000000000004), (third_step.speed.to_metres_a_step(), 0.8150000000000001), (third_step.lean.to_radians(), 0.155), ].all(|(got, want)| got == want) # Each is within 1e-9 of its want, scaled up by a want past 1. expect [ (first_step.route_place.road_point.along.to_metres(), 121.25108639750266), (first_step.route_place.road_point.across.to_metres(), 2.5532642799382796), (second_step.route_place.road_point.along.to_metres(), 122.00167174017032), (second_step.route_place.road_point.across.to_metres(), 2.8708278851774045), (third_step.route_place.road_point.along.to_metres(), 122.7472448817898), (third_step.route_place.road_point.across.to_metres(), 3.1999869508214647), ].all(|(got, want)| (got - want).abs() <= 0.000000001 * want.abs().max(1.0)) expect { a = Motorcycle.initial.motorcycle_at_next_step(Motorcycle.initial.steady_controls()) b = Motorcycle.motorcycle_at_next_step( Motorcycle.initial, { lean: Angle.Lean.radians(0.5), acceleration: Acceleration.metres_a_step_each_step(0.25) }, ) [ (a.route_place.road_point.across.to_metres(), 0.0), (a.yaw.to_radians(), 0.0), (a.lean.to_radians(), 0.0), (a.speed.to_metres_a_step(), 0.3), (b.lean.to_radians(), 0.5), (b.speed.to_metres_a_step(), 0.55), (b.yaw.to_radians(), 0.05), ].all(|(got, want)| got == want) } ## A bend at the end of a 500-metre segment, turning a little to the right. gentle_bend : Geom.Bend gentle_bend = { segment_length: Distance.metres(500.0), turn: Angle.Turn.radians(0.3) } ## A motorcycle on the middle of the road, `along` metres down its segment. motorcycle_at : F64 -> Motorcycle motorcycle_at = |along| { ..Motorcycle.initial, route_place: { ..RoutePlace.route_start, road_point: { ..RoutePlace.route_start.road_point, along: Along.metres(along) }, }, } ## The place of a motorcycle `along` metres down its segment, carried over the ## gentle bend. place_past_bend : F64 -> RoutePlace place_past_bend = |along| motorcycle_at(along).route_place.route_place_past_bend(gentle_bend) # Carried over the bend from well short of it, a place lands far off the next # segment's road, and from the bend itself it lands on it. Either way it is on # the next segment. expect place_past_bend(100.0).road_point.across.distance_from_middle() > Distance.metres(100.0) expect place_past_bend(500.0).is_on_road() expect { next_index = RoutePlace.route_start.segment_index.next() [100.0, 500.0].all(|along| place_past_bend(along).segment_index == next_index) } # So from well short of the bend the motorcycle stays where it was, and from the # bend it crosses, turned to the next segment's axis. expect motorcycle_at(100.0).cross_bend_if_on_road(gentle_bend) == motorcycle_at(100.0) expect { crossed = motorcycle_at(500.0).cross_bend_if_on_road(gentle_bend) next_index = RoutePlace.route_start.segment_index.next() crossed.route_place.segment_index == next_index and crossed.yaw.to_radians() == -0.3 } expect motorcycle_at(300.0).has_reached(Along.metres(300.0)) expect motorcycle_at(310.0).has_reached(Along.metres(300.0)) expect !motorcycle_at(299.99).has_reached(Along.metres(300.0))

name: canvas_apps/safari/PigHerd.roc
html: ## A herd of pigs grazes on the right of the road about a place along it, in a ## big herd or in two short rows. One pig of each herd stands out from the rest. import Across import Along import Billboard import Distance import EmojiStill import Geom import Scatter PigHerd := [BigHerd(PigHerd.BigPigHerd), TwoRows].{ ## A big herd: rows of columns, each pig strayed a little from its place. ## The front row is nearest the road, and each row behind it stands farther ## from the road and as far again along it. The front row always has its ## standout pig: the columns are counted either side of it. BigPigHerd := { ## How many columns stand before the standout pig's, and after it. columns_before_standout : U64, columns_after_standout : U64, ## How many rows stand behind the front row. rows_behind_front : U64, }.{ is_eq : _ } ## The herd's pigs about `herd_along`. herd_pigs : PigHerd, Along -> List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) herd_pigs = |herd, herd_along| match herd { BigHerd(big_herd) => big_herd_pigs(big_herd, herd_along) TwoRows => two_row_pigs(herd_along) } ## The herd's pig that stands out, about `herd_along`. standout_pig : PigHerd, Along -> Geom.Placed(Billboard) standout_pig = |herd, herd_along| match herd { BigHerd(big_herd) => big_herd_standout_pig(big_herd, herd_along) TwoRows => two_row_standout_pig(herd_along) } is_eq : _ } ## How far from the middle of the road the row of pigs nearest it stands, 10 ## metres off the road's edge. Each herd sets its own. front_row_distance : Distance front_row_distance = Geom.road_half_width.plus(Distance.metres(10.0)) ## Where the row of pigs nearest the road stands across it. front_row_across : Across front_row_across = Across.right_of_middle(front_row_distance) ## How every pig looks: the pig emoji, a little over a metre tall. pig_species : Billboard.Species pig_species = { emoji: EmojiStill.pig, adult_height: Distance.metres(1.1) } placed_pig : { along : Along, across : Across } -> Geom.Placed(Billboard) placed_pig = |{ along, across }| { road_point: { along, across }, lift: Distance.zero, kind: Billboard.adult_billboard(pig_species, FacesLeft), } ## Where the big herd's first column is along the road, from the herd's place, ## chosen by eye. big_herd_first_column_offset : Distance big_herd_first_column_offset = Distance.metres(-6.0) ## The distance between the big herd's columns, along the road, chosen by eye. big_herd_column_spacing : Distance big_herd_column_spacing = Distance.metres(4.0) ## How much farther from the road each row of the big herd stands than the one ## in front, and how much farther along it, chosen by eye. big_herd_row_depth : Distance big_herd_row_depth = Distance.metres(6.0) ## How far a pig of the big herd strays from its place along the road, chosen ## by eye. big_herd_jitter_along : Distance big_herd_jitter_along = Distance.metres(1.2) ## How far a pig of the big herd strays from its place across the road, chosen ## by eye. big_herd_jitter_across : Distance big_herd_jitter_across = Distance.metres(1.0) ## The big herd's pigs about `herd_along`, row by row from the road. big_herd_pigs : PigHerd.BigPigHerd, Along -> List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) big_herd_pigs = |herd, herd_along| { columns = List.from_iter(U64.until(0, column_count(herd))) List.from_iter(U64.until(0, herd.rows_behind_front + 1)) .join_map(|row| columns.map(|column| herd_pig(herd, { herd_along, row, column }))) } ## The big herd's pig that stands out, about `herd_along`. big_herd_standout_pig : PigHerd.BigPigHerd, Along -> Geom.Placed(Billboard) big_herd_standout_pig = |herd, herd_along| { column = herd.columns_before_standout herd_pig(herd, { herd_along, row: 0, column }) } ## How many columns the big herd has: those either side of the standout pig's, ## and its own. column_count : PigHerd.BigPigHerd -> U64 column_count = |herd| herd.columns_before_standout + 1 + herd.columns_after_standout ## The two-row herd, four pigs in front and six behind, the back row farther ## from the road, chosen by eye. The third pig of the front row stands out. four_in_front_six_behind : { ## Where the pigs of the front row are along the road, from the herd's ## place: the pigs before the standout pig, the standout pig, and the ## pigs after it. front_row : { offsets_before : List(Distance), standout_offset : Distance, offsets_after : List(Distance), }, ## Where the pigs of the back row are along the road, from the herd's ## place. back_offsets : List(Distance), ## How much farther from the road the back row stands than the front. back_row_depth : Distance, } four_in_front_six_behind = { front_row: { offsets_before: [-6.0, -2.0].map(Distance.metres), standout_offset: Distance.metres(2.0), offsets_after: [6.0].map(Distance.metres), }, back_offsets: [ -10.0, -6.0, -2.0, 2.0, 6.0, 10.0, ].map(Distance.metres), back_row_depth: Distance.metres(6.0), } ## Where the two-row herd's front row pigs are along the road, from the herd's ## place, in the order they stand. two_row_front_offsets : List(Distance) two_row_front_offsets = { row = four_in_front_six_behind.front_row row.offsets_before.append(row.standout_offset).concat(row.offsets_after) } ## The two-row herd's pig that stands out, about `herd_along`. two_row_standout_pig : Along -> Geom.Placed(Billboard) two_row_standout_pig = |herd_along| { along = herd_along.plus(four_in_front_six_behind.front_row.standout_offset) placed_pig({ along, across: front_row_across }) } ## The two-row herd's pigs about `herd_along`, front row first. two_row_pigs : Along -> List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) two_row_pigs = |herd_along| { herd = four_in_front_six_behind back_across = front_row_across.plus(herd.back_row_depth) row_pigs(herd_along, { across: front_row_across, offsets: two_row_front_offsets }) .concat(row_pigs(herd_along, { across: back_across, offsets: herd.back_offsets })) } ## The big herd's pig in `row` and `column`. The scatter's phases, 2.3 along ## the road and 1.7 across it, are chosen by eye. herd_pig : PigHerd.BigPigHerd, { herd_along : Along, row : U64, column : U64, } -> Geom.Placed(Billboard) herd_pig = |herd, { herd_along, row, column }| { rows_back = row.to_f64() columns_along = column.to_f64() first_column = herd_along.plus(big_herd_first_column_offset) in_column = first_column.plus(big_herd_column_spacing.times(columns_along)) in_line = in_column.plus(big_herd_row_depth.times(rows_back)) in_row = front_row_across.plus(big_herd_row_depth.times(rows_back)) stray = Scatter.stray_of( row * column_count(herd) + column, { along_phase: 2.3, across_phase: 1.7, jitter_along: big_herd_jitter_along, jitter_across: big_herd_jitter_across, }, ) placed_pig({ along: in_line.plus(stray.along), across: in_row.plus(stray.across) }) } row_pigs : Along, { across : Across, offsets : List(Distance) } -> List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) row_pigs = |herd_along, { across, offsets }| offsets.map(|offset| placed_pig({ along: herd_along.plus(offset), across })) ## A big herd of three rows of four, the second pig of the front row standing ## out. It has more columns after the standout than before it, and more columns ## than rows, so a swap of either pair shows. three_rows_of_four : PigHerd.BigPigHerd three_rows_of_four = { columns_before_standout: 1, columns_after_standout: 2, rows_behind_front: 2, } ## Where this herd stands along the road. fixture_herd_along : Along fixture_herd_along = Along.metres(940.0) # A big herd has a pig for each row and column, wherever the herd stands. expect PigHerd.BigHerd(three_rows_of_four).herd_pigs(fixture_herd_along).len() == 12 expect PigHerd.BigHerd(three_rows_of_four).herd_pigs(Along.metres(440.0)).len() == 12 eye_catcher : Geom.Placed(Billboard) eye_catcher = PigHerd.BigHerd(three_rows_of_four).standout_pig(fixture_herd_along) all_pigs : List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) all_pigs = PigHerd.BigHerd(three_rows_of_four).herd_pigs(fixture_herd_along) herd_pig_at : U64 -> Geom.Placed(Billboard) herd_pig_at = |i| all_pigs.get(i) ?? crash "PigHerd's expects: the big herd has 12 pigs" # The big herd's standout is the pig of the front row after the columns before # it, and it is one pig of the herd. expect herd_pig_at(1) == eye_catcher expect all_pigs.count_if(|herd_member| herd_member == eye_catcher) == 1 # Row by row from the road, each pig within the jitter of its place: along the # road and across it. expect [ (0, 934.0, 12.0), (1, 938.0, 12.0), (2, 942.0, 12.0), (3, 946.0, 12.0), (4, 940.0, 18.0), (5, 944.0, 18.0), (6, 948.0, 18.0), (7, 952.0, 18.0), (8, 946.0, 24.0), (9, 950.0, 24.0), (10, 954.0, 24.0), (11, 958.0, 24.0), ].all( |(i, along, across)| { place = herd_pig_at(i).road_point along_miss = (place.along.to_metres() - along).abs() across_miss = (place.across.to_metres() - across).abs() along_miss <= 1.2 and across_miss <= 1.0 }, )

name: canvas_apps/safari/Pipeline.roc
html: ## Pipeline carries an object through a frame, by way of three forms of it. An ## object is placed on the road (`Geom.Placed`), sighted from the camera ## (`Pipeline.Sighted`) and rendered (`Rendered`). The steps between them are ## written once here, for every kind of object. A kind is a type like `Conifer`, ## which knows nothing of this module: a `where` clause names the methods a step ## needs, and it matches them by name alone, so those names say what they are ## for. A kind holds how the object looks right now, and the form around it holds ## where the object is. ## ## A sighting can be refused with `OutOfSight`, which means the object isn't ## drawn this frame. No caller needs to know which test refused it. Three tests ## give it, one inside the next. ## The near plane test refuses an object whose foot is short of the camera's ## near plane, as `RiderView.rider_point_ahead` decides for ## `Pipeline.sighting_of`, and every sighting takes this test. ## The horizon test refuses an object the earth's curve hides whole, as ## `EarthCurve.is_below_horizon` decides for `Pipeline.sighting_above_horizon_of`, ## which every kind with a height takes, the towers among them. ## The size test refuses an object that would stand less than ## `Pipeline.smallest_height_on_screen` tall, as `Pipeline.scenery_sighting_of` ## decides for the trees, the billboards, the cats and the birds, though not ## for the towers or the truck. ## `TruckSighting.truck_in_view` also gives `OutOfSight` when the truck is past ## the route's end or off the road ahead, before it sights the truck. ## `NoPose` means a segment in view has no cat or bird, or its encounter is ## over, as `EncounterPoses` decides before any camera looks. ## `NoMidTower` means the segment is too short for a tower halfway along, as ## `TowerSighting` decides from its length. ## Only the segments of `RoadAhead.segments_in_view` are looked at at all. Below ## a sighting, a shape can be dropped too: a part of the guard rail, a ground ## patch or a face of the truck cut away whole at the near plane ## (`Camera.clipped_polygon`), a ground patch `PastHorizon`, or a beacon that is ## `TooDim` or `TooSmall` (`Beacon.disc`). import RoadAhead import SegmentFromRider import Camera import Distance import EarthCurve import Geom import RiderView import Sprite import lib.Pixels import Rendered import Spot Pipeline :: [].{ ## An object in the rider's view, and what kind of object it is, for one ## frame. Sighted(kind) : { spot : Spot, kind : kind } ## The camera a sighting is made through: where it stands and faces, and ## the focal length of its lens. SightingCamera : { vantage : Geom.Vantage, focal_length : Pixels } ## `placed` as a camera at `vantage` sees it, on the segment that lies at ## `from_rider`, if it is at or past the camera's near plane. sighting_of : Geom.Placed(kind), { road : RoadAhead.RoadView, vantage : Geom.Vantage, from_rider : SegmentFromRider, } -> Try(Pipeline.Sighted(kind), [OutOfSight]) sighting_of = |placed, { road, vantage, from_rider }| { road_point = placed.road_point rider_point = RoadAhead.rider_point_at(road, { vantage, from_rider, road_point }) foot = RiderView.rider_point_ahead(rider_point) ? |BehindCamera| OutOfSight road_heading = RoadAhead.road_heading_at(road, { vantage, from_rider, road_point }) spot = Spot.at({ lift: placed.lift, foot, road_heading }) Ok({ spot, kind: placed.kind }) } ## The sighting of `placed` on the segment at `from_rider`, if some of it shows ## over the horizon: its top, its kind's height above its lift and lowered ## by the ground's drop, is not hidden behind the curve of the ground. Every ## kind with a height takes this test here. sighting_above_horizon_of : Geom.Placed(kind), { road : RoadAhead.RoadView, vantage : Geom.Vantage, from_rider : SegmentFromRider, } -> Try(Pipeline.Sighted(kind), [OutOfSight]) where [kind.scenery_height : kind -> Distance] sighting_above_horizon_of = |placed, { road, vantage, from_rider }| { sighting = sighting_of(placed, { road, vantage, from_rider })? spot = sighting.spot top = spot.lift().plus(placed.kind.scenery_height()).minus(spot.drop()) if EarthCurve.is_below_horizon({ point: spot.foot().to_rider(), top }) { Err(OutOfSight) } else { Ok(sighting) } } ## The sighting of scenery `placed` on the segment at `from_rider`, if it shows ## over the horizon and stands at least `smallest_height_on_screen` tall ## through the camera's own lens, so that what is at the edge of sight ## comes and goes as the camera widens. Every kind with a size test takes ## it here. scenery_sighting_of : Geom.Placed(kind), { road : RoadAhead.RoadView, camera : Pipeline.SightingCamera, from_rider : SegmentFromRider, } -> Try(Pipeline.Sighted(kind), [OutOfSight]) where [kind.scenery_height : kind -> Distance] scenery_sighting_of = |placed, { road, camera, from_rider }| { sighting = sighting_above_horizon_of(placed, { road, vantage: camera.vantage, from_rider })? height_on_screen = Camera.height_on_screen( { height: placed.kind.scenery_height(), forward: sighting.spot.foot().forward() }, camera.focal_length, ) if height_on_screen < smallest_height_on_screen { Err(OutOfSight) } else { Ok(sighting) } } ## The rendering of `sighting` through the frame's lens, in its light. rendering_of : Pipeline.Sighted(kind), Sprite.LensAndLight -> Rendered where [kind.scenery_sprite : kind, Sprite.Setting -> Sprite] rendering_of = |sighting, { focal_length, darkness }| Rendered.of( sighting.spot.foot().forward(), sighting.kind.scenery_sprite({ spot: sighting.spot, focal_length, darkness }), ) ## The smallest thing worth drawing: an object that would stand less than ## this tall on the screen isn't drawn. smallest_height_on_screen : Pixels smallest_height_on_screen = Pixels.of(2.0) }

name: canvas_apps/safari/RailSighting.roc
html: ## RailSighting lays out the guard rail at each bend in view. The rail follows ## the outer edge of the road for the last few metres before the bend, ## cuts across the bend's corner to where the two outer edges meet and ## back, and follows the next segment's outer edge for as far again. Unlike its ## sibling sightings, it doesn't go through `Pipeline`: a rail is a path in the ## rider's frame, not an object standing at a spot. The rail is worked out each ## frame from where the rider's camera stands and the route. import Along import Distance import RoadAhead import Geom import RiderView import GuardRail import BendInView RailSighting :: [].{ ## The quads of the rails at every bend in view: the bends along the road ## ahead, then the bend from the segment behind. rail_quads_in_view : RoadAhead.RoadView, Geom.Vantage -> List(GuardRail.RailQuad) rail_quads_in_view = |road, vantage| RoadAhead.segments_in_view(road).join_map( |in_view| match BendInView.bend_after(road, in_view) { Ok(bend_in_view) => { path_points = rail_points(road, { vantage, bend_in_view }) GuardRail.quads_along(path_points) } Err(RoadEndsInView) => [] }, ) } ## The rail along the last `rail_run_on` of the segment before a bend, at ## the bend's outer edge: a point a metre, ending at the segment's end. runup_points : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, bend_in_view : BendInView, } -> List(RiderView.RiderPoint) runup_points = |road, { vantage, bend_in_view }| { length = bend_in_view.length_before() across = bend_in_view.outer_edge() run_on_metres = leg_pieces(rail_run_on) List.from_iter(U32.to(0, run_on_metres)).map( |metres_in| { metres_left = Distance.metres((run_on_metres - metres_in).to_f64()) road_point = { along: Along.at(length.minus(metres_left)), across } bend_in_view.rider_point_before({ road, vantage, road_point }) }, ) } ## The rail along the first `rail_run_on` of the segment after a bend, at ## the bend's outer edge: a point a metre, the first a metre in. runout_points : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, bend_in_view : BendInView, } -> List(RiderView.RiderPoint) runout_points = |road, { vantage, bend_in_view }| { across = bend_in_view.outer_edge() List.from_iter(U32.to(1, leg_pieces(rail_run_on))).map( |metres_in| { road_point = { along: Along.metres(metres_in.to_f64()), across } bend_in_view.rider_point_after({ road, vantage, road_point }) }, ) } ## How far the rail runs on, a post a metre, past each end of a bend. rail_run_on : Distance rail_run_on = Distance.metres(10.0) ## How many pieces a leg `distance` long is cut into: one a metre, and at ## least one. leg_pieces : Distance -> U32 leg_pieces = |distance| { pieces = distance.to_metres().round_to_i64_try() ?? crash "RailSighting.leg_pieces: a leg's length is finite" pieces.max(1).to_u32_wrap() } ## `pieces` + 1 points evenly spaced from `from` to `to`, both included. evenly_spaced : { from : RiderView.RiderPoint, to : RiderView.RiderPoint, pieces : U32, } -> List(RiderView.RiderPoint) evenly_spaced = |{ from, to, pieces }| { rightward = to.right.minus(from.right) forward = to.forward.minus(from.forward) List.from_iter(U32.to(0, pieces)).map( |step| { fraction = step.to_f64() / pieces.to_f64() { right: from.right.plus(rightward.times(fraction)), forward: from.forward.plus(forward.times(fraction)), } }, ) } ## A leg of rail from `from` to `to`: a point about every metre, the ## last at `to`, and none at `from`, which ends the leg before it. leg_points : { from : RiderView.RiderPoint, to : RiderView.RiderPoint, } -> List(RiderView.RiderPoint) leg_points = |{ from, to }| { pieces = leg_pieces(RiderView.ground_distance({ from, to })) evenly_spaced({ from, to, pieces }).drop_first(1) } ## The path of the rail at a bend, along the road's outer edge: up to the ## bend, out to where the two outer edges meet, back to the next segment, ## and along it. rail_points : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, bend_in_view : BendInView, } -> List(RiderView.RiderPoint) rail_points = |road, { vantage, bend_in_view }| { { end_before, apex, start_after } = bend_in_view.outer_corner_in_view({ road, vantage }) [ runup_points(road, { vantage, bend_in_view }), leg_points({ from: end_before, to: apex }), leg_points({ from: apex, to: start_after }), runout_points(road, { vantage, bend_in_view }), ].join() } expect [ (0.0, 1), (0.4, 1), (0.5, 1), (1.0, 1), (1.4, 1), (1.5, 2), (2.5, 3), (10.0, 10), (49.6, 50), (50.0, 50), ].all(|(distance, want)| leg_pieces(Distance.metres(distance)).to_i64() == want) origin_point : RiderView.RiderPoint origin_point = { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(0.0) } point_at : List(RiderView.RiderPoint), U64 -> RiderView.RiderPoint point_at = |points, i| points.get(i) ?? crash "RailSighting: an index past the leg's end" straight_points : List(RiderView.RiderPoint) straight_points = leg_points({ from: origin_point, to: { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0) }, }) expect straight_points.len() == 10 expect point_at(straight_points, 0).forward.to_metres() == 1.0 expect point_at(straight_points, 4).forward.to_metres() == 5.0 expect point_at(straight_points, 9).forward.to_metres() == 10.0 expect point_at(straight_points, 0).right.to_metres() == 0.0 expect point_at(straight_points, 9).right.to_metres() == 0.0 diagonal_points : List(RiderView.RiderPoint) diagonal_points = leg_points({ from: origin_point, to: { right: Distance.metres(30.0), forward: Distance.metres(40.0) }, }) expect diagonal_points.len() == 50 expect point_at(diagonal_points, 49).right.to_metres() == 30.0 expect point_at(diagonal_points, 49).forward.to_metres() == 40.0 expect point_at(diagonal_points, 24).right.to_metres() == 15.0 expect point_at(diagonal_points, 24).forward.to_metres() == 20.0 expect { in_place = leg_points({ from: { right: Distance.metres(3.0), forward: Distance.metres(4.0) }, to: { right: Distance.metres(3.0), forward: Distance.metres(4.0) }, }) in_place.len() == 1 and point_at(in_place, 0) == { right: Distance.metres(3.0), forward: Distance.metres(4.0), } } expect { spaced = evenly_spaced({ from: origin_point, to: { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0) }, pieces: 10, }) spaced.len() == 11 and point_at(spaced, 0).forward.to_metres() == 0.0 and point_at(spaced, 10).forward.to_metres() == 10.0 }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Rendered.roc
html: ## A Rendered is one object as a frame paints it: its sprite and how far ahead ## of the camera it stands. Nothing here says what sort of object it is, so every ## sort meets in one list, and that list is what the depth sort orders. import DepthSort import Distance import Sprite Rendered :: { depth : Distance, sprite : Sprite }.{ ## The rendering of `sprite`, standing `depth` ahead of the camera. of : Distance, Sprite -> Rendered of = |depth, sprite| Rendered.({ depth, sprite }) ## How far ahead of the camera it is, negative for what is behind the rider. depth : Rendered -> Distance depth = |Rendered.(rendering)| rendering.depth ## What the frame paints. sprite : Rendered -> Sprite sprite = |Rendered.(rendering)| rendering.sprite ## `renderings` from far to near, sorted by `DepthSort.sort_by`. depth_sorted_renderings : List(Rendered) -> List(Rendered) depth_sorted_renderings = |renderings| DepthSort.sort_by(renderings, |rendering| rendering.depth()) }

name: canvas_apps/safari/RideInstant.roc
html: ## RideInstant is one step of the ride, and how the ride moves from one step to ## the next: the rider and the truck each move once, the clock ticks, and the ## encounter on the rider's segment is planned as the rider nears it. A ride ## that has finished starts again from the beginning. import Animation import Encounter import EncounterPlan import Clock import Distance import Motorcycle import Route import Rider import TruckJourney ## One instant of the ride, and all that is kept from one step to the next: the ## rider and the truck, each moved once a step from where it was, the clock, ## which counts the steps, and when the encounter on the rider's segment ## starts. Everything else that changes is worked out from these four. It is ## nominal, not opaque: other modules read its fields. RideInstant := { rider : Rider, truck : TruckJourney.TruckProgress, clock : Clock, encounter_plan : EncounterPlan, }.{ initial : RideInstant initial = { rider: Rider.initial, truck: TruckJourney.initial, clock: Clock.start, encounter_plan: Unplanned, } ## The instant a step after `instant`, or the ride's start again once the ## rider has finished; the tag says which. next_or_restart : Route, RideInstant -> [Continued(RideInstant), Restarted(RideInstant)] next_or_restart = |route, instant| if instant.rider.is_finished(route) { Restarted(initial) } else { Continued(next(route, instant)) } ## How far along `route` the rider of `instant` is. rider_distance : Route, RideInstant -> Distance rider_distance = |route, instant| instant.rider.motorcycle.route_place.distance_along(route) ## The index of the segment the rider of `instant` is on. rider_segment_index : RideInstant -> Route.SegmentIndex rider_segment_index = |instant| instant.rider.motorcycle.route_place.segment_index ## Where the encounter on the rider's segment of `route` has got to at ## `instant`. encounter_stage : Route, RideInstant -> Animation.Stage encounter_stage = |route, instant| instant.rider.motorcycle.route_place.segment_on(route).encounter.encounter_stage( { plan: instant.encounter_plan, now: instant.clock }, ) } ## The instant a step after `instant`. The world and the rider change each ## other within one step, in this order. First the rider reads the world as it ## stands at the old clock: the stage of the encounter on the rider's segment. ## Then the rider steps, and the clock ticks. Then the world answers the rider ## that has just moved. The truck aims at how far along the route this step's ## rider is, and the encounter plan is kept, forgotten at a new segment, or made ## from this step's rider at the new clock. The rider never reads the truck. next : Route, RideInstant -> RideInstant next = |route, instant| { stage_before = RideInstant.encounter_stage(route, instant) rider = instant.rider.rider_at_next_step({ route, encounter_stage: stage_before }) clock = instant.clock.next() rider_place = rider.motorcycle.route_place truck = TruckJourney.truck_progress_at_next_step( instant.truck, { rider_distance: rider_place.distance_along(route), route }, ) segment_change = if rider_place.segment_index == RideInstant.rider_segment_index(instant) { SameSegment } else { NewSegment } encounter_plan = instant.encounter_plan.plan_at_next_step({ segment_change, approach: encounter_approach(rider_place.segment_on(route).encounter, rider.motorcycle), now: clock, }) { rider, truck, clock, encounter_plan } } ## How `motorcycle` comes at `encounter`, or none on a quiet road. encounter_approach : Encounter, Motorcycle -> EncounterPlan.Approach encounter_approach = |encounter, motorcycle| match encounter.encounter_span() { Ok({ span, planned_along }) => Approaching({ span, gap: planned_along.distance_from(motorcycle.route_place.road_point.along), speed: motorcycle.speed, }) Err(QuietRoad) => QuietRoad }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Rider.roc
html: ## The rider from one step to the next: the motorcycle they ride, which knows ## where on the route it is, and where their eyes are. It is kept from one step ## to the next, one of the four things the ride remembers. import Along import Angle import Animation import Attention import EncounterReaction import Motorcycle import RiderEyes import RiderMind import Route import Segment ## The rider at one step. Nominal, not opaque: other modules read its fields. Rider := { motorcycle : Motorcycle, eyes : RiderEyes }.{ initial : Rider initial = { motorcycle: Motorcycle.initial, eyes: RiderEyes.initial } ## The rider a step on along `route`, with the encounter on their segment at ## `encounter_stage`: the move, the crossing onto the next segment, the stop ## at the route's end, and then where the rider looks. rider_at_next_step : Rider, { route : Route, encounter_stage : Animation.Stage } -> Rider rider_at_next_step = |rider, { route, encounter_stage }| { segment = rider.motorcycle.route_place.segment_on(route) moved = rider.motorcycle.motorcycle_at_next_step( RiderMind.controls(rider.motorcycle, { segment, encounter_stage }), ) motorcycle = match segment.segment_ending() { Bends({ bend, .. }) => moved.cross_bend_if_on_road(bend) RouteEnds => stop_at_route_end(moved, segment) } gaze_target = RiderMind.gaze_target(motorcycle, motorcycle.route_place.segment_on(route)) { motorcycle, eyes: rider.eyes.eyes_at_next_step(gaze_target) } } ## Whether the rider has reached the end of the route. is_finished : Rider, Route -> Bool is_finished = |rider, route| { segment = rider.motorcycle.route_place.segment_on(route) match segment.segment_ending() { Bends(_) => False RouteEnds => match route_end_arrival(rider.motorcycle, segment) { AtEnd(_) => True ShortOfEnd => False } } } ## How strongly something holds the rider's eye on their segment of `route`, ## with its encounter at `encounter_stage`: the stronger of what the ## encounter asks and what the rider's own look holds. attention : Rider, { route : Route, encounter_stage : Animation.Stage } -> Attention attention = |rider, { route, encounter_stage }| { encounter = rider.motorcycle.route_place.segment_on(route).encounter EncounterReaction.encounter_attention(encounter, encounter_stage) .max(rider.eyes.attention()) } ## How far the rider's head turns from the way the motorcycle points: the ## gaze, and a little more with the lean, as a rider's head turns into a bend. head_yaw : Rider -> Angle.Turn head_yaw = |rider| rider.eyes.gaze_yaw.plus(rider.motorcycle.lean.steer(head_turn_per_lean)) } ## How far the head turns for each radian of lean. head_turn_per_lean : F64 head_turn_per_lean = 0.15 ## The motorcycle held at the route's end once it reaches it. The throttle ## brakes it to rest there, and this catches the last step's overrun. stop_at_route_end : Motorcycle, Segment -> Motorcycle stop_at_route_end = |moved, segment| match route_end_arrival(moved, segment) { AtEnd(route_end) => moved.stopped_at(route_end) ShortOfEnd => moved } ## Whether `motorcycle` has reached the route's end on `segment`, the route's ## last, and where on the segment that end is. route_end_arrival : Motorcycle, Segment -> [AtEnd(Along), ShortOfEnd] route_end_arrival = |motorcycle, segment| { route_end = Along.at(segment.length) if motorcycle.has_reached(route_end) { AtEnd(route_end) } else { ShortOfEnd } } # With no lean, the head turns from the way the motorcycle points exactly as # far as the rider looks. expect { gaze_yaw = Angle.Turn.radians(0.375) upright = { ..Rider.initial.motorcycle, lean: Angle.Lean.radians(0.0) } eyes = { ..Rider.initial.eyes, gaze_yaw } looking = { ..Rider.initial, motorcycle: upright, eyes } looking.head_yaw() == gaze_yaw }

name: canvas_apps/safari/RiderCamera.roc
html: ## The camera the ride is seen through at one instant, worked out each frame ## from the rider, the route, the encounter plan and the clock: where it stands, ## which way it faces, its lens, and its roll. ## It turns with the rider's gaze, and a little with the motorcycle's lean, as a ## rider's head turns into a bend. import Angle import Animation import Attention import lib.Fraction import Geom import Lens import Pipeline import lib.Pixels import Rider import Route import RoutePlace ## Where the camera stands, which way it faces, its lens and its roll. It is ## nominal, not opaque: other modules read its fields. RiderCamera := { ## Where the camera stands on the route, which is where the rider is. route_place : RoutePlace, ## Which way the camera faces, as a turn from its segment's axis. yaw : Angle.Turn, ## The lens's focal length. focal_length : Pixels, ## The roll the camera is held at: the whole frame turns by minus this about ## the screen's centre. roll : Angle.Lean, }.{ ## The camera for `rider` on `route`, with the encounter on their segment at ## `encounter_stage`. of : Rider, { route : Route, encounter_stage : Animation.Stage } -> RiderCamera of = |rider, { route, encounter_stage }| { route_place: rider.motorcycle.route_place, yaw: rider.motorcycle.yaw.plus(rider.head_yaw()), focal_length: ride_focal_length(rider, { route, encounter_stage }), roll: rider_roll(rider.motorcycle.lean), } ## Where this camera points in the world on `route`, and its lens, as the sun ## and the skyline take them. Its heading is the bearing its segment sets off ## on, turned by its yaw. aim : RiderCamera, Route -> { heading : Angle.Bearing, focal_length : Pixels } aim = |camera, route| { heading: route.bearing_of(camera.route_place.segment_index).plus(camera.yaw), focal_length: camera.focal_length, } ## Where this camera stands on its segment, and which way it faces, as the ## projection onto the screen takes them. vantage : RiderCamera -> Geom.Vantage vantage = |camera| { along: camera.route_place.road_point.along, across: camera.route_place.road_point.across, yaw: camera.yaw, } ## This camera as a sighting takes it: its vantage and its lens. sighting_camera : RiderCamera -> Pipeline.SightingCamera sighting_camera = |camera| { vantage: camera.vantage(), focal_length: camera.focal_length } } ## The lean that widens the view all it can. Nothing holds the bike to it: ## a deeper lean just widens the view no further. full_lean : Angle.Lean full_lean = Angle.Lean.degrees(20.0) ## A lean smaller than this leaves the canvas level. roll_deadband : Angle.Lean roll_deadband = Angle.Lean.radians(0.001) ## How far the canvas rolls with the rider's `lean`: not at all inside the ## deadband, and with the lean past it. rider_roll : Angle.Lean -> Angle.Lean rider_roll = |lean| if lean.abs() < roll_deadband { Angle.upright } else { lean } ## The camera's focal length for where the rider is and how they ride. The ## view widens as the rider leans, and as the rider's attention is caught, by ## an encounter on the road or by a look to the side. ride_focal_length : Rider, { route : Route, encounter_stage : Animation.Stage } -> Pixels ride_focal_length = |rider, { route, encounter_stage }| { attention = rider.attention({ route, encounter_stage }) focal_length_for({ lean: rider.motorcycle.lean, attention }) } ## The focal length the camera uses: the shorter of the two, which ## gives the wider view. A lean to either side widens it alike. focal_length_for : { lean : Angle.Lean, attention : Attention } -> Pixels focal_length_for = |{ lean, attention }| { lean_fraction = Fraction.clamp(lean.abs().ratio_to(full_lean)) for_lean = focal_length_for_lean(lean_fraction) for_attention = focal_length_for_attention(attention) if for_lean < for_attention { for_lean } else { for_attention } } ## How much of the resting focal length is left at `full_lean`. focal_length_share_at_full_lean : Fraction focal_length_share_at_full_lean = Fraction.of(0.35) ## How much of the resting focal length is left at an attention of 1. It is no ## minimum, because a cat in the road holds the eye harder than that. focal_length_share_at_full_attention : Fraction focal_length_share_at_full_attention = Fraction.of(0.61) ## The focal length for a lean, from 0 (upright) to 1 (`full_lean`). focal_length_for_lean : Fraction -> Pixels focal_length_for_lean = |lean_fraction| { lean = lean_fraction.to_f64() lost_at_full_lean = focal_length_share_at_full_lean.complement().to_f64() Lens.resting_focal_length.times(1.0 - lost_at_full_lean * lean * lean) } ## The focal length for the rider's attention. The length shrinks as the ## attention grows and reaches zero at an attention of about 2.56, the lens's ## limit; past it the lens has no length, so this crashes rather than draw ## through it. focal_length_for_attention : Attention -> Pixels focal_length_for_attention = |attention| { lost_at_full_attention = focal_length_share_at_full_attention.complement().to_f64() share_left = 1.0 - lost_at_full_attention * attention.to_f64() focal_length = Lens.resting_focal_length.times(share_left) if focal_length > Pixels.zero { focal_length } else { crash "RiderCamera.focal_length_for_attention: the attention is past the lens's limit, so the focal length is not positive" } } ## Whether `got` is within 1e-9 of `want`, scaled up by a want past 1. is_close : F64, F64 -> Bool is_close = |got, want| (got - want).abs() <= 0.000000001 * want.abs().max(1.0) expect [ (0.0, 685.5110432362151), (0.25, 657.6621571047439), (0.5, 574.1154987103301), (0.75, 434.8710680529739), (1.0, 239.92886513267527), ].all(|(lean, want)| is_close(focal_length_for_lean(Fraction.of(lean)).to_f64(), want)) expect [ (0.0, 685.5110432362151), (0.5, 551.8363898051531), (1.0, 418.16173637409116), (1.5, 284.4870829430293), ].all( |(strength, want)| { got = focal_length_for_attention(Attention.of(strength)).to_f64() is_close(got, want) }, ) # The lens holds a positive length at a crossing cat's peak attention, 1.8, and # just short of its limit, where the length is down to about a pixel. expect { at_peak = focal_length_for_attention(Attention.of(1.8)).to_f64() near_limit = focal_length_for_attention(Attention.of(2.56)).to_f64() at_peak > 0.0 and is_close(at_peak, 204.2822908843921) and near_limit > 0.0 and is_close(near_limit, 1.0968176691779442) } expect [ ((0.0, 0.0), 685.5110432362151), ((1.0, 0.0), 239.92886513267527), ((0.0, 1.0), 418.16173637409116), ((0.5, 0.3), 574.1154987103301), ((0.9, 1.4), 311.2220136292417), ((0.6, 0.5), 525.1014591189407), ].all( |((lean, strength), want)| { got = focal_length_for({ lean: Angle.Lean.degrees(lean * 20.0), attention: Attention.of(strength), }) is_close(got.to_f64(), want) }, ) ## The focal length for `lean`, with nothing holding the rider's eye. focal_length_at_lean : Angle.Lean -> Pixels focal_length_at_lean = |lean| focal_length_for({ lean, attention: Attention.none }) ## The full lean, to the left. full_left_lean : Angle.Lean full_left_lean = Angle.Lean.radians(-full_lean.to_radians()) # The view widens as the rider leans, either way, and widest at the full lean. expect { half = Angle.upright.halfway_to(full_lean) focal_length_at_lean(half) < focal_length_at_lean(Angle.upright) and focal_length_at_lean(full_lean) < focal_length_at_lean(half) and focal_length_at_lean(full_left_lean) < focal_length_at_lean(Angle.upright) and focal_length_at_lean(Angle.upright) <= Lens.resting_focal_length } # A lean past the full one widens the view no further. expect focal_length_at_lean(full_lean) == focal_length_at_lean(full_left_lean) expect { twice = Angle.Lean.radians(2.0 * full_lean.to_radians()) ten_times = Angle.Lean.radians(10.0 * full_lean.to_radians()) at_full_lean = focal_length_at_lean(full_lean) focal_length_at_lean(twice).minus(at_full_lean) == Pixels.zero and focal_length_at_lean(ten_times).minus(at_full_lean) == Pixels.zero } # A full lean and the attention of a hard look together widen the view as far # as the wider of the two alone, and no further. expect { hard_look = Attention.from_fraction(Fraction.whole) both = focal_length_for({ lean: full_lean, attention: hard_look }) looking = focal_length_for({ lean: Angle.upright, attention: hard_look }) wider = focal_length_at_lean(full_lean).to_f64().min(looking.to_f64()) both.to_f64().to_bits() == wider.to_bits() } # Inside the deadband the canvas stays level; at its edge and past it, either # way, the canvas rolls with the rider. expect [ (0.0, 0.0), (0.00001, 0.0), (0.0005, 0.0), (-0.0005, 0.0), (0.0009999, 0.0), (0.001, 0.001), (-0.001, -0.001), (0.002, 0.002), (-0.002, -0.002), (0.35, 0.35), (-0.42, -0.42), ].all(|(lean, roll)| rider_roll(Angle.Lean.radians(lean)).to_radians() == roll)

name: canvas_apps/safari/RiderEyes.roc
html: ## Where the rider's eyes are: the look away from the way the motorcycle ## points, and how far into a look the rider has gone. They are kept from one ## step to the next, as part of the `Rider`. import Angle import Attention import Easing import lib.Fraction import Gaze ## The rider's eyes at one step. `gaze_yaw` is the look away from the way the ## motorcycle points, and `look_depth` how far into a look the rider has gone, ## which outlasts the look. Nominal, not opaque: other modules read its fields. RiderEyes := { gaze_yaw : Angle.Turn, look_depth : Fraction }.{ initial : RiderEyes initial = { gaze_yaw: Angle.straight_ahead, look_depth: Fraction.zero } ## These eyes moved on a step toward `target`: the gaze, and the look depth ## it leaves. eyes_at_next_step : RiderEyes, Gaze.GazeTarget -> RiderEyes eyes_at_next_step = |eyes, target| { gaze_yaw = next_gaze_yaw(eyes, target) { gaze_yaw, look_depth: next_look_depth(eyes, gaze_yaw) } } ## How strongly the depth of these eyes' look holds the rider's eye. The ## easing keeps a shallow look from widening the view much. attention : RiderEyes -> Attention attention = |eyes| Attention.from_fraction(Easing.smoothstep(eyes.look_depth)) is_eq : _ } ## The most the gaze swivels toward a pig in one step. look_swivel_rate : Angle.Turn look_swivel_rate = Angle.Turn.degrees(4.0) ## How far the gaze turns back toward the road in one step. A gaze nearer ## the road than this goes all the way there, so a return ends by itself. look_return_rate : Angle.Turn look_return_rate = Angle.Turn.degrees(0.2) ## How much look depth fades in one step. It is subtracted from the depth, ## and is no share of it, so the fade runs at one rate all the way down. look_depth_decay : Fraction look_depth_decay = Fraction.of(0.0012) ## The gaze one step on. It swivels toward a pig by at most the swivel rate. ## With only the road to look at, it turns back by the return rate, and the ## last step lands it straight ahead. next_gaze_yaw : RiderEyes, Gaze.GazeTarget -> Angle.Turn next_gaze_yaw = |eyes, target| { gaze = eyes.gaze_yaw match target { OnPig(turn) => gaze.plus(turn.minus(gaze).clamped_within(look_swivel_rate)) OnRoad => gaze.minus(gaze.clamped_within(look_return_rate)) } } ## The rider's look depth after the gaze moves to `gaze_yaw`. It rises with ## how far the gaze has turned, and it holds while the gaze is off straight ## ahead by any amount, so it holds all through the return. It fades only ## once the return has put the gaze exactly straight ahead. next_look_depth : RiderEyes, Angle.Turn -> Fraction next_look_depth = |eyes, gaze_yaw| if gaze_yaw == Angle.straight_ahead { Fraction.clamp(eyes.look_depth.to_f64() - look_depth_decay.to_f64()) } else { eyes.look_depth.max(Fraction.clamp(gaze_yaw.abs().ratio_to(Gaze.look_release_angle))) } ## Radians in `d` degrees. radians_of_degrees : F64 -> F64 radians_of_degrees = |d| Angle.Turn.degrees(d).to_radians() ## Eyes looking `gaze_yaw` from straight ahead. head : F64 -> RiderEyes head = |gaze_yaw| { ..RiderEyes.initial, gaze_yaw: Angle.Turn.radians(gaze_yaw) } ## The gaze one step after `eyes`, wanting a pig `want` radians off. gaze_after : RiderEyes, F64 -> F64 gaze_after = |eyes, want| next_gaze_yaw(eyes, OnPig(Angle.Turn.radians(want))).to_radians() ## The gaze one step after `eyes`, with only the road to look at. gaze_returning : RiderEyes -> F64 gaze_returning = |eyes| next_gaze_yaw(eyes, OnRoad).to_radians() ## The look depth after the gaze moves to `gaze` radians. depth_after : RiderEyes, F64 -> F64 depth_after = |eyes, gaze| next_look_depth(eyes, Angle.Turn.radians(gaze)).to_f64() swivel_rate : F64 swivel_rate = look_swivel_rate.to_radians() return_rate : F64 return_rate = look_return_rate.to_radians() expect gaze_after(head(0.0), 1.0) - swivel_rate == 0.0 expect gaze_after(head(0.0), -1.0) + swivel_rate == 0.0 expect gaze_after(head(0.0), swivel_rate / 2.0) - swivel_rate / 2.0 == 0.0 # Each is within 1e-12 of its want, in degrees. A far gaze and a near one move # back by the same return rate. expect [ (30.0, 29.8), (-30.0, -29.8), (2.0, 1.8), (-2.0, -1.8), ].all( |(from, to)| { returned = gaze_returning(head(radians_of_degrees(from))) (returned / radians_of_degrees(1.0) - to).abs() <= 0.000000000001 }, ) # A gaze within the return rate comes all the way home, exactly, and one just # past it doesn't. expect gaze_returning(head(return_rate)) == 0.0 expect gaze_returning(head(-return_rate)) == 0.0 expect gaze_returning(head(return_rate / 2.0)) == 0.0 expect gaze_returning(head(return_rate * 1.5)) > 0.0 expect gaze_returning(head(-return_rate * 1.5)) < 0.0 expect gaze_returning(head(0.0)) == 0.0 # A pig dead ahead is still a pig: the gaze swivels to it, and doesn't ease. expect gaze_after(head(radians_of_degrees(2.0)), 0.0) == 0.0 ## Eyes `look_depth` into a look, looking `gaze_radians` from straight ahead. eyes_at_depth : { look_depth : Fraction, gaze_radians : F64 } -> RiderEyes eyes_at_depth = |{ look_depth, gaze_radians }| { ..head(gaze_radians), look_depth } expect { wide_gaze = radians_of_degrees(20.0) small_gaze = radians_of_degrees(1.0) fresh_eyes = eyes_at_depth({ look_depth: Fraction.zero, gaze_radians: wide_gaze }) deep_eyes = eyes_at_depth({ look_depth: Fraction.of(0.9), gaze_radians: small_gaze }) rising = depth_after(fresh_eyes, wide_gaze) held = depth_after(deep_eyes, small_gaze) easing = depth_after(eyes_ahead_at_depth(0.9), 0.0) rising > 0.0 and held >= 0.9 and easing < 0.9 and easing > 0.0 } ## Eyes this deep into a look, looking straight ahead. eyes_ahead_at_depth : F64 -> RiderEyes eyes_ahead_at_depth = |depth| eyes_at_depth({ look_depth: Fraction.of(depth), gaze_radians: 0.0 }) # The depth holds until the gaze is exactly straight ahead, and fades from there. expect depth_after(eyes_ahead_at_depth(0.9), return_rate / 10.0) == 0.9 expect (depth_after(eyes_ahead_at_depth(0.9), 0.0) - 0.8988).abs() <= 0.000000000001 expect eyes_ahead_at_depth(0.25).attention().to_f64() == 0.15625 expect depth_after(eyes_ahead_at_depth(0.0), 0.0) == 0.0 expect { right_angle = radians_of_degrees(90.0) eyes = eyes_at_depth({ look_depth: Fraction.zero, gaze_radians: right_angle }) depth_after(eyes, right_angle) == 1.0 }

name: canvas_apps/safari/RiderMind.roc
html: ## The rider's mind: every decision the rider makes in a step. It chooses how ## far to lean, how hard to accelerate and where to look. Motorcycle and ## RiderEyes hold the dynamics, which carry those choices out. import Animation import Gaze import LeanSearch import Motorcycle import Segment import Throttle RiderMind :: [].{ ## The lean toward the best line, and the acceleration the throttle gives ## the motorcycle once it leans so, on `segment`, the one it is on, with the ## segment's encounter at `encounter_stage`. controls : Motorcycle, { segment : Segment, encounter_stage : Animation.Stage, } -> Motorcycle.Controls controls = |motorcycle, situation| { lean = LeanSearch.best_lean(motorcycle) { lean, acceleration: Throttle.next_acceleration(motorcycle.with_lean(lean), situation) } } ## Where the rider wants to look from `motorcycle`, on `segment`, the one ## it is on. gaze_target : Motorcycle, Segment -> Gaze.GazeTarget gaze_target = |motorcycle, segment| Gaze.desired_gaze(motorcycle, segment) }

name: canvas_apps/safari/RiderView.roc
html: ## A point in the rider's view is measured from the rider: metres to the right, ## metres forward, and metres up where height matters. It is on the rider's level ## or at a height, and anywhere or at or past the near plane, the closest thing the ## camera can see; only a point past the near plane can go on the screen. This ## module cuts lines and polygons at the near plane. import Distance import lib.Fraction RiderView :: [].{ ## A point on the ground in the rider's view. Both parts are signed: a ## negative `right` is to the rider's left, and a negative `forward` is ## behind the rider. RiderPoint : { right : Distance, forward : Distance } ## How far apart two points on the ground are, along the ground. ground_distance : { from : RiderView.RiderPoint, to : RiderView.RiderPoint } -> Distance ground_distance = |{ from, to }| { rightward = to.right.minus(from.right).to_metres() forward = to.forward.minus(from.forward).to_metres() Distance.metres((rightward * rightward + forward * forward).sqrt()) } ## A point in the rider's view, at a height above the level of the rider. ## All three parts are signed: `right` and `forward` as on a `RiderPoint`, ## and a negative `height` is below that level, where the ground curves ## away. PointAtHeight : { right : Distance, forward : Distance, height : Distance, } ## A point in the rider's view at or past the near plane, so the camera can ## put it on the screen. Only `point_at_height_ahead`, the near-plane cut, and raising ## a point already in view build one. PointAtHeightAhead :: RiderView.PointAtHeight.{ right : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead -> Distance right = |RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.(point)| point.right forward : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead -> Distance forward = |RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.(point)| point.forward height : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead -> Distance height = |RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.(point)| point.height to_point_at_height : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead -> RiderView.PointAtHeight to_point_at_height = |RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.(point)| point ## The point at `height` instead. It is as far ahead, so still in view. at_height : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead, Distance -> RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead at_height = |RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.(point), new_height| RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.({ ..point, height: new_height }) ## The point at `right` instead. It is as far ahead, so still in view. at_right : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead, Distance -> RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead at_right = |RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.(point), new_right| RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.({ ..point, right: new_right }) is_eq : _ } ## `point`, if it is at or past the near plane. point_at_height_ahead : RiderView.PointAtHeight -> Try( RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead, [BehindCamera], ) point_at_height_ahead = |point| if is_in_view(point.forward) { Ok(RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.(point)) } else { Err(BehindCamera) } ## A point on the rider's level at or past the near plane, such as where an ## object stands. It has no height, so whatever stands above it says how ## high with `at_height`. Only `rider_point_ahead` builds one. RiderPointAhead :: RiderView.RiderPoint.{ right : RiderView.RiderPointAhead -> Distance right = |RiderView.RiderPointAhead.(point)| point.right forward : RiderView.RiderPointAhead -> Distance forward = |RiderView.RiderPointAhead.(point)| point.forward to_rider : RiderView.RiderPointAhead -> RiderView.RiderPoint to_rider = |RiderView.RiderPointAhead.(point)| point ## The point raised to `height`. It is as far ahead, so still in view. at_height : RiderView.RiderPointAhead, Distance -> RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead at_height = |RiderView.RiderPointAhead.(point), height| RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.({ right: point.right, forward: point.forward, height }) is_eq : _ } ## `point`, if it is at or past the near plane. rider_point_ahead : RiderView.RiderPoint -> Try(RiderView.RiderPointAhead, [BehindCamera]) rider_point_ahead = |point| if is_in_view(point.forward) { Ok(RiderView.RiderPointAhead.(point)) } else { Err(BehindCamera) } ## Every one of `points`, in order, if all of them are at or past the near ## plane. points_at_height_ahead : List(RiderView.PointAtHeight) -> Try( List(RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead), [BehindCamera], ) points_at_height_ahead = |points| points.fold( Ok(List.with_capacity(points.len())), |kept, point| { ahead = RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(point)? Ok(kept?.append(ahead)) }, ) ## The part of the line from `from` to `to` at or past the near plane: the ## whole line, or the line cut where it crosses the near plane. A line ## with both ends behind the near plane has no such part. line_ahead : { from : RiderView.PointAtHeight, to : RiderView.PointAtHeight } -> Try( { from : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead, to : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead }, [BehindCamera], ) line_ahead = |{ from, to }| match (RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(from), RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(to)) { (Ok(start), Ok(end)) => Ok({ from: start, to: end }) (Ok(start), Err(BehindCamera)) => Ok({ from: start, to: near_plane_crossing({ from, to }) }) (Err(BehindCamera), Ok(end)) => Ok({ from: near_plane_crossing({ from, to }), to: end }) (Err(BehindCamera), Err(BehindCamera)) => Err(BehindCamera) } ## A region of the rider's view that a polygon can be cut to: which of its ## corners lie in the region, and where its edges cross the boundary. Region(point) : { ## `corner` as a point of the cut polygon, if it lies in the region. corner_in_region : RiderView.PointAtHeight -> Try(point, [Outside]), ## Where the edge from `from` to `to` crosses the region's boundary, ## strictly between its ends, nearest `from` first. edge_crossings : { from : RiderView.PointAtHeight, to : RiderView.PointAtHeight, } -> List(point), } ## The polygon cut to what lies in `region`. Where an edge leaves the ## region and another comes back into it, a straight line joins them. points_in_region : List(RiderView.PointAtHeight), RiderView.Region(point) -> List(point) points_in_region = |polygon_points, region| { next_corners = polygon_points.drop_first(1).concat(polygon_points.take_first(1)) edges = polygon_points.map2(next_corners, |from, to| { from, to, region }) edges.fold(List.with_capacity(2 * polygon_points.len()), edge_points_onto) } ## The polygon cut to what lies at or past the near plane. clipped_points : List(RiderView.PointAtHeight) -> List(RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead) clipped_points = |polygon_points| RiderView.points_in_region(polygon_points, near_plane_region) ## The point `fraction` of the way from `from` to `to`. point_between : { from : RiderView.PointAtHeight, to : RiderView.PointAtHeight, fraction : Fraction, } -> RiderView.PointAtHeight point_between = |{ from, to, fraction }| { right: from.right.plus(to.right.minus(from.right).scaled_by(fraction)), forward: from.forward.plus(to.forward.minus(from.forward).scaled_by(fraction)), height: from.height.plus(to.height.minus(from.height).scaled_by(fraction)), } } ## The closest distance ahead that the camera can see. near_plane : Distance near_plane = Distance.metres(0.4) ## Whether a point `forward` of the camera is at or past the near plane, ## where the camera can see it. is_in_view : Distance -> Bool is_in_view = |forward| forward >= near_plane ## Where an edge that has one end on each side crosses the near plane. near_plane_crossing : { from : RiderView.PointAtHeight, to : RiderView.PointAtHeight, } -> RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead near_plane_crossing = |{ from, to }| { fraction = Fraction.of(near_plane.minus(from.forward).ratio_to(to.forward.minus(from.forward))) crossing = RiderView.point_between({ from, to, fraction }) RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.({ ..crossing, forward: near_plane }) } ## `kept_points` with what one edge of a polygon adds to it: the edge's first ## corner if that lies in `region`, then each point where the edge crosses the ## region's boundary, in order along the edge. edge_points_onto : List(point), { from : RiderView.PointAtHeight, to : RiderView.PointAtHeight, region : RiderView.Region(point), } -> List(point) edge_points_onto = |kept_points, { from, to, region }| { corner_in_region = region.corner_in_region edge_crossings = region.edge_crossings with_corner = match corner_in_region(from) { Ok(corner) => kept_points.append(corner) Err(Outside) => kept_points } with_corner.concat(edge_crossings({ from, to })) } ## The part of the rider's view at or past the near plane. An edge crosses it ## where its two ends lie on either side of the near plane. near_plane_region : RiderView.Region(RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead) near_plane_region = { corner_in_region: |point| match RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(point) { Ok(ahead) => Ok(ahead) Err(BehindCamera) => Err(Outside) }, edge_crossings: |{ from, to }| if is_in_view(from.forward) == is_in_view(to.forward) { [] } else { [near_plane_crossing({ from, to })] }, } ## A point `forward` metres straight ahead, on the rider's level. straight_ahead : F64 -> RiderView.PointAtHeight straight_ahead = |forward| { right: Distance.zero, forward: Distance.metres(forward), height: Distance.zero, } ## A point 2 m right, 9 m ahead and 1 m up. sample_point : RiderView.PointAtHeight sample_point = { right: Distance.metres(2.0), forward: Distance.metres(9.0), height: Distance.metres(1.0), } # A point past the near plane gives back each of its parts. expect match RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(sample_point) { Ok(point) => [point.right(), point.forward(), point.height()] == [sample_point.right, sample_point.forward, sample_point.height] and point.to_point_at_height() == sample_point Err(BehindCamera) => False } # A point exactly on the near plane is in view, and one short of it, at the # camera, or behind it is not. expect RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(straight_ahead(0.4)).is_ok() expect RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(straight_ahead(0.41)).is_ok() expect RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(straight_ahead(0.39)) == Err(BehindCamera) expect RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(straight_ahead(0.0)) == Err(BehindCamera) expect RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(straight_ahead(-5.0)) == Err(BehindCamera) # A point on the rider's level is past the near plane as one at a height is, and # gives back each of its parts. expect { on_ground = { right: sample_point.right, forward: sample_point.forward } match RiderView.rider_point_ahead(on_ground) { Ok(point) => [point.right(), point.forward()] == [on_ground.right, on_ground.forward] and point.to_rider() == on_ground Err(BehindCamera) => False } } expect RiderView.rider_point_ahead({ right: Distance.zero, forward: Distance.metres(0.4) }).is_ok() expect { short_of_plane = { right: Distance.zero, forward: Distance.metres(0.39) } RiderView.rider_point_ahead(short_of_plane) == Err(BehindCamera) } # Raising a point on the rider's level keeps where it is and gives it the # height asked for, above or below that level. expect match RiderView.rider_point_ahead({ right: sample_point.right, forward: sample_point.forward, }) { Ok(point) => [Distance.metres(3.0), Distance.zero, Distance.metres(-1.0)].all( |height| point.at_height(height).to_point_at_height() == { ..sample_point, height }, ) Err(BehindCamera) => False } # A list is ahead when every point is, one on the near plane included, and an # empty list is ahead. expect RiderView.points_at_height_ahead([10.0, 0.4, 30.0].map(straight_ahead)).map_ok( |points| points.map(|point| point.forward().to_metres()), ) == Ok([10.0, 0.4, 30.0]) expect RiderView.points_at_height_ahead([10.0, 0.2, 30.0].map(straight_ahead)) == Err(BehindCamera) expect RiderView.points_at_height_ahead([straight_ahead(0.39)]) == Err(BehindCamera) expect RiderView.points_at_height_ahead([]) == Ok([]) # Moving a point past the near plane up or sideways keeps how far ahead it is. expect match RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(sample_point) { Ok(point) => { moved = point.at_height(Distance.metres(3.0)).at_right(Distance.metres(-4.0)) moved.to_point_at_height() == { right: Distance.metres(-4.0), forward: Distance.metres(9.0), height: Distance.metres(3.0), } } Err(BehindCamera) => False } expect near_plane_crossing({ from: { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(0.0), height: Distance.metres(10.0), }, to: { right: Distance.metres(8.0), forward: Distance.metres(0.8), height: Distance.metres(30.0), }, }).to_point_at_height() == { right: Distance.metres(4.0), forward: Distance.metres(0.4), height: Distance.metres(20.0), } ## How far ahead each end of the part of a line straight ahead, from `from` ## metres to `to` metres, lies at or past the near plane. ahead_line_ends : F64, F64 -> Try((F64, F64), [BehindCamera]) ahead_line_ends = |from, to| RiderView.line_ahead({ from: straight_ahead(from), to: straight_ahead(to) }).map_ok( |line| (line.from.forward().to_metres(), line.to.forward().to_metres()), ) # A line wholly past the near plane is whole, one that crosses it is cut there # whichever end is behind, and one wholly behind it has no part ahead. A line # with an end on the near plane is whole. expect ahead_line_ends(10.0, 30.0) == Ok((10.0, 30.0)) expect ahead_line_ends(0.4, 30.0) == Ok((0.4, 30.0)) expect ahead_line_ends(10.0, 0.0) == Ok((10.0, 0.4)) expect ahead_line_ends(0.0, 10.0) == Ok((0.4, 10.0)) expect ahead_line_ends(0.0, 0.39) == Err(BehindCamera) expect ahead_line_ends(-5.0, 0.2) == Err(BehindCamera) expect RiderView.clipped_points([ { right: Distance.metres(-1.0), forward: Distance.metres(2.0), height: Distance.metres(0.0), }, { right: Distance.metres(1.0), forward: Distance.metres(2.0), height: Distance.metres(0.5), }, { right: Distance.metres(1.0), forward: Distance.metres(-1.0), height: Distance.metres(1.0), }, { right: Distance.metres(-1.0), forward: Distance.metres(-1.0), height: Distance.metres(1.5), }, ]).map(RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead.to_point_at_height) == [ { right: Distance.metres(-1.0), forward: Distance.metres(2.0), height: Distance.metres(0.0), }, { right: Distance.metres(1.0), forward: Distance.metres(2.0), height: Distance.metres(0.5), }, { right: Distance.metres(1.0), forward: Distance.metres(0.4), height: Distance.metres(0.7666666666666666), }, { right: Distance.metres(-1.0), forward: Distance.metres(0.4), height: Distance.metres(0.8), }, ] expect RiderView.point_between({ from: { right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(10.0), height: Distance.metres(20.0), }, to: { right: Distance.metres(8.0), forward: Distance.metres(30.0), height: Distance.metres(0.0), }, fraction: Fraction.of(0.25), }) == { right: Distance.metres(2.0), forward: Distance.metres(15.0), height: Distance.metres(15.0), } # Along the ground, whichever way the second point lies from the first. expect [ ({ right: Distance.metres(-1.0), forward: Distance.metres(2.0) }, 5.0), ({ right: Distance.metres(2.0), forward: Distance.metres(6.0) }, 0.0), ].all( |(from, want)| { to = { right: Distance.metres(2.0), forward: Distance.metres(6.0) } RiderView.ground_distance({ from, to }).to_metres() == want }, )

name: canvas_apps/safari/RoadAhead.roc
html: ## RoadAhead finds where the road ahead lies, and where the segment just behind ## the rider lies. The road ahead is the line of segments the rider can see, the ## rider's own first, and a point on any of them, or on the segment just behind, ## is carried back round the bends between to the rider's own segment and into ## the view of a camera standing there. import Angle import Distance import Geom import RiderView import Route import Segment import SegmentFromRider RoadAhead :: [].{ ## The road in view: the route, and the run of its segments ahead of the ## rider. Only `ahead_of` builds one, so a road holds just what a rider on ## its route can see. ## It keeps how many segments lie ahead, the bends between them, and the ## bend from the segment just behind, each worked out once from the route ## by `ahead_of`: the count for every walk along the road ahead, and the ## bends for all the points carried across them. RoadView :: { route : Route, segments_ahead : RoadAhead.SegmentsAhead, bends_ahead : List(Geom.WorkedBend), bend_behind : [Behind(Geom.WorkedBend), AtRouteStart], }.{ ## The road ahead of a rider on the route's segment at `rider_index`: as ## far as the rider can see, or to the route's end. ahead_of : Route, Route.SegmentIndex -> RoadAhead.RoadView ahead_of = |route, rider_index| { segments_ahead = segments_ahead_of(route, rider_index) RoadAhead.RoadView.( { route, segments_ahead, bends_ahead: worked_bends_ahead(route, segments_ahead), bend_behind: worked_bend_behind(route, rider_index), }, ) } ## The route the road is on. route : RoadAhead.RoadView -> Route route = |RoadAhead.RoadView.(road)| road.route ## The segments of the route the road ahead holds. segments_ahead : RoadAhead.RoadView -> RoadAhead.SegmentsAhead segments_ahead = |RoadAhead.RoadView.(road)| road.segments_ahead } ## The segments of the route ahead of the rider: the index of the rider's ## own, which is the first, and how many there are, one after another from ## it. SegmentsAhead : { first_index : Route.SegmentIndex, count : U32 } ## A segment in view: where it is in the route, the segment itself, and where ## it lies from the rider. SegmentInView : { index : Route.SegmentIndex, segment : Segment, from_rider : SegmentFromRider, } ## The segment at `position` on the road ahead. segment_at : RoadAhead.RoadView, SegmentFromRider.Position -> Segment segment_at = |road, position| road.route().segment_at(index_at(road, position)) ## The segments in view: those of the road ahead, the rider's own first, then ## the one just behind the rider, unless the rider's is the route's first. segments_in_view : RoadAhead.RoadView -> List(RoadAhead.SegmentInView) segments_in_view = |road| { segments_ahead = SegmentFromRider.Position.positions_in(road.segments_ahead()) .map(|position| segment_in_view_at(road, position)) match previous_segment_index(road) { Previous(index) => { segment = road.route().segment_at(index) segments_ahead.append({ index, segment, from_rider: JustBehind }) } AtRouteStart => segments_ahead } } ## Where the route's segment at `index` is on the road ahead, or `NotAhead` ## when the road ahead doesn't hold it. position_of : RoadAhead.RoadView, Route.SegmentIndex -> Try(SegmentFromRider.Position, _) position_of = |road, index| { positions = SegmentFromRider.Position.positions_in(road.segments_ahead()) match positions.find_first(|position| index_at(road, position) == index) { Ok(position) => Ok(position) Err(NotFound) => Err(NotAhead) } } ## The segment at `position` on the road ahead, as a segment in view. segment_in_view_at : RoadAhead.RoadView, SegmentFromRider.Position -> RoadAhead.SegmentInView segment_in_view_at = |road, position| { index = index_at(road, position) { index, segment: road.route().segment_at(index), from_rider: Ahead(position), } } ## A point on the segment that lies at `from_rider`, as the camera at ## `vantage` on the rider's segment sees it. rider_point_at : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, from_rider : SegmentFromRider, road_point : Geom.RoadPoint, } -> RiderView.RiderPoint rider_point_at = |road, { vantage, from_rider, road_point }| match from_rider { Ahead(position) => rider_point_round_bends(road, { vantage, position, road_point }) JustBehind => match bend_behind(road) { Behind(bend) => { on_rider_segment = Geom.point_after_worked_bend(road_point, bend) to_rider_point(on_rider_segment, vantage) } AtRouteStart => crash "RoadAhead.rider_point_at: a rider on the route's first segment has no segment behind" } } ## Which way the road runs at `road_point` on the segment that lies at ## `from_rider`, as the camera at `vantage` sees it: zero straight away from ## the camera, positive to the right. A segment comes into the rider's view ## by a turn and a shift, so the road runs the same way all along it, and ## two points a metre apart are enough to find which way that is. road_heading_at : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, from_rider : SegmentFromRider, road_point : Geom.RoadPoint, } -> Angle.Turn road_heading_at = |road, { vantage, from_rider, road_point }| { further_along = { ..road_point, along: road_point.along.plus(Distance.metres(1.0)) } here = RoadAhead.rider_point_at(road, { vantage, from_rider, road_point }) there = RoadAhead.rider_point_at(road, { vantage, from_rider, road_point: further_along }) Angle.Turn.radians( F64.atan2({ x: there.forward.minus(here.forward).to_metres(), y: there.right.minus(here.right).to_metres(), }), ) } } ## The road ahead of a rider on the segment at `start`: as far as the rider can ## see, or to the route's end. segments_ahead_of : Route, Route.SegmentIndex -> RoadAhead.SegmentsAhead segments_ahead_of = |route, start| { left_on_route = route.segment_count() -
