start.count_before() { first_index: start, count: left_on_route.min(most_segments_ahead.to_u64()).to_u32_wrap() } } ## The most segments the road ahead holds. most_segments_ahead : U32 most_segments_ahead = 7 ## The bend out of each segment of the road ahead but its last, the rider's ## own first, worked out. bends_ahead : RoadAhead.RoadView -> List(Geom.WorkedBend) bends_ahead = |RoadAhead.RoadView.(road)| road.bends_ahead ## The bend from the segment just behind the rider into the rider's own, ## worked out, unless the rider's is the route's first. bend_behind : RoadAhead.RoadView -> [Behind(Geom.WorkedBend), AtRouteStart] bend_behind = |RoadAhead.RoadView.(road)| road.bend_behind ## The index of the segment the rider is on, which is the road ahead's first. rider_segment_index : RoadAhead.RoadView -> Route.SegmentIndex rider_segment_index = |road| road.segments_ahead().first_index ## The segment behind the rider's, unless the rider's is the route's first. previous_segment_index : RoadAhead.RoadView -> [Previous(Route.SegmentIndex), AtRouteStart] previous_segment_index = |road| rider_segment_index(road).previous() ## A point on the segment at `position` on the road ahead, carried back round ## each bend between it and the rider's segment, as the camera at `vantage` ## there sees it. rider_point_round_bends : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, position : SegmentFromRider.Position, road_point : Geom.RoadPoint, } -> RiderView.RiderPoint rider_point_round_bends = |road, { vantage, position, road_point }| { bends = bends_ahead(road) var $point = road_point var $bends_left = position.to_u32().to_u64() while $bends_left > 0 { $bends_left = $bends_left - 1 bend = bends.get($bends_left) ?? crash "RoadAhead.rider_point_round_bends: past the road's end" $point = Geom.point_before_worked_bend($point, bend) } to_rider_point($point, vantage) } ## A point on the rider's segment, as the camera at `vantage` sees it. to_rider_point : Geom.RoadPoint, Geom.Vantage -> RiderView.RiderPoint to_rider_point = |{ along, across }, vantage| { ahead = along.distance_from(vantage.along).to_metres() aside = across.distance_from(vantage.across).to_metres() cos_yaw = vantage.yaw.to_radians().cos() sin_yaw = vantage.yaw.to_radians().sin() { forward: Distance.metres(ahead * cos_yaw + aside * sin_yaw), right: Distance.metres((0.0 - ahead) * sin_yaw + aside * cos_yaw), } } ## The route's index of the segment at `position` on the road ahead. index_at : RoadAhead.RoadView, SegmentFromRider.Position -> Route.SegmentIndex index_at = |road, position| { segments_ahead = road.segments_ahead() if position.is_within_first(segments_ahead.count) { Route.SegmentIndex.number(segments_ahead.first_index.to_u32() + position.to_u32()) } else { crash "RoadAhead.index_at: past the road's end" } } ## The bends out of the segments of `segments_ahead` but the last, worked out. worked_bends_ahead : Route, RoadAhead.SegmentsAhead -> List(Geom.WorkedBend) worked_bends_ahead = |route, { first_index, count }| { first = first_index.to_u32() List.from_iter(U32.until(0, count - 1)).map( |n| Geom.worked_bend(route.segment_at(Route.SegmentIndex.number(first + n)).bend_out_of()), ) } ## The bend from the segment behind the one at `rider_index` into it, worked ## out, unless that is the route's first. worked_bend_behind : Route, Route.SegmentIndex -> [Behind(Geom.WorkedBend), AtRouteStart] worked_bend_behind = |route, rider_index| match rider_index.previous() { Previous(index) => Behind(Geom.worked_bend(route.segment_at(index).bend_out_of())) AtRouteStart => AtRouteStart }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Route.roc
html: ## The route is the line of segments the ride follows, in order. Every segment ## but the last bends into the one after it, and the last ends the route, so a ## route can only be built in that shape. A segment's place in the route is its ## `Route.SegmentIndex`. import Along import Angle import Distance import Segment Route :: List(Segment).{ ## A segment's place in the route, counted from 0. It says where a segment ## is in the route, where a SegmentFromRider.Position says how far ahead of the ## rider it is. SegmentIndex :: U32.{ number : U32 -> Route.SegmentIndex number = |n| Route.SegmentIndex.(n) to_u32 : Route.SegmentIndex -> U32 to_u32 = |Route.SegmentIndex.(n)| n ## The route's first segment. first : Route.SegmentIndex first = Route.SegmentIndex.(0) next : Route.SegmentIndex -> Route.SegmentIndex next = |Route.SegmentIndex.(n)| Route.SegmentIndex.(n + 1) ## The segment before this one, unless this is the first. previous : Route.SegmentIndex -> [Previous(Route.SegmentIndex), AtRouteStart] previous = |Route.SegmentIndex.(n)| if n == 0 { AtRouteStart } else { Previous(Route.SegmentIndex.(n - 1)) } ## How many segments come before this one. count_before : Route.SegmentIndex -> U64 count_before = |Route.SegmentIndex.(n)| n.to_u64() ## The segment with `count` segments before it, the inverse of ## `count_before`. from_count_before : U64 -> Route.SegmentIndex from_count_before = |count| Route.SegmentIndex.( count.to_u32_try() ?? crash "Route.SegmentIndex.from_count_before: a route holds fewer than 2^32 segments", ) is_eq : _ } ## The route along `route_segments`, which must have the route's shape: ## every segment but the last bends into the next, and the last ends the ## route. from_segments : List(Segment) -> Route from_segments = |route_segments| { count = route_segments.len() is_in_place = |segment, at| match segment.ending { Bends(_) => at + 1 < count RouteEnds => at + 1 == count } is_route_shaped = route_segments.map_with_index(is_in_place).all(|is_ok| is_ok) if !route_segments.is_empty() and is_route_shaped { Route.(route_segments) } else { crash "Route.from_segments: every segment but the last bends, and the last ends the route" } } ## The route's segments, in order. route_segments : Route -> List(Segment) route_segments = |Route.(segments)| segments ## How many segments the route has. segment_count : Route -> U64 segment_count = |Route.(segments)| segments.len() ## The segment at `index`. segment_at : Route, Route.SegmentIndex -> Segment segment_at = |Route.(segments), index| segments.get(index.count_before()) ?? crash "Route.segment_at: the route has no segment there" ## The route's length, end to end: where its last segment ends. route_length : Route -> Distance route_length = |route| match route.segments_with_ends().last() { Ok(last) => last.end Err(_) => crash "Route.route_length: a route has a segment" } ## How far along the route the point at `along` on the segment at `index` ## is: where the segment before it ends, plus `along`. distance_along_route : Route, { index : Route.SegmentIndex, along : Along } -> Distance distance_along_route = |route, { index, along }| { start = match index.previous() { AtRouteStart => Distance.zero Previous(before) => match route.segments_with_ends().get(before.count_before()) { Ok(stretch) => stretch.end Err(_) => crash "Route.distance_along_route: the route has no segment there" } } start.plus(along.from_start()) } ## Each of the route's segments, in order, with how far along the route it ## ends. It is the one sum of the route's lengths, which every other ## distance along the route reads. The lengths are added from the first ## segment on: a float sum's rounding depends on its order, and another order ## can move a pixel. segments_with_ends : Route -> List({ segment : Segment, end : Distance }) segments_with_ends = |Route.(segments)| segments .fold( { reached: Distance.zero, stretches: [] }, |{ reached, stretches }, segment| { end = reached.plus(segment.length) { reached: end, stretches: stretches.append({ segment, end }) } }, ) .stretches ## The bearing the segment at `index` sets off on: north, turned by the bend ## out of each segment before it. The turns are added from the first segment ## on: a float sum's rounding depends on its order, and another order can ## move a pixel of the sky. bearing_of : Route, Route.SegmentIndex -> Angle.Bearing bearing_of = |Route.(segments), index| segments .take_first(index.count_before()) .fold(Angle.north, |bearing, segment| bearing.plus(segment.bend_out_of().turn)) } # A count of segments before and a segment index are one number, either way. expect [0, 1, 18].all(|n| Route.SegmentIndex.from_count_before(n).count_before() == n)

name: canvas_apps/safari/SafariApp.roc
html: ## SafariApp is the ride as a value the canvas apps can run. It sits between the ## ride and what a runner wants: Tour holds the ride and its history, FrameView ## says what the camera shows, and this module says which keys move it. ## ## The ride plays on its own. Space pauses it. Left steps back through the ride's ## history and Right forward, a frame at a time while paused and faster while it ## runs. J jumps to the next of the route's segments, and R starts the ## ride again. import lib.CanvasApp import lib.Input import FrameView import Screen import Steps import Tour SafariApp :: [].{ Model : { tour : Tour, motion : [Playing, Paused] } canvas_app : CanvasApp.CanvasApp(SafariApp.Model) canvas_app = { size: { width: Screen.width.to_f64(), height: Screen.height.to_f64() }, # The ride's motion is written per step, and thirty steps a second is the # speed it is meant to look like, chosen by eye. frames_a_second: 30, init: initial_model, model_at_next_step: CanvasApp.untimed_model_at_next_step(model_at_next_step), frame_shapes: |m| FrameView.frame_view_at(m.tour.route(), m.tour.instant()).leaned_shapes(), sounds: |_m| 0, tones: [], title: "Safari", } } model_at_next_step : SafariApp.Model, Input.Snapshot -> SafariApp.Model model_at_next_step = |m, input| if input.key_pressed(KeyR) { initial_model } else { motion = if input.key_pressed(KeySpace) { match m.motion { Playing => Paused Paused => Playing } } else { m.motion } steps_a_frame = match motion { Paused => Steps.one_step Playing => Steps.of(4) } moved = if input.key_down(KeyRight) { m.tour.steps_forward(steps_a_frame) } else if input.key_down(KeyLeft) { m.tour.steps_back(steps_a_frame) } else { match motion { Paused => m.tour Playing => m.tour.step_forward() } } tour = if input.key_pressed(KeyJ) { moved.at_next_segment() } else { moved } { tour, motion } } ## The ride at its start, playing. initial_model : SafariApp.Model initial_model = { tour: Tour.initial, motion: Playing }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Scene.roc
html: ## Scene gathers what one frame shows beside the road: the trees, towers, ## billboards, cats, guard rails, the truck and the birds in view, each found by ## its own sighting and rendered as soon as it is found. Past the sighting ## nothing asks what kind a thing is, so each field holds only renderings. A ## scene is worked out each frame from the ride's instant and the route. import Animation import Clock import Distance import EncounterSighting import BillboardSighting import RoadAhead import GuardRail import Pipeline import RailSighting import Rendered import Sky import Sprite import TowerSighting import TreeSighting import Truck import TruckSighting import lib.Shapes ## The things in view, rendered, one field for each sighting that found them. ## It is nominal, not opaque: other modules read its fields, and the frame ## widget builds a scene of some of them to draw a few layers alone. Scene := { trees : List(Rendered), birds : List(Rendered), towers : List(Rendered), billboards : List(Rendered), cats : List(Rendered), trucks : List(Rendered), rails : List(Rendered), }.{ ## What the sightings read beyond the road: where the encounter on the ## rider's segment has got to, where the truck is and how it looks, and the ## clock. The truck's lights are worked out from the clock and the truck's ## pace, and in play `FrameView.ride_facts` is the one builder of these ## facts, so the headlights always agree with `clock`. RideFacts : { encounter_stage : Animation.Stage, truck : { route_position : Distance, lights : Truck }, clock : Clock, } ## Everything `camera` sees of `road`, each thing rendered as it is sighted. scene_in_view : RoadAhead.RoadView, { camera : Pipeline.SightingCamera, facts : Scene.RideFacts, } -> Scene scene_in_view = |road, { camera, facts }| { lens_and_light = { focal_length: camera.focal_length, darkness: Sky.darkness_at(facts.clock), } vantage = camera.vantage encounter = { camera, encounter_stage: facts.encounter_stage } birds_seen = EncounterSighting.birds_in_view(road, encounter) cats_seen = EncounterSighting.cats_in_view(road, encounter) trees_seen = TreeSighting.trees_in_view(road, camera) truck_fate = TruckSighting.truck_in_view(road, { vantage, truck: facts.truck }) { trees: trees_seen.map(|tree| Pipeline.rendering_of(tree, lens_and_light)), birds: birds_seen.map(|bird| Pipeline.rendering_of(bird, lens_and_light)), towers: TowerSighting.towers_in_view(road, { vantage, clock: facts.clock }).map( |tower| Pipeline.rendering_of(tower, lens_and_light), ), billboards: BillboardSighting.billboards_in_view(road, camera).map( |billboard| Pipeline.rendering_of(billboard, lens_and_light), ), cats: cats_seen.map(|cat| Pipeline.rendering_of(cat, lens_and_light)), trucks: truck_renderings(truck_fate, lens_and_light), rails: RailSighting.rail_quads_in_view(road, vantage).keep_oks( |quad| GuardRail.quad_rendering(quad, lens_and_light), ), } } ## The scene's things as shapes, far to near: a list for each thing. scene_shape_lists : Scene -> List(List(Shapes.Shape)) scene_shape_lists = |scene| Scene.scene_renderings(scene).map(|rendering| rendering.sprite().to_shapes()) ## The scene's renderings far to near. The order of the fields they come ## from breaks ties, so the trees go before the birds: a perched bird stands ## at its tree's own depth and is drawn over it. scene_renderings : Scene -> List(Rendered) scene_renderings = |scene| Rendered.depth_sorted_renderings( [ scene.trees, scene.birds, scene.towers, scene.billboards, scene.cats, scene.trucks, scene.rails, ].join(), ) } ## The truck's renderings: one when its sighting kept it, and an empty list ## when it is out of sight. truck_renderings : TruckSighting.TruckFate, Sprite.LensAndLight -> List(Rendered) truck_renderings = |fate, lens_and_light| match fate { Ok(truck) => [Pipeline.rendering_of(truck, lens_and_light)] Err(OutOfSight) => [] }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Screen.roc
html: ## The screen Safari draws on: its size in pixels, and where the horizon ## crosses it before the camera rolls, and the space the frame leans in once it ## does. import Angle import lib.Point import lib.Pixels import lib.Brush import lib.Shapes Screen :: [].{ ## The distance between two points on the screen. distance : { from : Point, to : Point } -> Pixels distance = |{ from, to }| { dx = from.x.minus(to.x).to_f64() dy = from.y.minus(to.y).to_f64() Pixels.of((dx * dx + dy * dy).sqrt()) } ## How far the farthest of `points` is from `center`, or zero for no ## points. farthest_distance : List(Point), Point -> Pixels farthest_distance = |points, center| points.fold_rev( Pixels.zero, |corner, farthest| Screen.distance({ from: corner, to: center }).max(farthest), ) width_px : I64 width_px = 960 height_px : I64 height_px = 600 ## The size again as lengths, for the geometry. width : Pixels width = Pixels.of(width_px.to_f64()) height : Pixels height = Pixels.of(height_px.to_f64()) ## The middle of the screen, halfway across it and halfway down. middle : Point middle = { x: width.divided_by(2.0), y: height.divided_by(2.0) } ## The camera looks at the middle of the screen, across its width. center_x : Pixels center_x = middle.x ## The horizon crosses the screen halfway down, by rule: the camera looks ## level, and a level line of sight lands halfway down the screen. It sits ## at `middle.y` only because of that choice; a camera tilted up or down ## would move it. horizon_y : Pixels horizon_y = height.divided_by(2.0) ## How far past each edge of the screen the backdrop and the skyline reach, ## so the camera's roll never shows their edges. The roll turns the screen ## about its middle, and 200 pixels covers a roll of up to 30° either way. ## Nothing caps the roll, but the ride's leans stay under 18°. It is a whole, ## even number of pixels, so the skyline's columns, two pixels apart from ## this far left, land on the screen's own whole pixels. roll_margin : Pixels roll_margin = Pixels.of(200.0) ## The left edge of what the backdrop and the skyline draw: `roll_margin` ## left of the screen. drawn_left : Pixels drawn_left = roll_margin.opposite() ## The right edge of what the backdrop and the skyline draw: `roll_margin` ## right of the screen. drawn_right : Pixels drawn_right = width.plus(roll_margin) ## A rectangle from `top` down to `bottom`, painted with `fill`, from ## `drawn_left` across to `drawn_right`. margin_rect : { top : Pixels, bottom : Pixels }, Brush.Fill -> Shapes.Shape margin_rect = |{ top, bottom }, fill| Shapes.rectangle({ top_left: { x: drawn_left, y: top }, width: drawn_right.minus(drawn_left), height: bottom.minus(top), fill, }) ## The rectangle above the horizon, painted with `fill`: from `roll_margin` ## above the screen down to the horizon, and `roll_margin` past each side. above_horizon_rect : Brush.Fill -> Shapes.Shape above_horizon_rect = |fill| margin_rect({ top: roll_margin.opposite(), bottom: horizon_y }, fill) ## The space the whole frame is drawn in when the camera rolls by `roll`: ## the screen turns by minus the roll about its middle. leaned_by : Angle.Lean -> Shapes.Space leaned_by = |roll| Shapes.world_space({ target: middle, offset: middle, rotation: 0.0 - roll.to_degrees(), zoom: 1.0, }) } expect Screen.distance({ from: Point.at(3.0, 4.0), to: Point.at(0.0, 0.0) }).to_f64() == 5.0 expect Screen.distance({ from: Point.at(0.0, 0.0), to: Point.at(3.0, 4.0) }).to_f64() == 5.0 expect Screen.distance({ from: Point.at(0.0, 0.0), to: Point.at(0.0, 0.0) }).to_f64() == 0.0 expect Screen.farthest_distance( [ Point.at(3.0, 4.0), Point.at(6.0, 8.0), Point.at(0.0, 0.0), Point.at(7.0, 4.0), ], Point.at(0.0, 0.0), ).to_f64() == 10.0 # At a roll of 30°, the screen's corners turn no further from its middle than # the margin reaches: up and down, and left and right. expect { roll = 30.0 * F64.pi / 180.0 half_width = Screen.width.to_f64() / 2.0 half_height = Screen.height.to_f64() / 2.0 reach_down = half_width * roll.sin() + half_height * roll.cos() reach_across = half_width * roll.cos() + half_height * roll.sin() reach_down <= half_height + Screen.roll_margin.to_f64() and reach_across <= half_width + Screen.roll_margin.to_f64() } # At 31°, the corners would pass the margin up and down. expect { roll = 31.0 * F64.pi / 180.0 half_width = Screen.width.to_f64() / 2.0 half_height = Screen.height.to_f64() / 2.0 half_width * roll.sin() + half_height * roll.cos() > half_height + Screen.roll_margin.to_f64() }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Segment.roc
html: ## A segment is one straight stretch of the route's road, from one bend to the ## next: its length, its trees, its herds, what the rider meets on it, and how ## it ends. It is built once, from choices the route has already made, and this ## module answers the questions asked of one segment: where its herds stand, ## which trees its cat and its bird wait by, where the rider commits to its ## bend, and what on it may catch the rider's eye. ## ## Segment is nominal, not opaque, because many modules read its fields (its ## length, its trees, its herds, its encounter and its ending) and every value ## of them is a valid segment, so there is nothing for a maker to check. import Across import Along import Angle import BendAnimal import Billboard import BirdFlight import CatCrossing import CowHerd import Distance import Encounter import Geom import PigHerd import Pond import Trees Segment := { length : Distance, trees : List(Trees.RoadsideTree), ## The segment's herd of pigs, if it has one, and how the rider takes it. pigs : Segment.Pigs, ## The segment's herd of cows, led by a bull or not. cows : Segment.Cows, ## What the rider meets on the road here. The cat crosses by one of ## `trees`, and the bird's flight holds copies of two of them, its perch and ## the tree it flies to. In play `from_choices` is the one builder of a ## segment, and it picks those trees from `trees`, so the flight's trees ## always stand among them. encounter : Encounter, ending : Segment.Ending, }.{ ## How the rider takes a herd, whatever its shape. PigInterest : [Unnoticed, Distracting] ## A segment's herd of pigs, if it has one, and how the rider takes it. Pigs : [NoPigs, Herd({ herd : PigHerd, interest : Segment.PigInterest })] ## A segment's herd of cows, led by a bull or not. Cows : { herd : CowHerd, bull : CowHerd.Bull } ## What lives at the bend that ends a segment: nothing, a safari animal and ## its baby, or a pond with its ducks. BendLife := [Quiet, Animal(BendAnimal), DuckPond] ## How a segment ends: by turning into the next, positive to the right, ## with what lives at the bend, or by ending the route. Ending : [Bends({ turn : Angle.Turn, bend_life : Segment.BendLife }), RouteEnds] ## How a segment ends, with its bend measured: the segment's `Ending`, its ## turn joined by the segment's length. MeasuredEnding : [Bends({ bend : Geom.Bend, bend_life : Segment.BendLife }), RouteEnds] ## What the route plans for the rider to meet on a segment, before the ## segment's trees say where. PlannedEncounter : [CatCrosses, BirdHere, QuietRoad] ## A segment built from the route's choices for it: its trees are planted ## for its scheme, and what the rider meets on it is placed among them. from_choices : { length : Distance, scheme : Trees.Scheme, pigs : Segment.Pigs, cows : Segment.Cows, encounter : Segment.PlannedEncounter, ending : Segment.Ending, } -> Segment from_choices = |choices| { trees = Trees.roadside_trees({ scheme: choices.scheme, length: choices.length }) { length: choices.length, trees, pigs: choices.pigs, cows: choices.cows, encounter: match choices.encounter { CatCrosses => CatCrosses( CatCrossing.by_tree({ tree: nearest_tree_ahead(trees, cat_along).road_point }), ) BirdHere => { perch = fifth_left_tree(trees) ?? crash "Segment.from_choices: a segment planned with a bird has a tree for it to start on" flight = BirdFlight.flight_from(trees, perch) ?? crash "Segment.from_choices: a segment planned with a bird has a tree for it to fly to" BirdHere(flight) } QuietRoad => QuietRoad }, ending: choices.ending, } } ## The pigs of `segment`'s herd. segment_pigs : Segment -> List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) segment_pigs = |segment| match segment.pigs { Herd({ herd, .. }) => herd.herd_pigs(pig_herd_along(segment.length)) NoPigs => [] } ## The cows of `segment`'s herd, led by its bull if it has one. segment_cows : Segment -> List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) segment_cows = |segment| segment.cows.herd.herd_cows({ herd_along: cow_herd_along, bull: segment.cows.bull }) ## The billboards at the end of `segment`, placed on it: what lives at its ## bend, or nothing at the route's end. segment_bend_billboards : Segment -> List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) segment_bend_billboards = |segment| match segment.segment_ending() { Bends({ bend, bend_life }) => bend_billboards(bend_life, bend) RouteEnds => [] } ## The pig of `segment`'s herd that stands out, and how the rider takes the ## herd. segment_standout_pig : Segment -> [ Standout({ pig : Geom.Placed(Billboard), interest : Segment.PigInterest }), NoPigs, ] segment_standout_pig = |segment| match segment.pigs { Herd({ herd, interest }) => Standout({ pig: herd.standout_pig(pig_herd_along(segment.length)), interest }) NoPigs => NoPigs } ## How `segment` ends: at the bend into the next segment, with what lives ## there, or at the end of the route. segment_ending : Segment -> Segment.MeasuredEnding segment_ending = |segment| match segment.ending { Bends({ turn, bend_life }) => { bend = { segment_length: segment.length, turn } Bends({ bend, bend_life }) } RouteEnds => RouteEnds } ## The bend at the end of `segment`, which some segment follows. bend_out_of : Segment -> Geom.Bend bend_out_of = |segment| match segment.segment_ending() { Bends({ bend, .. }) => bend RouteEnds => crash "Segment.bend_out_of: nothing follows the route's last segment" } ## How far along `segment` a rider on the middle of the road comes onto the ## next segment's road, or the end of the route. commit_along : Segment -> Along commit_along = |segment| match segment.segment_ending() { Bends({ bend, .. }) => Geom.commit_along(bend) RouteEnds => Along.at(segment.length) } ## Whether a segment's pigs draw the rider's eye. has_distracting_pigs : Segment -> Bool has_distracting_pigs = |segment| match segment.pigs { Herd({ interest: Distracting, .. }) => True Herd({ interest: Unnoticed, .. }) | NoPigs => False } } ## The billboards of `bend_life`, placed on the segment that ends at `bend`: ## the animal and its baby, or the ducks on the pond, whose places are measured ## from the bend. bend_billboards : Segment.BendLife, Geom.Bend -> List(Geom.Placed(Billboard)) bend_billboards = |bend_life, bend| match bend_life { Animal(animal) => animal.bend_billboards(bend) DuckPond => Pond.placed_ducks(bend) Quiet => [] } ## How far before the end of its segment a herd of pigs stands. pig_distance_before_end : Distance pig_distance_before_end = Distance.metres(60.0) ## Where the cow herd stands along its segment: the bull's place, with the ## cows behind him. cow_herd_along : Along cow_herd_along = Along.metres(24.0) ## Where a segment's cat starts looking for its tree: it waits by the first ## tree on the right from here on. cat_along : Along cat_along = Along.metres(105.0) ## The nearest tree on the right at or past `along`, which a segment's cat waits ## by. A segment's trees are planted in order along the road, so the first found ## is the nearest. nearest_tree_ahead : List(Trees.RoadsideTree), Along -> Trees.RoadsideTree nearest_tree_ahead = |trees, along| trees.find_first( |{ road_point, .. }| road_point.across > Across.middle and road_point.along >= along, ) ?? crash "Segment.nearest_tree_ahead: a segment with a cat is long enough to have its tree" ## The tree a segment's bird perches on until its flight starts: the fifth on ## the left, with a negative `across`, among `trees`. fifth_left_tree : List(Trees.RoadsideTree) -> Try(Trees.RoadsideTree, [NoPerch]) fifth_left_tree = |trees| { left_trees = trees.keep_if(|tree| tree.road_point.across < Across.middle) left_trees.drop_first(4).first().map_err(|ListWasEmpty| NoPerch) } ## Where a herd of pigs stands on a segment `length` long. pig_herd_along : Distance -> Along pig_herd_along = |length| Along.at(length.minus(pig_distance_before_end)) ## The trees of a gold segment 300 m long, where each pair on the right has one ## tree near the road and one far from it. gold_trees : List(Trees.RoadsideTree) gold_trees = Trees.roadside_trees({ scheme: GoldGreen, length: Distance.metres(300.0) }) # On a gold segment the pairs differ. The tree found is whichever comes next, near # the road or far from it, and never one on the left. expect nearest_tree_ahead(gold_trees, cat_along).road_point.across == Across.metres(3.5) expect nearest_tree_ahead(gold_trees, Along.metres(90.0)).road_point.across == Across.metres(8.0) expect nearest_tree_ahead(gold_trees, Along.metres(90.0)).road_point.along == Along.metres(96.0) expect nearest_tree_ahead(gold_trees, Along.metres(96.0)).road_point.along == Along.metres(96.0) expect nearest_tree_ahead(gold_trees, Along.metres(96.5)).road_point.along == Along.metres(126.0) ## A tree at `along` and `across` metres, of whatever kind a gold segment starts ## with. tree_at : F64, F64 -> Trees.RoadsideTree tree_at = |along, across| { ..(gold_trees.first() ?? crash "Segment.tree_at: a gold segment has trees"), road_point: { along: Along.metres(along), across: Across.metres(across) }, } ## A left and a right tree at each of `alongs`. pairs_at : List(F64) -> List(Trees.RoadsideTree) pairs_at = |alongs| alongs.join_map(|along| [tree_at(along, -6.0), tree_at(along, 6.0)]) ## How far along the fifth left tree of `trees` is, if there is one. fifth_along : List(Trees.RoadsideTree) -> Try(F64, [NoPerch]) fifth_along = |trees| fifth_left_tree(trees).map_ok(|tree| tree.road_point.along.to_metres()) # Only trees on the left count toward the fifth, and a segment too short for five # of them has none. expect fifth_along([]) == Err(NoPerch) expect fifth_along(pairs_at([10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0])) == Err(NoPerch) expect fifth_along(pairs_at([10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0, 50.0])) == Ok(50.0) expect fifth_along(pairs_at([10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0, 50.0, 60.0])) == Ok(50.0) expect fifth_along([50.0, 60.0, 70.0, 80.0, 90.0].map(|along| tree_at(along, 6.0))) == Err(NoPerch) expect { short_trees = Trees.roadside_trees({ scheme: RedGreen, length: Distance.metres(50.0) }) fifth_along(short_trees) == Err(NoPerch) }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Sky.roc
html: ## The sky through the ride: it darkens toward dusk as the sun sinks, and the ## horizon warms red while the sun is near it. Its colors are worked out each ## frame from the clock. import Clock import FarHeight import FarRise import lib.Fraction import lib.ColorShade import Screen import SunPath import lib.Brush import lib.Pixels import lib.RgbColor import lib.Shapes Sky :: [].{ ## The sky's two colors in a frame: at the top of the frame, and at the ## horizon. Colors : { top : RgbColor, horizon : RgbColor } ## How dark the sky is at `clock`, from 0 (day) to 1 (night). darkness_at : Clock -> Fraction darkness_at = |clock| { height = SunPath.height_at(clock) if height >= SunPath.height_when_set { darkness_while_up(height) } else { darkness_after_set(height) } } ## How warm the horizon is at `clock`: most while the sun touches it, none ## once the sun is `warmth_reach` above or below. horizon_warmth_at : Clock -> Fraction horizon_warmth_at = |clock| { from_horizon = SunPath.height_at(clock).minus(FarHeight.zero).abs() Fraction.clamp(from_horizon.ratio_to(warmth_reach)).complement() } ## `color` under a sky `darkness` dark: itself by day, and losing up to ## `night_dim` of its light as night falls. Everything the sky lights, ## from the rock and the grass to the truck, is dimmed here. color_at_darkness : RgbColor, Fraction -> RgbColor color_at_darkness = |color, darkness| ColorShade.shade_color(color, Darkened(night_dim.times(darkness))) ## The sky's two colors at `clock`. colors_at : Clock -> Sky.Colors colors_at = |clock| { top: sky_top_color(clock), horizon: sky_horizon_color(clock) } ## How far down to the horizon the sky holds its top colour before it ## fades to the horizon's. sky_top_stop : Fraction sky_top_stop = Fraction.of(0.2) ## The sky in `colors`: a gradient from the top colour down to the ## horizon's, over the rectangle above the horizon. sky_shape : Sky.Colors -> Shapes.Shape sky_shape = |colors| Screen.above_horizon_rect( Linear({ stops: { start_color: Brush.opaque_rgba(colors.top), end_color: Brush.opaque_rgba(colors.horizon), start_offset: sky_top_stop.to_f64(), end_offset: 1.0, }, start_point: { x: Pixels.zero, y: Pixels.zero }, end_point: { x: Pixels.zero, y: Screen.horizon_y }, }), ) } ## How dark the sky is when the sun has just set: a little over half, so ## the sky goes on darkening after the sun has gone. darkness_at_set : Fraction darkness_at_set = Fraction.of(0.6) ## How far above or below the horizon the sun warms it. Once the sun is ## further away than this, the horizon has the sky's own color. warmth_reach : FarRise warmth_reach = FarRise.of(110.0) ## How much of its light a thing the sky lights loses at full night: half. ## Night then reads as night, and the trees, the truck and the rails stay ## dark shapes on darker ground, under a sky lighter than either. night_dim : Fraction night_dim = Fraction.of(0.5) day_sky : RgbColor day_sky = RgbColor.of(0x8ECAE6) night_sky : RgbColor night_sky = RgbColor.of(0x243A5E) sunset_red : RgbColor sunset_red = RgbColor.of(0xDE5834) ## How far the horizon goes toward sunset red at its warmest, with the sun on ## it: most of the way, so a little of the sky's own color still shows. horizon_warmth_at_most : Fraction horizon_warmth_at_most = Fraction.of(0.85) ## The sky's color at the top of the frame. sky_top_color : Clock -> RgbColor sky_top_color = |clock| ColorShade.color_between({ from: day_sky, to: night_sky, fraction: Sky.darkness_at(clock), }) ## The sky's color at the horizon: the sky warmed toward sunset red. sky_horizon_color : Clock -> RgbColor sky_horizon_color = |clock| ColorShade.color_between({ from: sky_top_color(clock), to: sunset_red, fraction: Sky.horizon_warmth_at(clock).times(horizon_warmth_at_most), }) ## How dark the sky is while the sun, `height` up, is ## still above the line where it has fully set. darkness_while_up : FarHeight -> Fraction darkness_while_up = |height| { whole_fall = SunPath.height_at_start.minus(SunPath.height_when_set) set_so_far = Fraction.of(SunPath.height_at_start.minus(height).ratio_to(whole_fall)) darkness_at_set.times(set_so_far).times(set_so_far) } ## How far below fully set the sun sinks before the sky is full night. night_depth : FarRise night_depth = FarRise.of(46.0) ## How dark the sky is once the sun has fully set, darkening on to full ## night as it sinks a further `night_depth`. darkness_after_set : FarHeight -> Fraction darkness_after_set = |height| { sunk_past_set = SunPath.height_when_set.minus(height).ratio_to(night_depth) Fraction.clamp(darkness_at_set.to_f64() + sunk_past_set * darkness_at_set.complement().to_f64()) } # The sky is at least at darkness_at_set as the sun fully sets, and darker a # step later. A step earlier is in gates/expects/RideExpects.roc, which counts # steps. expect Sky.darkness_at(SunPath.fully_set_at) >= darkness_at_set expect darkness_at_set < Sky.darkness_at(SunPath.fully_set_at.next()) expect Sky.darkness_at(Clock.at_step(0)).to_f64() == 0.0 expect Sky.horizon_warmth_at(Clock.at_step(0)).to_f64() == 0.0 expect Sky.darkness_at(Clock.at_step(6000)).to_f64() == 1.0 expect Sky.horizon_warmth_at(Clock.at_step(6000)).to_f64() == 0.0 # A color is itself by day, half itself at full night, and between at dusk. expect [ (0.0, RgbColor.of(0x4A8F43)), (0.5, RgbColor.of(0x386B32)), (1.0, RgbColor.of(0x254822)), ].all( |(darkness, want)| Sky.color_at_darkness( RgbColor.of(0x4A8F43), Fraction.of(darkness), ) == want, ) # The sky and the horizon at each thousandth step of the ride. expect [ (0, RgbColor.of(0x8ECAE6), RgbColor.of(0x8ECAE6)), (1000, RgbColor.of(0x8DC8E5), RgbColor.of(0x8DC8E5)), (2000, RgbColor.of(0x86BFDB), RgbColor.of(0x86BFDB)), (3000, RgbColor.of(0x73A6C4), RgbColor.of(0x9A898F)), (4000, RgbColor.of(0x517697), RgbColor.of(0x9C6662)), (5000, RgbColor.of(0x243A5E), RgbColor.of(0x243A5E)), (6000, RgbColor.of(0x243A5E), RgbColor.of(0x243A5E)), ].all(|(step, top, horizon)| Sky.colors_at(Clock.at_step(step)) == { top, horizon })

name: canvas_apps/safari/Skyline.roc
html: ## The skyline, the farthest of the ride's shapes and painted first among them, ## over the backdrop's sky, sun and grass: a high range to the north with snow on ## its peaks, a lower range to the west, and the rolling land in front of both. ## Each is a silhouette across the screen whose height depends on the bearing it ## is seen at and on the lens, so the skyline turns with the rider but never comes ## nearer. The rock darkens at dusk, and the snow goes blue. It is worked out ## each frame from the clock and the camera's heading and lens. import lib.Pixels import Angle import FarHeight import FarRise import lib.Fraction import Grass import Lens import lib.ColorShade import Screen import Sky import lib.RgbColor import lib.Brush import lib.Shapes Skyline :: [].{ ## The rolling land: low, and all the way round. It stands 18 pixels high on ## average and rises and falls 12 either side of that, in 0.9 of a wave all ## the way round, a little under one. The 1.9 sets where along the wave north ## falls. Each number was tuned by eye. land_height : Angle.Bearing -> FarHeight land_height = |bearing| FarHeight.of(18.0 + 12.0 * (bearing.turn_from_north().to_radians() * 0.9 + 1.9).sin()) ## The north range's height at `bearing`. north_range_height : Angle.Bearing -> FarHeight north_range_height = |bearing| range_height(north_range, bearing) ## The west range's height at `bearing`. west_range_height : Angle.Bearing -> FarHeight west_range_height = |bearing| range_height(west_range, bearing) ## The skyline, back to front, for a camera facing `heading` through a lens ## of `focal_length`: the west range, the north range, the north's snow, then the ## land. `darkness` is how far the sky has darkened, and the rock and snow ## darken as far. skyline_shapes : { heading : Angle.Bearing, focal_length : Pixels, .. }, { darkness : Fraction, } -> List(Shapes.Shape) skyline_shapes = |aim, { darkness }| { sky_columns = sky_columns_for(aim) snow_shapes = match snow_shape( sky_columns, { focal_length: aim.focal_length, color: snow_color(darkness) }, ) { Ok(snow) => [snow] Err(NoSnow) => [] } [ [ silhouette( sky_columns, { focal_length: aim.focal_length, height_at: |column| Skyline.west_range_height(column.bearing), color: Sky.color_at_darkness(west_rock, darkness), base_y: range_base_y, }, ), silhouette( sky_columns, { focal_length: aim.focal_length, height_at: |column| column.north_height, color: Sky.color_at_darkness(north_rock, darkness), base_y: range_base_y, }, ), ], snow_shapes, [ silhouette( sky_columns, { focal_length: aim.focal_length, height_at: |column| Skyline.land_height(column.bearing), color: Grass.grass_color_at(darkness), base_y: land_base_y, }, ), ], ].join() } } ## A column of the skyline: where it is across the screen, the bearing seen ## there, and the north range's height at that bearing, which the north range's ## silhouette and its snow both need. That height is worked out once per column, ## from its bearing, by `sky_columns_for`, the one builder of a column. SkylineColumn : { x : Pixels, bearing : Angle.Bearing, north_height : FarHeight, } ## The skyline's columns, every `column_step` pixels from `Screen.drawn_left` to ## `Screen.drawn_right`, for a camera facing `heading` through a lens of ## `focal_length`. sky_columns_for : { heading : Angle.Bearing, focal_length : Pixels, .. } -> List(SkylineColumn) sky_columns_for = |aim| columns({ from: Screen.drawn_left, to: Screen.drawn_right }).map( |x| { bearing = bearing_at(aim, x) { x, bearing, north_height: Skyline.north_range_height(bearing) } }, ) north_rock : RgbColor north_rock = RgbColor.of(0x5B6A8F) west_rock : RgbColor west_rock = RgbColor.of(0x39435F) snow_day : RgbColor snow_day = RgbColor.of(0xEEF3F8) snow_night : RgbColor snow_night = RgbColor.of(0x465468) snow_color : Fraction -> RgbColor snow_color = |darkness| ColorShade.color_between({ from: snow_day, to: snow_night, fraction: darkness, }) west_range_bearing : Angle.Bearing west_range_bearing = Angle.Bearing.radians(-2.0416) ## The north range is snowy above this height. snow_threshold : FarHeight snow_threshold = FarHeight.of(124.0) ## How far the snowline dips below the threshold under the highest peak. snow_dip : FarRise snow_dip = FarRise.of(10.0) ## The silhouettes are sampled every `column_step` pixels across the screen. column_step : Pixels column_step = Pixels.of(2.0) ## The height of the north range's highest peak, as its samples across the ## whole range find it. snow_peak_height : FarHeight snow_peak_height = { first = north_range.center.plus(Angle.straight_ahead.minus(north_range.half_width)) last = north_range.center.plus(north_range.half_width) var $highest = Skyline.north_range_height(first) var $at = first.plus(peak_sample_step) while $at <= last { $highest = $highest.max(Skyline.north_range_height($at)) $at = $at.plus(peak_sample_step) } $highest } ## The snowline's height where the north range stands `north_height` high: at ## the threshold, dipping lower under the higher peaks. snowline_under : FarHeight -> FarHeight snowline_under = |north_height| { above_threshold = north_height.minus(snow_threshold) peak_above_threshold = snow_peak_height.minus(snow_threshold) above_fraction = Fraction.clamp(above_threshold.ratio_to(peak_above_threshold)) snow_threshold.lowered_by(snow_dip.scaled_by(above_fraction)) } ## The bearing seen at `x` across the screen. bearing_at : { heading : Angle.Bearing, focal_length : Pixels, .. }, Pixels -> Angle.Bearing bearing_at = |aim, x| aim.heading.plus(Lens.turn_at_x({ x, focal_length: aim.focal_length })) ## A mountain range: the bearing of its middle, how far it reaches either ## side, how far above the horizon it reaches at most, and the two frequencies of the ridges ## along it, broad and fine. Each ridge frequency is how many waves would fit ## a whole turn. MountainRange : { center : Angle.Bearing, half_width : Angle.Turn, height_ceiling : FarRise, broad_ridge_waves : F64, fine_ridge_waves : F64, } north_range : MountainRange north_range = { center: Angle.north, half_width: Angle.Turn.radians(0.95), height_ceiling: FarRise.of(150.0), broad_ridge_waves: 8.0, fine_ridge_waves: 21.0, } west_range : MountainRange west_range = { center: west_range_bearing, half_width: Angle.Turn.radians(0.72), height_ceiling: FarRise.of(120.0), broad_ridge_waves: 11.0, fine_ridge_waves: 27.0, } ## A range's height at `bearing`: under an envelope that is highest in its ## middle and falls to nothing at its ends, with two ridges along it. The ridge ## line sits at 0.6 of the envelope, and the broad ridges rise and fall 0.24 ## either side of it and the fine ones 0.16, so the three add up to the whole ## envelope at most. The fine ridges start a radian along, so the two don't peak ## together in the middle. The shares were tuned by eye. range_height : MountainRange, Angle.Bearing -> FarHeight range_height = |range, bearing| { from_center = bearing.turn_from(range.center) fraction = from_center.ratio_to(range.half_width) if fraction.abs() >= 1.0 { FarHeight.zero } else { envelope = (fraction * F64.pi / 2.0).cos() radians = from_center.to_radians() first_wave = 0.24 * (radians * range.broad_ridge_waves).cos() second_wave = 0.16 * (radians * range.fine_ridge_waves + 1.0).cos() ridge = 0.6 + first_wave + second_wave FarHeight.zero.plus(range.height_ceiling.times(envelope).times(ridge)) } } ## The north range's peak is searched for every hundredth of a radian. peak_sample_step : Angle.Turn peak_sample_step = Angle.Turn.radians(0.01) ## The columns sampled, every `column_step` pixels from `from` up to `to`. columns : { from : Pixels, to : Pixels } -> List(Pixels) columns = |{ from, to }| { var $sampled = [] var $at = from while $at <= to { $sampled = $sampled.append($at) $at = $at.plus(column_step) } $sampled } ## The ranges are seen only above the grass, so they stop where it begins. range_base_y : Pixels range_base_y = Grass.grass_top_y ## The land is in front of the ranges and closes along the horizon. The grass ## begins a pixel above the horizon so that no seam shows under the roll, and ## the land reaches that same pixel past the ranges' foot, for the same reason. land_base_y : Pixels land_base_y = Screen.horizon_y ## A silhouette across the screen, its top at `height_at` each of `sky_columns` ## through a lens of `focal_length`, but never below `base_y`, closed along ## `base_y`. silhouette : List(SkylineColumn), { focal_length : Pixels, height_at : SkylineColumn -> FarHeight, color : RgbColor, base_y : Pixels, } -> Shapes.Shape silhouette = |sky_columns, { focal_length, height_at, color, base_y }| { left = Screen.drawn_left right = Screen.drawn_right crest = sky_columns.map( |column| { top_y = Lens.y_for_height({ height: height_at(column), focal_length }) { x: column.x, y: if top_y > base_y { base_y } else { top_y }, } }, ) Shapes.region_from_corners( crest.concat([{ x: right, y: base_y }, { x: left, y: base_y }]), Brush.flat(color), ) } ## Snow thinner than this, between the range's crest and the snowline, isn't ## drawn. thinnest_snow : FarRise thinnest_snow = FarRise.of(0.01) ## The north range's snow: along its crest where the range is above the ## snowline, then back along the snowline, unless fewer than two of ## `sky_columns` on the screen itself show snow. snow_shape : List(SkylineColumn), { focal_length : Pixels, color : RgbColor } -> Try(Shapes.Shape, [NoSnow]) snow_shape = |sky_columns, { focal_length, color }| { snowy = sky_columns .keep_if(|column| column.x >= Pixels.zero and column.x <= Screen.width) .map( |column| { x: column.x, north_height: column.north_height, snowline_height: snowline_under(column.north_height), }, ) .keep_if(|column| column.north_height > column.snowline_height.plus(thinnest_snow)) if snowy.len() < 2 { Err(NoSnow) } else { crest = snowy.map( |column| { height = column.north_height { x: column.x, y: Lens.y_for_height({ height, focal_length }) } }, ) snowline_points = snowy.fold_rev( [], |column, back| { height = column.snowline_height back.append({ x: column.x, y: Lens.y_for_height({ height, focal_length }) }) }, ) Ok(Shapes.region_from_corners(crest.concat(snowline_points), Brush.flat(color))) } } # The bearing `radians` to the right of north. north_by : F64 -> Angle.Bearing north_by = |radians| Angle.Bearing.radians(radians) # The west range's middle, `radians` to its right. west_by : F64 -> Angle.Bearing west_by = |radians| west_range_bearing.plus(Angle.Turn.radians(radians)) aim_at_rest : { heading : Angle.Bearing, focal_length : Pixels } aim_at_rest = { heading: Angle.north, focal_length: Lens.resting_focal_length } expect Sky.color_at_darkness(north_rock, Fraction.zero) == RgbColor.of(0x5B6A8F) expect Sky.color_at_darkness(west_rock, Fraction.zero) == RgbColor.of(0x39435F) expect Sky.color_at_darkness(north_rock, Fraction.whole) == RgbColor.of(0x2E3548) expect Sky.color_at_darkness(west_rock, Fraction.whole) == RgbColor.of(0x1D2230) expect Sky.color_at_darkness(north_rock, Fraction.of(0.5)) == RgbColor.of(0x44506B) expect snow_color(Fraction.zero) == RgbColor.of(0xEEF3F8) expect snow_color(Fraction.whole) == RgbColor.of(0x465468) expect snow_color(Fraction.of(0.5)) == RgbColor.of(0x9AA4B0) ## A color's brightness: the sum of its three channels, widened first because ## the sum can pass a channel's 255. brightness : RgbColor -> I64 brightness = |color| color.red().to_i64() + color.green().to_i64() + color.blue().to_i64() # The snow stays brighter than the rock it lies on, by day and at dusk. expect [Fraction.zero, Fraction.whole].all( |darkness| { rock = Sky.color_at_darkness(north_rock, darkness) brightness(snow_color(darkness)) > brightness(rock) }, ) expect [0.95, 1.0, 2.0, -0.95, -3.0].all( |radians| Skyline.north_range_height(north_by(radians)) == FarHeight.zero, ) expect [ west_by(0.8), west_by(-0.8), north_by(0.0), north_by(1.5), ].all(|bearing| Skyline.west_range_height(bearing) == FarHeight.zero) expect Skyline.north_range_height(north_by(0.0)) > FarHeight.zero expect Skyline.north_range_height(north_by(0.94)) > FarHeight.zero expect Skyline.north_range_height(north_by(0.0)) > snow_threshold expect !(Skyline.north_range_height(north_by(0.9)) > snow_threshold) expect Skyline.west_range_height(west_range_bearing) > FarHeight.zero expect snowline_under(Skyline.north_range_height(north_by(0.9))) == snow_threshold expect snowline_under(Skyline.north_range_height(north_by(2.0))) == snow_threshold expect snowline_under(Skyline.north_range_height(north_by(0.0))) < snow_threshold expect { deepest_snowline = snow_threshold.lowered_by(snow_dip) snowline_under(Skyline.north_range_height(north_by(0.0))) > deepest_snowline } expect snowline_under(Skyline.north_range_height(north_by(0.5))) <= snow_threshold expect { deepest_snowline = snow_threshold.lowered_by(snow_dip) snowline_under(Skyline.north_range_height(north_by(0.5))) >= deepest_snowline } expect snow_peak_height > snow_threshold # The y of each corner of a silhouette. corner_ys : Shapes.Shape -> List(F64) corner_ys = |shape| match Shapes.region_corners(shape) { Ok(corners) => corners.map(|corner| corner.y.to_f64()) Err(NoCorners) => crash "Skyline: a silhouette has corners" } lowest_y : Shapes.Shape -> F64 lowest_y = |shape| corner_ys(shape).fold(-F64.infinity, |low, y| low.max(y)) highest_y : Shapes.Shape -> F64 highest_y = |shape| corner_ys(shape).fold(F64.infinity, |high, y| high.min(y)) range_silhouette : { heading : Angle.Bearing, focal_length : Pixels } -> Shapes.Shape range_silhouette = |aim| silhouette( sky_columns_for(aim), { focal_length: aim.focal_length, height_at: |column| column.north_height, color: north_rock, base_y: range_base_y, }, ) land_silhouette : { heading : Angle.Bearing, focal_length : Pixels } -> Shapes.Shape land_silhouette = |aim| silhouette( sky_columns_for(aim), { focal_length: aim.focal_length, height_at: |column| Skyline.land_height(column.bearing), color: Grass.grass_color, base_y: land_base_y, }, ) # Facing south, the north range is out of sight: it lies flat along its base, # never below it. expect { south = range_silhouette({ ..aim_at_rest, heading: north_by(3.0) }) lowest_y(south) == range_base_y.to_f64() and highest_y(south) == range_base_y.to_f64() } # Facing north, it stands above its base, and still closes along it. expect { north_view = range_silhouette(aim_at_rest) lowest_y(north_view) == range_base_y.to_f64() and highest_y(north_view) < range_base_y.to_f64() } # The land closes along its own base, below the ranges'. expect lowest_y(land_silhouette(aim_at_rest)) == land_base_y.to_f64() expect highest_y(land_silhouette(aim_at_rest)) < range_base_y.to_f64()

name: canvas_apps/safari/Speed.roc
html: ## Safari's speeds. A speed is how many metres something covers in one step ## of the ride; the rider and the truck each hold one. An `Acceleration` is ## a type of its own, so no speed can be mistaken for one: `accelerated_by` ## takes one, and `acceleration_to` gives one. import Acceleration import Distance import lib.Fraction import Steps Speed :: F64.{ ## A speed of this many metres a step. Nothing in the ride goes backwards, ## so a negative speed means the sum behind it is wrong. metres_a_step : F64 -> Speed metres_a_step = |metres| if metres < 0.0 { crash "Speed.metres_a_step: this speed is below zero, so the sum behind it is wrong" } else { Speed.(metres) } to_metres_a_step : Speed -> F64 to_metres_a_step = |Speed.(s)| s ## Standing still. at_rest : Speed at_rest = Speed.(0.0) ## This speed after `acceleration`, the change over one step, or `BelowRest` ## when that would take it below zero. accelerated_by_try : Speed, Acceleration -> Try(Speed, [BelowRest]) accelerated_by_try = |Speed.(s), acceleration| { after = s + acceleration.to_metres_a_step_each_step() if after < 0.0 { Err(BelowRest) } else { Ok(Speed.(after)) } } ## This speed after `acceleration`, the change over one step. Nothing in the ## ride goes backwards, so a speed below zero means the braking behind it is ## wrong. accelerated_by : Speed, Acceleration -> Speed accelerated_by = |speed, acceleration| Speed.accelerated_by_try(speed, acceleration) ?? crash "Speed.accelerated_by: this acceleration takes the speed below zero, so the braking behind it is wrong" ## The steady acceleration that brings this speed to `target` within this ## distance. acceleration_to : Speed, { target : Speed, within : Distance } -> Acceleration acceleration_to = |Speed.(s), { target: Speed.(t), within }| Acceleration.metres_a_step_each_step((t * t - s * s) / (2.0 * within.to_metres())) times : Speed, F64 -> Speed times = |Speed.(s), factor| Speed.metres_a_step(s * factor) ## This fraction of this speed. scaled_by : Speed, Fraction -> Speed scaled_by = |Speed.(s), fraction| Speed.(s * fraction.to_f64()) ## How far this speed covers in `length`. distance_in : Speed, Steps -> Distance distance_in = |Speed.(s), length| Distance.metres(s * length.to_f64()) ## How many whole steps this speed takes to cover `distance`, a part step ## dropped. Nothing goes backwards, and a speed at rest covers nothing, so ## either means the sum behind it is wrong. steps_to_cover : Speed, Distance -> Steps steps_to_cover = |Speed.(s), distance| { metres = distance.to_metres() if metres < 0.0 { crash "Speed.steps_to_cover: this distance is below zero, so the sum behind it is wrong" } else if s == 0.0 { crash "Speed.steps_to_cover: a speed at rest covers nothing, so the sum behind it is wrong" } else { whole_steps = (metres / s).floor_to_u32_try() ?? crash "Speed.steps_to_cover: more steps than a ride's clock counts" Steps.of(whole_steps) } } ## How far this speed covers in one step. step_length : Speed -> Distance step_length = |Speed.(s)| Distance.metres(s) ## The smaller of this speed and `other`. min : Speed, Speed -> Speed min = |Speed.(s), Speed.(other)| Speed.(s.min(other)) ## The larger of this speed and `other`. max : Speed, Speed -> Speed max = |Speed.(s), Speed.(other)| Speed.(s.max(other)) is_gt : Speed, Speed -> Bool is_gt = |Speed.(s), Speed.(other)| s > other is_lt : Speed, Speed -> Bool is_lt = |Speed.(s), Speed.(other)| s < other is_lte : Speed, Speed -> Bool is_lte = |Speed.(s), Speed.(other)| s <= other is_eq : _ } # Rest is the slowest speed, and still a speed. expect Speed.metres_a_step(0.0) == Speed.at_rest # A part step is dropped: just short of a whole number of steps, at it, and # just past it. expect [ (0.0, 0), (9.9, 7), (10.0, 8), (10.1, 8), ].all( |(metres, steps)| { speed = Speed.metres_a_step(1.25) speed.steps_to_cover(Distance.metres(metres)) == Steps.of(steps) }, ) half_metre_a_step : Speed half_metre_a_step = Speed.metres_a_step(0.5) # Braking to rest exactly, or short of it, is a speed, and a hair harder goes # below rest. expect [ (-0.25, Ok(Speed.metres_a_step(0.25))), (-0.5, Ok(Speed.at_rest)), (-0.5000001, Err(BelowRest)), ].all( |(loss, want)| { acceleration = Acceleration.metres_a_step_each_step(loss) half_metre_a_step.accelerated_by_try(acceleration) == want }, ) # Scaling by nothing is rest, and by a positive factor a speed. expect half_metre_a_step.times(0.0) == Speed.at_rest expect half_metre_a_step.times(3.0) == Speed.metres_a_step(1.5)

name: canvas_apps/safari/Spot.roc
html: ## A Spot is where an object stands in one frame: its height off the ground, ## where its foot is in the rider's view, and which way the road runs there. ## `Pipeline.sighting_of` works one out for each object in view from its place ## on the road, and every sprite is drawn from it. ## ## Every object stands on the road through its spot. A card, which faces the ## camera, stands at its foot (`base`). A solid thing stands each of its points ## with `standing_point`, turned the way it faces against the road. ## ## It has a module of its own because a kind's sprite names it, and Segment ## and Trees, which hold the kinds, sit under RoadAhead and Pipeline. import Angle import Distance import EarthCurve import RiderView Spot :: { lift : Distance, foot : RiderView.RiderPointAhead, road_heading : Angle.Turn, }.{ ## The spot of an object `lift` off the ground, its foot at `foot` in the ## rider's view, where the road runs `road_heading`. A sighting builds each ## spot in play from the road, so the foot and the heading follow from ## where the object stands. A kind's test builds one here, to draw from a ## foot it chooses. at : { lift : Distance, foot : RiderView.RiderPointAhead, road_heading : Angle.Turn, } -> Spot at = |parts| Spot.(parts) ## How high off the ground the object is. lift : Spot -> Distance lift = |Spot.(spot)| spot.lift ## Where the object's foot is in the rider's view, on the rider's level and ## past the near plane. foot : Spot -> RiderView.RiderPointAhead foot = |Spot.(spot)| spot.foot ## Which way the road runs at the spot, seen from the camera: zero straight ## away from it, positive to the right. road_heading : Spot -> Angle.Turn road_heading = |Spot.(spot)| spot.road_heading ## How far the ground has curved away below the rider's level beneath the ## object's foot. Every part of an object is lowered by this one drop: it ## changes by a few centimetres at most across anything we draw, well under ## a pixel, so working it out once per object is enough. drop : Spot -> Distance drop = |spot| EarthCurve.ground_drop(spot.foot().to_rider()) ## The middle of the object's foot, raised as high off the ground as the ## object is, on the ground as it curves away: where an upright object ## stands. base : Spot -> RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead base = |spot| spot.foot().at_height(spot.lift().minus(spot.drop())) ## Where a point of a solid thing standing at the spot lands in the rider's ## view. `offset` is the point in the thing's own frame: how far ahead of ## its foot, how far to the right, and how high above the ground under it. ## `facing` is how the thing is turned against the road: zero along the ## road, positive to the right. The offset is turned by the road's heading ## and the facing, carried out from the foot, raised by the lift, and ## lowered by the ground's drop. standing_point : Spot, { facing : Angle.Turn, offset : { ahead : Distance, rightward : Distance, height : Distance, }, } -> RiderView.PointAtHeight standing_point = |spot, { facing, offset }| { turn = spot.road_heading().plus(facing).to_radians() ahead_metres = offset.ahead.to_metres() rightward_metres = offset.rightward.to_metres() { forward: spot.foot().forward().plus( Distance.metres(ahead_metres * turn.cos() - rightward_metres * turn.sin()), ), right: spot.foot().right().plus( Distance.metres(ahead_metres * turn.sin() + rightward_metres * turn.cos()), ), height: spot.lift().plus(offset.height).minus(spot.drop()), } } }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Sprite.roc
html: ## A Sprite is how one object looks in one frame: the shapes that paint it, ## in order. Outside this module a sprite is a single thing, handed along ## whole until something paints it. import lib.Fraction import lib.Pixels import Spot import lib.Shapes Sprite :: List(Shapes.Shape).{ ## What a kind of object draws its sprite from: where it stands in the ## frame, the camera's focal length, and how dark the sky is. Setting : { spot : Spot, focal_length : Pixels, darkness : Fraction, } ## What every sprite in a frame shares: the camera's focal length, and ## how dark the sky is. A `Setting` adds a thing's own spot to these. LensAndLight : { focal_length : Pixels, darkness : Fraction } from_shapes : List(Shapes.Shape) -> Sprite from_shapes = |shapes| Sprite.(shapes) to_shapes : Sprite -> List(Shapes.Shape) to_shapes = |Sprite.(shapes)| shapes ## One sprite of several, each painted over the ones before it. composite : List(Sprite) -> Sprite composite = |sprites| Sprite.(sprites.join_map(Sprite.to_shapes)) }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Sun.roc
html: ## The sun as the rider sees it: where `SunPath` puts it in the sky lands on ## the screen, and it's drawn only while the rider faces it. It knows its own ## look too, a glow and a disc over it. It is worked out each frame from the ## clock and the camera's heading and lens. import Angle import Clock import FarRise import Lens import lib.ColorShade import lib.Fraction import lib.Point import lib.Pixels import Screen import Sky import SunPath import lib.Brush import lib.RgbColor import lib.Shapes Sun :: [].{ ## Where the sun stands on the screen, the focal length of the lens it is ## seen through, which sizes its glow and disc, and how warm the horizon ## is, which reddens them as the sun nears it. OnScreen : { center : Point, focal_length : Pixels, warmth : Fraction, } ## The sun in a frame: in view at its place, or out of view, too far to ## the side of where the rider faces. Sighting : [InView(Sun.OnScreen), OutOfView] ## The sun's paint where it stands: a wide glow, and over it a disc. Look : { glow : Brush.Fill, disc : Brush.Fill } ## The sun in a frame, for a camera facing `heading` through a lens of ## `focal_length`. It is in view while it is in front of the camera and its glow ## reaches the screen. sun_in_view : { heading : Angle.Bearing, focal_length : Pixels, .. }, Clock -> Sun.Sighting sun_in_view = |camera, clock| { direction = SunPath.sun_direction_at(clock) far_point = Lens.far_point({ turn: direction.bearing.turn_from(camera.heading), height: direction.height, focal_length: camera.focal_length, }) match far_point { Ok(point) => { sun = { center: point, focal_length: camera.focal_length, warmth: Sky.horizon_warmth_at(clock), } if is_glow_on_screen(sun) { InView(sun) } else { OutOfView } } Err(BehindCamera) => OutOfView } } ## How far the glow reaches from the sun's middle where it stands. glow_radius_on_screen : Sun.OnScreen -> Pixels glow_radius_on_screen = |sun| sun_size_on_screen(glow_radius, sun) ## The disc's radius where the sun stands. disc_radius_on_screen : Sun.OnScreen -> Pixels disc_radius_on_screen = |sun| sun_size_on_screen(SunPath.radius, sun) ## The sun's shapes in a frame: while it is in view, its glow over the ## rectangle above the horizon, adding its light to the sky, and its disc ## over that, and nothing while it isn't. sun_shapes : Sun.Sighting -> List(Shapes.Shape) sun_shapes = |sun_sighting| match sun_sighting { InView(sun) => { look = Sun.look(sun) Shapes.added_light_shapes([Screen.above_horizon_rect(look.glow)]).append( Disc({ center: sun.center, radius: Sun.disc_radius_on_screen(sun), fill: look.disc, }), ) } OutOfView => [] } ## The sun's glow and disc where it stands, sized by its lens and warmed ## from their noon colors toward their setting ones as far as the horizon ## is warm. look : Sun.OnScreen -> Sun.Look look = |sun| { warmed = |colors| ColorShade.color_between({ from: colors.noon, to: colors.setting, fraction: sun.warmth, }) { glow: Brush.glow({ inner_color: Brush.with_alpha(warmed(glow_core), 0.85), middle_color: Brush.with_alpha(warmed(glow_haze), 0.32), outer_color: Brush.with_alpha(warmed(glow_haze), 0.0), middle_offset: 0.4, center: sun.center, inner_radius: sun_size_on_screen(glow_inner_radius, sun), outer_radius: Sun.glow_radius_on_screen(sun), }), disc: Radial({ inner_color: Brush.opaque_rgba(warmed(disc_core)), outer_color: Brush.opaque_rgba(warmed(disc_rim)), center: sun.center, inner_radius: sun_size_on_screen(disc_inner_radius, sun), outer_radius: Sun.disc_radius_on_screen(sun), }), } } } ## One of the sun's colors at noon, and as it sets, with the horizon at its ## warmest. SunColors : { noon : RgbColor, setting : RgbColor } ## The light the middle of the glow adds to the sky: a soft gold at noon, ## which the pale sky takes nearly to white, and deep orange as the sun sets. ## The glow adds light, so a dim color here is a gentle glow, not a dark one. glow_core : SunColors glow_core = { noon: RgbColor.of(0xA08060), setting: RgbColor.of(0xFF8A3C) } ## The light of the haze the glow fades through: a faint warmth at noon, red ## as the sun sets. glow_haze : SunColors glow_haze = { noon: RgbColor.of(0x806048), setting: RgbColor.of(0xE04A28) } ## The middle of the disc: pale yellow at noon, orange as the sun sets. disc_core : SunColors disc_core = { noon: RgbColor.of(0xFFE6A3), setting: RgbColor.of(0xFFA860) } ## The disc's rim: orange at noon, red as the sun sets. disc_rim : SunColors disc_rim = { noon: RgbColor.of(0xFF9D5C), setting: RgbColor.of(0xD83A22) } ## How long `size`, one of the sun's sizes, is drawn where `sun` stands. sun_size_on_screen : FarRise, Sun.OnScreen -> Pixels sun_size_on_screen = |size, sun| Lens.size_on_screen({ size, focal_length: sun.focal_length }) ## Whether any of the glow around `sun` reaches across the screen, as far out ## as the frame is drawn, from `Screen.drawn_left` to `Screen.drawn_right`, ## which every roll of the screen stays inside. is_glow_on_screen : Sun.OnScreen -> Bool is_glow_on_screen = |sun| { from_middle = sun.center.x.minus(Screen.center_x).abs() reach = Screen.drawn_right.minus(Screen.center_x) from_middle.minus(Sun.glow_radius_on_screen(sun)) < reach } ## How far the glow reaches from the sun's middle. glow_radius : FarRise glow_radius = FarRise.of(340.0) ## Where the glow's fade starts, near the sun's middle. glow_inner_radius : FarRise glow_inner_radius = FarRise.of(8.0) ## Where the disc's shading from pale to orange starts. disc_inner_radius : FarRise disc_inner_radius = FarRise.of(4.0) ## Whether `sun_sighting` is in view at `x` across the screen and within a ## thousandth of a pixel of `y` up it, as `focal_length` draws it. is_in_view_at : Sun.Sighting, { x : F64, y : F64, focal_length : Pixels, } -> Bool is_in_view_at = |sun_sighting, { x, y, focal_length }| match sun_sighting { InView(sun) => { is_near_y = sun.center.y.minus(Pixels.of(y)).abs() < Pixels.of(0.001) sun.center.x == Pixels.of(x) and is_near_y and sun.focal_length == focal_length } OutOfView => False } # The rider faces the sun at the start, 262.5 pixels above the horizon through # the lens at rest. expect { facing_sun = { heading: SunPath.bearing_at(Clock.start), focal_length: Lens.resting_focal_length, } is_in_view_at( Sun.sun_in_view(facing_sun, Clock.start), { x: 480.0, y: 37.487, focal_length: Lens.resting_focal_length, }, ) } # A lens at half its focal length draws the sun nearer the horizon, and at # half its size. expect { half_focal_length = Lens.resting_focal_length.times(0.5) facing_sun = { heading: SunPath.bearing_at(Clock.start), focal_length: half_focal_length } sighting = Sun.sun_in_view(facing_sun, Clock.start) half_on_screen = { center: Point.at(480.0, 168.744), focal_length: half_focal_length, warmth: Fraction.zero, } is_in_view_at( sighting, { x: 480.0, y: 168.744, focal_length: half_focal_length, }, ) and Sun.disc_radius_on_screen(half_on_screen).to_f64() == SunPath.radius.times(0.5).to_f64() } ## The sun in the middle of the screen through the lens at rest, with the ## horizon `warmth` warm. sun_with_warmth : F64 -> Sun.OnScreen sun_with_warmth = |warmth| { center: Point.at(480.0, 200.0), focal_length: Lens.resting_focal_length, warmth: Fraction.of(warmth), } ## The disc's middle and rim colors in `look`. disc_colors : Sun.Look -> List(Brush.Rgba) disc_colors = |look| match look.disc { Radial({ inner_color, outer_color, .. }) => [inner_color, outer_color] _ => crash "Sun: the disc is a radial gradient" } ## The glow's middle color in `look`. glow_core_color : Sun.Look -> Brush.Rgba glow_core_color = |look| match look.glow { Glow({ inner_color, .. }) => inner_color _ => crash "Sun: the glow is a glow" } # The sun keeps its noon colors with the horizon cold, takes its setting ones # with the horizon at its warmest, and lies between them in between. expect [ (0.0, brush_color(0xFFE6A3), brush_color(0xFF9D5C)), (0.5, brush_color(0xFFC782), brush_color(0xEC6C3F)), (1.0, brush_color(0xFFA860), brush_color(0xD83A22)), ].all(|(warmth, core, rim)| disc_colors(Sun.look(sun_with_warmth(warmth))) == [core, rim]) expect [ (0.0, Brush.with_alpha(RgbColor.of(0xA08060), 0.85)), (1.0, Brush.with_alpha(RgbColor.of(0xFF8A3C), 0.85)), ].all(|(warmth, core)| glow_core_color(Sun.look(sun_with_warmth(warmth))) == core) ## An opaque color as a brush paints it, from its hex digits. brush_color : I64 -> Brush.Rgba brush_color = |rgb| Brush.opaque_rgba(RgbColor.of(rgb)) # The glow adds its light to the sky, and the disc paints over it. expect { drawn = Sun.sun_shapes(InView(sun_with_warmth(0.0))) drawn.len() == 4 and drawn.first() == Ok(Blend(Add)) and drawn.get(2) == Ok(Blend(Over)) } # Facing north at the start, the rider faces away from the sun. expect { facing_north = { heading: Angle.north, focal_length: Lens.resting_focal_length } Sun.sun_in_view(facing_north, Clock.start) == OutOfView } ## Whether the sun is in view at the ride's start, for a camera at rest that ## faces `radians` to the left of it. is_in_view_beside : F64 -> Bool is_in_view_beside = |radians| { heading = SunPath.bearing_at(Clock.start).plus(Angle.Turn.radians(0.0 - radians)) match Sun.sun_in_view({ heading, focal_length: Lens.resting_focal_length }, Clock.start) { InView(_) => True OutOfView => False } } # At rest the glow still reaches the screen's margin with the sun 0.95 radians # to the side, either side, and has left it at 1.0. expect [0.95, -0.95].all(is_in_view_beside) expect [1.0, -1.0, 1.5, -1.5, 3.0].all(|radians| !is_in_view_beside(radians))

name: canvas_apps/safari/SunPath.roc
html: ## The sun's path across the sky through the ride: the sky turns about its ## pole as the earth does, carrying the sun down an arc into the southwest. ## The sun's place is worked out each frame from the clock, and its height is ## what the rest of the sunset follows: the sky, the mountains and the truck's ## headlights. import Angle import Clock import FarHeight import FarRise import Lens import Steps SunPath :: [].{ ## The direction the sun stands in: its bearing, and its height above the ## horizon, a far height, which is how the resting lens holds an elevation. Direction : { bearing : Angle.Bearing, height : FarHeight } ## The sun's direction at `clock`, from where the turning sky has carried ## it. In the frame of the sky's pole the sun stands `declination` from the ## sky's equator and `hour_angle_at(clock)` west of the meridian; the pole ## stands `latitude` above the north horizon. Turning that into the ## rider's frame is the one piece of spherical trig: the sun's direction ## as a unit vector, up, north and east. sun_direction_at : Clock -> SunPath.Direction sun_direction_at = |clock| { pole = latitude.to_radians() from_equator = declination.to_radians() hour = hour_angle_at(clock).to_radians() up = pole.sin() * from_equator.sin() + pole.cos() * from_equator.cos() * hour.cos() north = pole.cos() * from_equator.sin() - pole.sin() * from_equator.cos() * hour.cos() east = 0.0 - from_equator.cos() * hour.sin() level = (north * north + east * east).sqrt() elevation = Angle.Turn.radians(F64.atan2({ x: level, y: up })) { bearing: Angle.Bearing.radians(F64.atan2({ x: north, y: east })), height: Lens.height_at_elevation(elevation), } } ## The sun's bearing at `clock`. It starts a little west of south and ## swings west as it sinks. bearing_at : Clock -> Angle.Bearing bearing_at = |clock| sun_direction_at(clock).bearing ## How high the sun stands above the horizon at `clock`; below it once ## negative. height_at : Clock -> FarHeight height_at = |clock| sun_direction_at(clock).height ## The sun's radius: how far its top stands above its middle, and its ## bottom below. radius : FarRise radius = FarRise.of(46.0) ## How high the sun stands above the horizon as the ride starts. height_at_start : FarHeight height_at_start = height_at(Clock.start) ## How high the sun stands once it has fully set: its top on the horizon. height_when_set : FarHeight height_when_set = FarHeight.zero.lowered_by(radius) ## The first step at which the sun has fully set, its whole disc below the ## horizon. The sky's turning places it; `sunset_climax` in ## gates/expects/RideExpects.roc holds where the sunset falls in the ride. fully_set_at : Clock fully_set_at = { var $clock = Clock.start while height_at($clock) > height_when_set { $clock = $clock.next() } $clock } } ## How far the sky's pole stands above the north horizon, which is the ## latitude the ride is at: 45°, halfway from the equator to the pole. The ## further from the equator, the more slantwise the sun goes down. latitude : Angle.Turn latitude = Angle.Turn.degrees(45.0) ## How far the sun stands south of the sky's equator: as far as it goes, at ## the winter solstice. It makes the year's shortest day, with the sun low at ## noon and setting in the southwest. declination : Angle.Turn declination = Angle.Turn.degrees(-23.44) ## How many steps the sky takes to turn an hour, a 24th of a whole turn. The ## ride of about 7,000 steps lasts most of an afternoon and evening. steps_an_hour : Steps steps_an_hour = Steps.of(1000) ## How far past noon the ride starts: 10°, forty minutes at the sky's 15° an ## hour. hour_angle_at_start : Angle.Turn hour_angle_at_start = Angle.Turn.degrees(10.0) ## How far west of the meridian the sky has turned the sun at `clock`. It ## turns at one steady rate, so the sun climbs and sinks fastest near the ## horizon and lingers near noon. hour_angle_at : Clock -> Angle.Turn hour_angle_at = |clock| { hours_in = clock.steps_since(Clock.start).ratio_to(steps_an_hour) hour_angle_at_start.plus(Angle.Turn.degrees(15.0).times(hours_in)) } # Part of the disc is still above the horizon a step before `fully_set_at`, # which gates/expects/RideExpects.roc holds, and none of it from then on. expect SunPath.height_at(SunPath.fully_set_at) <= SunPath.height_when_set # At noon the sun stands due south, as high as it climbs: 90° less the # latitude, less the declination south of the equator, so 21.56°. The ride # starts forty minutes later, a little lower and west of south. expect { noon = Lens.height_at_elevation(Angle.Turn.degrees(21.56)) a_little_lower = Lens.height_at_elevation(Angle.Turn.degrees(20.5)) start = SunPath.sun_direction_at(Clock.start) west_of_south = start.bearing.turn_from(Angle.Bearing.radians(F64.pi)) start.height < noon and start.height > a_little_lower and west_of_south > Angle.straight_ahead } # The sun swings west as it sinks, and sinks faster the lower it is: the # second hour of the ride takes it further down than the first. expect { at_hour = |hour| SunPath.sun_direction_at(Clock.at_step(hour * 1000)) first_drop = at_hour(0).height.minus(at_hour(1).height) second_drop = at_hour(1).height.minus(at_hour(2).height) at_hour(2).bearing.turn_from(at_hour(1).bearing) > Angle.straight_ahead and second_drop > first_drop }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Throttle.roc
html: ## Throttle decides how hard the rider accelerates on the next step. Each limit ## asks for nothing or for an acceleration no harder than its own, and the ## acceleration offered is held to the least of them. import Acceleration import Along import Animation import Coast import Distance import EncounterReaction import Gawking import Motorcycle import Segment import Speed import Steps import ThrottleLimit import VehicleLimits Throttle :: [].{ ## The acceleration the motorcycle takes on the next step, on `segment`, the ## one it is on, with the segment's encounter at `encounter_stage`. next_acceleration : Motorcycle, { segment : Segment, encounter_stage : Animation.Stage, } -> Acceleration next_acceleration = |motorcycle, { segment, encounter_stage }| { offered = VehicleLimits.cruise_acceleration limits = [ bend_limit(motorcycle, segment), EncounterReaction.encounter_throttle(segment.encounter, encounter_stage), Gawking.gawk_brake(motorcycle, segment), shoulder_limit(motorcycle), ] limits.fold(offered, held_to) } } ## The speed to leave `segment` at: the speed for its bend, or rest at the route's ## end. exit_speed : Segment -> Speed exit_speed = |segment| match segment.ending { Bends({ turn, .. }) => VehicleLimits.turn_speed(turn) RouteEnds => Speed.at_rest } ## How fast the shoulder brake fades with the steps left to the shoulder: it ## falls to about a third every 20 steps, a time constant chosen by eye. brake_decay : Steps brake_decay = Steps.of(20) ## The acceleration `a`, held to what `limit` asks. held_to : Acceleration, ThrottleLimit -> Acceleration held_to = |a, limit| match limit { AtMost(most) => a.min(most) NoLimit => a } ## Whether a motorcycle at `rider_along` is near enough the end of a segment ## `segment_length` long to brake for its bend. is_near_end : Along, Distance -> Bool is_near_end = |rider_along, segment_length| Along.at(segment_length).distance_from(rider_along) <= bend_approach ## How far short of a segment's end the rider starts to brake for its bend. bend_approach : Distance bend_approach = Distance.metres(60.0) ## Near the end of the segment, the brake that brings the rider to the exit ## speed at the point where they commit to the turn. Past that point there is ## no road left to brake on, and the limit holds the acceleration at none. bend_limit : Motorcycle, Segment -> ThrottleLimit bend_limit = |motorcycle, segment| { rider_along = motorcycle.route_place.road_point.along if is_near_end(rider_along, segment.length) { segment_exit_speed = exit_speed(segment) room_to_commit = segment.commit_along().distance_from(rider_along) AtMost( VehicleLimits.braking_to( motorcycle.speed, { target: segment_exit_speed, within: room_to_commit }, ), ) } else { NoLimit } } ## Nothing, unless a coast from here leaves the road; then the brake for the ## shoulder it reaches. shoulder_limit : Motorcycle -> ThrottleLimit shoulder_limit = |motorcycle| match Coast.coast_outcome(motorcycle) { EndsAt(_) => NoLimit Leaves({ after, .. }) => AtMost(shoulder_brake(motorcycle.speed, after)) } ## The brake at `speed` for a coast that leaves the road in ## `steps_to_shoulder`. A coast counts the step that leaves, so zero steps ## means the count behind it is wrong. shoulder_brake : Speed, Steps -> Acceleration shoulder_brake = |speed, steps_to_shoulder| if steps_to_shoulder == Steps.zero { crash "Throttle.shoulder_brake: a coast leaves the road after zero steps, but a coast counts the step that leaves" } else { n = steps_to_shoulder.to_f64() even_braking = -speed.to_metres_a_step() / (2.0 * n) Acceleration.metres_a_step_each_step(even_braking * F64.e.pow(-n / brake_decay.to_f64())) } ## This many metres a step, each step. acceleration_of : F64 -> Acceleration acceleration_of = |metres| Acceleration.metres_a_step_each_step(metres) # A limit lowers what it is offered, and never raises it. expect held_to(Acceleration.steady, NoLimit) == Acceleration.steady expect held_to(acceleration_of(-0.5), NoLimit) == acceleration_of(-0.5) expect held_to(acceleration_of(0.01), AtMost(acceleration_of(-0.5))) == acceleration_of(-0.5) expect held_to(acceleration_of(-0.5), AtMost(Acceleration.steady)) == acceleration_of(-0.5) ## The shoulder brake at 1 metre a step. brake_after : U32 -> Acceleration brake_after = |steps_to_shoulder| shoulder_brake(Speed.metres_a_step(1.0), Steps.of(steps_to_shoulder)) expect brake_after(40) < Acceleration.steady expect brake_after(40) > brake_after(2) # A coast that leaves the road on its first step still brakes. expect brake_after(1) < Acceleration.steady

name: canvas_apps/safari/ThrottleLimit.roc
html: ## What one limit on the throttle asks. Throttle holds the acceleration it ## offers to the least of its limits, and EncounterReaction and Gawking each ## give one. The type has a module of its own because Throttle imports both of ## them. import Acceleration ## Nothing, or to accelerate no harder than this. ThrottleLimit := [NoLimit, AtMost(Acceleration)].{ is_eq : _ }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Tour.roc
html: ## Tour is the whole ride, for any platform that draws it. It keeps the ## current instant of the ride and every instant behind it, back to the ride's ## start, so stepping back can reach step 0. The whole ride's instants come to ## under a megabyte. A restart clears them. SafariApp turns it into a canvas ## app, with the keys, the pause, and the frame leaned by the roll. import Clock import Route import World import RideInstant import Steps ## The route, the instant the ride has reached, and the instants before it. ## There is one past instant for each step the clock has taken since the ride ## last started, so `past_instants` is as long as the clock's count of steps: ## a step forward appends one, a step back drops one, and a restart empties it. Tour :: { route : Route, instant : RideInstant, past_instants : List(RideInstant), }.{ initial : Tour initial = Tour.({ route: World.route, instant: RideInstant.initial, past_instants: [] }) ## The instant the ride has reached. instant : Tour -> RideInstant instant = |Tour.(tour)| tour.instant ## The route the ride is on. route : Tour -> Route route = |Tour.(tour)| tour.route ## How many instants are kept behind the current one: how far back the ## tour can step. past_instant_count : Tour -> U64 past_instant_count = |Tour.(tour)| tour.past_instants.len() ## The tour a step on.
