A ride that has finished starts again. step_forward : Tour -> Tour step_forward = |tour| match tour_after_step(tour) { Continued(next_tour) | Restarted(next_tour) => next_tour } ## The tour `length` steps on. steps_forward : Tour, Steps -> Tour steps_forward = |tour, length| { var $tour = tour for _ in 0..<length.to_u32() { $tour = Tour.step_forward($tour) } $tour } ## The tour `length` steps back, or at the ride's start if that is ## nearer. steps_back : Tour, Steps -> Tour steps_back = |tour, length| { var $tour = tour for _ in 0..<length.to_u32() { $tour = Tour.step_back($tour) } $tour } ## The tour ridden from its start to `goal`, with the instants it passed ## behind it. The ride must not finish before `goal`. at_step : Clock -> Tour at_step = |goal| { var $tour = Tour.initial while Tour.instant($tour).clock != goal { $tour = match tour_after_step($tour) { Continued(next_tour) => next_tour Restarted(_) => crash "Tour.at_step: the ride finishes before step ${goal.to_str()}" } } $tour } ## The tour a step back. At the ride's start there is nothing behind it, ## so it stays there. step_back : Tour -> Tour step_back = |Tour.(tour)| match tour.past_instants.last() { Ok(previous_instant) => { past_instants = tour.past_instants.drop_last(1) Tour.({ ..tour, instant: previous_instant, past_instants }) } Err(ListWasEmpty) => Tour.(tour) } ## The tour stepped on until the rider is on another of the route's ## segments, which are its scenes. Every ride finishes and starts again on ## the first segment, so this ends: on the next segment, or on the first ## after the last. A route of one segment would never leave it, so that ## crashes. at_next_segment : Tour -> Tour at_next_segment = |tour| { from = rider_segment_index(tour) var $tour = tour while rider_segment_index($tour) == from { $tour = match tour_after_step($tour) { Continued(next_tour) => next_tour Restarted(next_tour) => if rider_segment_index(next_tour) == from { crash "Tour.at_next_segment: the ride started again on the segment it set out from, so the route has only one" } else { next_tour } } } $tour } } ## `tour` a step on, with its past instants kept. The ride that has finished ## starts again with none. tour_after_step : Tour -> [Continued(Tour), Restarted(Tour)] tour_after_step = |Tour.(tour)| match RideInstant.next_or_restart(tour.route, tour.instant) { Continued(next_instant) => { past_instants = tour.past_instants.append(tour.instant) Continued(Tour.({ ..tour, instant: next_instant, past_instants })) } Restarted(start) => Restarted(Tour.({ ..tour, instant: start, past_instants: [] })) } ## The index of the segment the rider is on. rider_segment_index : Tour -> Route.SegmentIndex rider_segment_index = |Tour.(tour)| tour.instant.rider_segment_index() # The next segment from the start is the second, reached on the step that # leaves the first. expect { reached = Tour.at_next_segment(Tour.initial) rider_segment_index(reached) == Route.SegmentIndex.number(1) and rider_segment_index(Tour.step_back(reached)) == Route.SegmentIndex.first } # A tour ridden to a step keeps every instant it passed, and none at the start. expect { ridden = Tour.at_step(Clock.at_step(3)) Tour.instant(ridden).clock == Clock.at_step(3) and Tour.past_instant_count(ridden) == 3 } expect Tour.past_instant_count(Tour.at_step(Clock.start)) == 0 # Stepping forward a number of steps lands where riding to that step does. expect { at_two = Tour.at_step(Clock.at_step(2)) Tour.instant(Tour.steps_forward(at_two, Steps.of(3))).clock == Clock.at_step(5) } # A tour stepped back from step 5 is one step short of the start after 4 backs, # at step 0 after 5, and still there after a sixth. expect { var $tour = Tour.steps_back(Tour.at_step(Clock.at_step(5)), Steps.of(4)) after_four = Tour.instant($tour).clock $tour = Tour.step_back($tour) after_five = Tour.instant($tour).clock $tour = Tour.step_back($tour) after_six = Tour.instant($tour).clock after_four == Clock.at_step(1) and after_five == Clock.start and after_six == Clock.start }

name: canvas_apps/safari/Tower.roc
html: ## A radio tower: a square lattice that tapers from its footprint to a point ## at its top. It is drawn as rods (four legs, a ring at every storey, and ## crossed braces in the lowest storeys) with a blinking beacon on top. ## The earth curves away under a far tower, so it sinks below the horizon ## from the bottom up. import lib.Point import lib.Pixels import Angle import Beacon import Camera import EarthCurve import Spot import Distance import lib.Fraction import RiderView import Sky import Sprite import lib.Brush import lib.RgbColor import Screen import lib.Shapes ## A tower in a frame: how it is turned, and its beacon as it shines. Tower :: { yaw : Angle.Turn, beacon : Beacon }.{ ## A tower turned by `yaw`, with `beacon` on top. standing : { yaw : Angle.Turn, beacon : Beacon } -> Tower standing = |{ yaw, beacon }| Tower.({ yaw, beacon }) ## How far the tower is turned from square with the road, positive to the ## right. yaw : Tower -> Angle.Turn yaw = |Tower.(tower)| tower.yaw ## How a tower looks. scenery_sprite : Tower, Sprite.Setting -> Sprite scenery_sprite = |tower, { spot, focal_length, darkness }| { footprint = tower_footprint(tower, spot) rod_color = Sky.color_at_darkness(tower_color, darkness) Sprite.from_shapes(tower_shapes(tower, { footprint, spot, focal_length, rod_color })) } ## How tall a tower stands, from its foot to its apex. scenery_height : Tower -> Distance scenery_height = |_tower| tower_height } ## How far up a tower the horizon hides it, when its foot stands at `foot` in ## the rider's view, `base_height` above the rider's level: the part below the ## lowest height the rider can see there, which is never negative. hidden_height : { foot : RiderView.RiderPoint, base_height : Distance } -> Distance hidden_height = |{ foot, base_height }| EarthCurve.lowest_visible_height(foot).minus(base_height).max(Distance.zero) ## A corner of the tower's square footprint, as seen along the route. Corner : [BackLeft, BackRight, FrontRight, FrontLeft] ## Where the footprint's four corners stand in the rider's view. Footprint : { back_left : RiderView.RiderPoint, back_right : RiderView.RiderPoint, front_right : RiderView.RiderPoint, front_left : RiderView.RiderPoint, } ## Where the four footprint corners of a tower standing at `spot` are in the ## rider's view, on the rider's level. tower_footprint : Tower, Spot -> Footprint tower_footprint = |tower, spot| { corner_point = |corner| { { ahead, rightward } = corner_offset(corner) standing = spot.standing_point({ facing: tower.yaw(), offset: { ahead, rightward, height: Distance.zero }, }) { forward: standing.forward, right: standing.right } } { back_left: corner_point(BackLeft), back_right: corner_point(BackRight), front_right: corner_point(FrontRight), front_left: corner_point(FrontLeft), } } ## The whole tower standing on `footprint`: legs, rings, braces and beacon, in ## that order, its rods in `rod_color`. Its sighting refuses a tower hidden ## wholly below the horizon, so there is always something to draw. tower_shapes : Tower, { footprint : Footprint, spot : Spot, focal_length : Pixels, rod_color : RgbColor, } -> List(Shapes.Shape) tower_shapes = |Tower.(tower), { footprint, spot, focal_length, rod_color }| { geometry = { footprint, spot, focal_length, metre_on_screen: metre_on_screen({ at: spot.foot(), focal_length }), rod_color, } if hidden_on_tower(geometry) >= tower_height { crash "Tower.tower_shapes: a tower hidden wholly below the horizon is refused at its sighting" } else { apex = spot.foot().at_height(height_in_view(geometry, tower_height)) rods = [ leg_shapes(geometry, apex.to_point_at_height()), ring_shapes(geometry), brace_shapes(geometry), ].join() beacon_disc = tower.beacon.disc({ center: Camera.project(apex, focal_length), metre_on_screen: geometry.metre_on_screen, }) match beacon_disc { Ok(disc) => rods.append(disc) Err(TooDim) | Err(TooSmall) => rods } } } tower_height : Distance tower_height = Distance.metres(80.0) tower_half_width : Distance tower_half_width = Distance.metres(6.0) storey_height : Distance storey_height = Distance.metres(20.0) brace_storeys : U64 brace_storeys = 2 rod_half_width : Distance rod_half_width = Distance.metres(0.12) rod_width : Distance rod_width = rod_half_width.times(2.0) tower_color : RgbColor tower_color = RgbColor.of(0x9AA0A8) ## A tower's measurements in this frame, which its rods are worked out from: ## where its footprint stands, its spot (which gives its foot, its lift and the ## ground's drop beneath it), and the focal length it is seen through. ## `metre_on_screen`, how many pixels a metre across spans as far ahead as its ## foot, sizes its rods and its beacon. It is a cache, worked out once per tower ## from the foot and the focal length, because every rod reads it. ## `rod_color` is the rods' color, dimmed as far as the sky has darkened; the ## beacon is a light, and never dims. TowerGeometry : { footprint : Footprint, spot : Spot, focal_length : Pixels, metre_on_screen : Pixels, rod_color : RgbColor, } ## How far up the tower the horizon hides it. hidden_on_tower : TowerGeometry -> Distance hidden_on_tower = |{ spot, .. }| hidden_height({ foot: spot.foot().to_rider(), base_height: spot.lift().minus(spot.drop()) }) ## How far a corner lies from the footprint's centre, ahead and to the right, ## in the tower's own frame. Left and back are the negative ways. corner_offset : Corner -> { ahead : Distance, rightward : Distance } corner_offset = |corner| match corner { BackLeft => { ahead: tower_half_width.opposite(), rightward: tower_half_width.opposite() } BackRight => { ahead: tower_half_width.opposite(), rightward: tower_half_width } FrontRight => { ahead: tower_half_width, rightward: tower_half_width } FrontLeft => { ahead: tower_half_width, rightward: tower_half_width.opposite() } } ## The corners in drawing order, going round the square. corners : List(Corner) corners = [BackLeft, BackRight, FrontRight, FrontLeft] ## The corner after this one, going round the square. next_corner : Corner -> Corner next_corner = |corner| match corner { BackLeft => BackRight BackRight => FrontRight FrontRight => FrontLeft FrontLeft => BackLeft } # Going round the square from the first corner meets `corners` in order, then # comes back to the first. expect { second = next_corner(BackLeft) third = next_corner(second) fourth = next_corner(third) [BackLeft, second, third, fourth] == corners and next_corner(fourth) == BackLeft } footprint_corner : Footprint, Corner -> RiderView.RiderPoint footprint_corner = |footprint, corner| match corner { BackLeft => footprint.back_left BackRight => footprint.back_right FrontRight => footprint.front_right FrontLeft => footprint.front_left } ## How high a point `height_on_tower` up the tower stands in the rider's ## view: raised by the tower's lift, and lowered by the ground's drop. height_in_view : TowerGeometry, Distance -> Distance height_in_view = |geometry, height_on_tower| geometry.spot.lift().plus(height_on_tower.minus(geometry.spot.drop())) ## A corner of the tower at `height_on_tower`: drawn in toward the foot as ## the tower tapers, raised by the tower's lift, and lowered by the ground's ## drop. corner_at : TowerGeometry, { corner : Corner, height_on_tower : Distance, } -> RiderView.PointAtHeight corner_at = |geometry, { corner, height_on_tower }| { taper_fraction = height_on_tower.ratio_to(tower_height) bottom = footprint_corner(geometry.footprint, corner) tapered = |start, end| start.plus(end.minus(start).times(taper_fraction)) { right: tapered(bottom.right, geometry.spot.foot().right()), forward: tapered(bottom.forward, geometry.spot.foot().forward()), height: height_in_view(geometry, height_on_tower), } } ## The shortest rod on screen that has a direction to turn its width across. ## A shorter one is drawn as if one pixel long, so its quad shrinks to its ## point rather than dividing by nearly nothing. shortest_rod_with_direction : Pixels shortest_rod_with_direction = Pixels.of(0.0001) ## A rod between two points on screen, `width` wide, in `color`. screen_rod : { from : Point, to : Point, width : Pixels, color : RgbColor, } -> Shapes.Shape screen_rod = |{ from, to, width, color }| { x_change = to.x.minus(from.x).to_f64() y_change = to.y.minus(from.y).to_f64() across = width.to_f64() measured_length = Screen.distance({ from, to }).to_f64() rod_length = if measured_length < shortest_rod_with_direction.to_f64() { 1.0 } else { measured_length } rod_quad({ from, to, offset_x: Pixels.of(across * ((0.0 - y_change) / rod_length) / 2.0), offset_y: Pixels.of(across * (x_change / rod_length) / 2.0), color, }) } ## The quad of a rod from `from` to `to`, its sides `offset_x` and ## `offset_y` either side of the line between them, in `color`. rod_quad : { from : Point, to : Point, offset_x : Pixels, offset_y : Pixels, color : RgbColor, } -> Shapes.Shape rod_quad = |{ from, to, offset_x, offset_y, color }| Quad({ first: { x: from.x.plus(offset_x), y: from.y.plus(offset_y) }, second: { x: to.x.plus(offset_x), y: to.y.plus(offset_y) }, third: { x: to.x.minus(offset_x), y: to.y.minus(offset_y) }, fourth: { x: from.x.minus(offset_x), y: from.y.minus(offset_y) }, fill: Brush.flat(color), }) ## A rod between two points in the rider's view, cut where it crosses the ## near plane. A rod wholly behind the near plane has no shape. rod_shape : TowerGeometry, { from : RiderView.PointAtHeight, to : RiderView.PointAtHeight, } -> Try(Shapes.Shape, [BehindCamera]) rod_shape = |geometry, line| { ahead = RiderView.line_ahead(line)? Ok( screen_rod({ from: Camera.project(ahead.from, geometry.focal_length), to: Camera.project(ahead.to, geometry.focal_length), width: geometry.metre_on_screen.times(rod_width.to_metres()), color: geometry.rod_color, }), ) } ## How many pixels one metre across spans as far ahead as `at`. metre_on_screen : { at : RiderView.RiderPointAhead, focal_length : Pixels } -> Pixels metre_on_screen = |{ at, focal_length }| { on_level = at.at_height(Distance.zero) one_metre_right = Camera.project(on_level.at_right(Distance.metres(1.0)), focal_length) on_level_point = Camera.project(on_level.at_right(Distance.zero), focal_length) one_metre_right.x.minus(on_level_point.x) } ## The four legs, from the footprint's corners up to the apex. leg_shapes : TowerGeometry, RiderView.PointAtHeight -> List(Shapes.Shape) leg_shapes = |geometry, apex| corners.keep_oks( |corner| rod_shape( geometry, { from: corner_at(geometry, { corner, height_on_tower: hidden_on_tower(geometry) }), to: apex, }, ), ) ## The ring of rods round the tower at `ring_height`. ring_shapes_at : TowerGeometry, Distance -> List(Shapes.Shape) ring_shapes_at = |geometry, ring_height| corners.keep_oks( |corner| rod_shape( geometry, { from: corner_at(geometry, { corner, height_on_tower: ring_height }), to: corner_at(geometry, { corner: next_corner(corner), height_on_tower: ring_height }), }, ), ) ## A ring at every storey below the top, bottom first, leaving out those ## the earth has hidden. ring_shapes : TowerGeometry -> List(Shapes.Shape) ring_shapes = |geometry| ring_heights.join_map( |ring_height| if ring_height <= hidden_on_tower(geometry) { [] } else { ring_shapes_at(geometry, ring_height) }, ) ## The height of each ring: a storey up, and a storey more, to the top. ring_heights : List(Distance) ring_heights = { var $heights = [] var $height = storey_height while $height < tower_height { $heights = $heights.append($height) $height = $height.plus(storey_height) } $heights } ## The crossed braces of the lowest storeys, bottom first. A storey the ## earth has partly hidden starts its braces at the horizon. brace_shapes : TowerGeometry -> List(Shapes.Shape) brace_shapes = |geometry| List.from_iter(U64.until(0, brace_storeys)).join_map(|storey| storey_shapes(geometry, storey)) storey_shapes : TowerGeometry, U64 -> List(Shapes.Shape) storey_shapes = |geometry, storey| { storey_bottom = storey_height.times(storey.to_f64()) storey_top = storey_bottom.plus(storey_height) if storey_top <= hidden_on_tower(geometry) { [] } else { hidden_in_storey = storey_bottom.max(hidden_on_tower(geometry)).minus(storey_bottom) hidden_fraction = Fraction.of(hidden_in_storey.ratio_to(storey_height)) corners.join_map( |corner| face_brace_shapes( geometry, { corner, storey_bottom, storey_top, hidden_fraction }, ), ) } } ## The two braces crossing the face from `corner` to the next corner: one ## rising each way. face_brace_shapes : TowerGeometry, { corner : Corner, storey_bottom : Distance, storey_top : Distance, hidden_fraction : Fraction, } -> List(Shapes.Shape) face_brace_shapes = |geometry, { corner, storey_bottom, storey_top, hidden_fraction }| { next = next_corner(corner) brace_up = { from: RiderView.point_between({ from: corner_at(geometry, { corner, height_on_tower: storey_bottom }), to: corner_at(geometry, { corner: next, height_on_tower: storey_top }), fraction: hidden_fraction, }), to: corner_at(geometry, { corner: next, height_on_tower: storey_top }), } brace_down = { from: RiderView.point_between({ from: corner_at(geometry, { corner: next, height_on_tower: storey_bottom }), to: corner_at(geometry, { corner, height_on_tower: storey_top }), fraction: hidden_fraction, }), to: corner_at(geometry, { corner, height_on_tower: storey_top }), } [brace_up, brace_down].keep_oks(|brace| rod_shape(geometry, brace)) } ## `point` on the rider's level and past the near plane, which every such ## point in these tests is. ahead : RiderView.RiderPoint -> RiderView.RiderPointAhead ahead = |point| RiderView.rider_point_ahead(point) ?? crash "a test's point is past the near plane" expect screen_rod({ from: Point.at(0.0, 0.0), to: Point.at(30.0, 40.0), width: Pixels.of(10.0), color: tower_color, }) == Quad({ first: Point.at(-4.0, 3.0), second: Point.at(26.0, 43.0), third: Point.at(34.0, 37.0), fourth: Point.at(4.0, -3.0), fill: Flat(Brush.opaque_rgba(tower_color)), }) # A rod of no length is still one quad, all at its one point. expect screen_rod({ from: Point.at(5.0, 6.0), to: Point.at(5.0, 6.0), width: Pixels.of(10.0), color: tower_color, }) == Quad({ first: Point.at(5.0, 6.0), second: Point.at(5.0, 6.0), third: Point.at(5.0, 6.0), fourth: Point.at(5.0, 6.0), fill: Flat(Brush.opaque_rgba(tower_color)), }) ## How many pixels a metre across spans `forward` metres ahead, through a ## 500 px focal length. metre_ahead : F64 -> F64 metre_ahead = |forward| { at = ahead({ right: Distance.metres(3.0), forward: Distance.metres(forward) }) metre_on_screen({ at, focal_length: Pixels.of(500.0) }).to_f64() } expect metre_ahead(10.0) == 50.0 expect metre_ahead(25.0) == 20.0 expect metre_ahead(50.0) == 10.0 ## How far up a tower standing on the ground `forward` metres straight ahead ## the horizon hides it, and whether its sighting refuses it as below the ## horizon. hidden_ahead : F64 -> { hidden : Distance, is_below_horizon : Bool } hidden_ahead = |forward| { foot = { right: Distance.zero, forward: Distance.metres(forward) } base_height = EarthCurve.ground_drop(foot).opposite() top = base_height.plus(tower_height) { hidden: hidden_height({ foot, base_height }), is_below_horizon: EarthCurve.is_below_horizon({ point: foot, top }), } } # Within the horizon nothing of a tower is hidden. 4 km out the horizon hides # its lowest 61.6 m. Its tip shows to 4489 m, and a metre further the whole # tower is hidden, which is where its sighting refuses it. expect hidden_ahead(400.0) == { hidden: Distance.zero, is_below_horizon: False } expect (hidden_ahead(4000.0).hidden.to_metres() - 61.604082).abs() <= 0.000001 expect { shown = hidden_ahead(4489.0) shown.hidden < tower_height and !shown.is_below_horizon } expect { sunk = hidden_ahead(4490.0) sunk.hidden >= tower_height and sunk.is_below_horizon }

name: canvas_apps/safari/TowerSighting.roc
html: ## TowerSighting finds the radio towers in front of the rider in a frame. A tower ## stands past the end of every segment, off to the right, and a long ## segment has one more halfway along, off to the left. Each tower's beacon ## blinks on the ride's clock, and the sighting lights it for the frame. ## Unlike the trees and the critters, a tower has no size test: it is ## sighted however small it stands, until the earth's curve sinks it wholly ## below the horizon, and then it is refused. The sightings are worked out each ## frame from where the rider's camera stands, the route and the clock: with no ## size test, they need no lens. import Across import Along import Angle import Beacon import Clock import Distance import RoadAhead import SegmentFromRider import Geom import Pipeline import Tower TowerSighting :: [].{ ## The towers in view, in the order of `RoadAhead.segments_in_view`. towers_in_view : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, clock : Clock, } -> List(Pipeline.Sighted(Tower)) towers_in_view = |road, { vantage, clock }| RoadAhead.segments_in_view(road).join_map( |in_view| segment_towers(road, { vantage, in_view, clock }), ) } ## How far past the end of its segment a tower stands. end_tower_beyond_end : Distance end_tower_beyond_end = Distance.metres(160.0) ## How far right of the road's middle a tower past a segment's end stands. end_tower_right_of_middle : Distance end_tower_right_of_middle = Distance.metres(20.0) ## How far a tower past a segment's end is turned from square with the road: ## a turn to the left, as a positive turn is to the right. end_tower_yaw : Angle.Turn end_tower_yaw = Angle.Turn.degrees(-30.0) ## A segment longer than this has a tower halfway along. mid_tower_min_length : Distance mid_tower_min_length = Distance.metres(1000.0) ## How far left of the road's middle a tower halfway along a segment stands. mid_tower_left_of_middle : Distance mid_tower_left_of_middle = Distance.metres(100.0) ## Where the tower halfway along a segment `segment_length` long stands, off ## to the left, if the segment is long enough to have one. mid_tower_point : Distance -> Try(Geom.RoadPoint, [NoMidTower]) mid_tower_point = |segment_length| if segment_length > mid_tower_min_length { Ok({ along: Along.at(segment_length.divided_by(2.0)), across: Across.left_of_middle(mid_tower_left_of_middle), }) } else { Err(NoMidTower) } # Only a segment longer than a kilometre has a tower halfway along. expect mid_tower_point(Distance.metres(1000.0)) == Err(NoMidTower) expect mid_tower_point(Distance.metres(1000.5)) == Ok({ along: Along.metres(500.25), across: Across.metres(-100.0) }) ## The towers in view of a segment in view: the one past its end, then the ## one halfway along. segment_towers : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, in_view : RoadAhead.SegmentInView, clock : Clock, } -> List(Pipeline.Sighted(Tower)) segment_towers = |road, { vantage, in_view, clock }| [ end_tower(road, { vantage, in_view, clock }), mid_tower(road, { vantage, in_view, clock }), ].keep_oks(|tower| tower) ## The tower past the end of a segment in view, if it is in front of the ## camera and above the horizon. end_tower : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, in_view : RoadAhead.SegmentInView, clock : Clock, } -> Try(Pipeline.Sighted(Tower), [OutOfSight]) end_tower = |road, { vantage, in_view, clock }| { beacon = Beacon.at({ segment: in_view.index, place: AtEnd }, clock) tower_if_ahead( road, { vantage, from_rider: in_view.from_rider, road_point: { along: Along.at(in_view.segment.length.plus(end_tower_beyond_end)), across: Across.right_of_middle(end_tower_right_of_middle), }, tower: Tower.standing({ yaw: end_tower_yaw, beacon }), }, ) } ## The tower halfway along a segment in view, if it has one and it is in ## front of the camera and above the horizon. mid_tower : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, in_view : RoadAhead.SegmentInView, clock : Clock, } -> Try(Pipeline.Sighted(Tower), [OutOfSight, NoMidTower]) mid_tower = |road, { vantage, in_view, clock }| { road_point = mid_tower_point(in_view.segment.length)? beacon = Beacon.at({ segment: in_view.index, place: Midway }, clock) tower_if_ahead( road, { vantage, from_rider: in_view.from_rider, road_point, tower: Tower.standing({ yaw: Angle.straight_ahead, beacon }), }, ) } ## `tower` standing on the ground at `road_point` in the segment that lies at ## `from_rider`, if it is in front of a camera at `vantage` and some of it ## shows above the horizon. tower_if_ahead : RoadAhead.RoadView, { vantage : Geom.Vantage, from_rider : SegmentFromRider, road_point : Geom.RoadPoint, tower : Tower, } -> Try(Pipeline.Sighted(Tower), [OutOfSight]) tower_if_ahead = |road, { vantage, from_rider, road_point, tower }| { placed_tower : Geom.Placed(Tower) placed_tower = { road_point, lift: Distance.zero, kind: tower } Pipeline.sighting_above_horizon_of(placed_tower, { road, vantage, from_rider }) }

name: canvas_apps/safari/TreeShapes.roc
html: ## A conifer: a trunk under eight tiers of foliage. A far tree's tiers are flat ## triangles on the screen. A near one's are cones seen from the camera: the ## hull of a ring of points round each tier's base and its apex, so the ## tiers fatten as the camera passes under them. It works from what it is ## handed: a tree's height and color, where it stands from the camera, the ## lens, and how dark the sky is, which dims its trunk and its foliage. import Camera import ConvexHull import Distance import lib.Fraction import RiderView import Sky import Sprite import lib.Pixels import Spot import lib.Brush import lib.RgbColor import lib.Point import lib.Shapes TreeShapes :: [].{ ## The tree on the screen: its trunk, then its tiers top to bottom. A tree ## within round_trunk_reach has a shaded trunk. The crown is cones, shaded by ## how near they are, within cone_reach, and triangles beyond it. tree_sprite : Sprite.Setting, { height : Distance, foliage_color : RgbColor } -> Sprite tree_sprite = |{ spot, focal_length, darkness }, { height, foliage_color }| { dimmed_foliage = Sky.color_at_darkness(foliage_color, darkness) inputs = tier_inputs_of(spot, { height, focal_length, foliage_color: dimmed_foliage }) forward = inputs.base.forward() crown = TreeShapes.crown_of(forward) trunk = trunk_shape( inputs.outline, { finish: trunk_finish_of(forward), color: Sky.color_at_darkness(trunk_color, darkness), }, ) Sprite.from_shapes([trunk].concat(tiers.map(|tier| tier_shape(tier, { inputs, crown })))) } ## How a crown is drawn: cones, shaded by how near they are, or flat triangles. Crown : [Cones({ shade : Fraction }), Triangles] ## How a tree's crown is drawn at distance `forward`. crown_of : Distance -> TreeShapes.Crown crown_of = |forward| if forward < cone_reach { Cones({ shade: crown_shade(forward) }) } else { Triangles } ## Where the tree whose foot's middle is at `base` is on the screen, ## `height` tall, through a lens of `focal_length`. tree_outline : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead, { height : Distance, focal_length : Pixels, } -> Camera.Upright tree_outline = |base, { height, focal_length }| Camera.upright_on_screen(base, { height, focal_length }) } ## The tree is drawn 136 parts tall, and the shares below are parts of that, ## all chosen by eye. tree_parts : U64 tree_parts = 136 ## A tree nearer than this has cones for a crown. cone_reach : Distance cone_reach = Distance.metres(200.0) ## A tree's crown is shaded fully at the camera, less the farther off it ## is, and not at all from this far on. crown_shade_reach : Distance crown_shade_reach = Distance.metres(80.0) ## A tree nearer than this gets a shaded trunk, which looks round. Past it, a ## trunk is only a few pixels wide on the screen, too narrow for the shading ## to show, so it is drawn flat. The reach is two pairs of trees deep, chosen ## by eye. round_trunk_reach : Distance round_trunk_reach = Distance.metres(60.0) ## How a tree's trunk is drawn: shaded, which looks round, or flat. TrunkFinish : [Shaded, Flat] ## How a tree's trunk is drawn at distance `forward`. trunk_finish_of : Distance -> TrunkFinish trunk_finish_of = |forward| if forward < round_trunk_reach { Shaded } else { Flat } ## How tall a tree's crown looks on the screen. crown_height : Camera.Upright -> Pixels crown_height = |outline| outline.height_on_screen.scaled_by(crown_height_share) ## Where the top of a tree's crown is on the screen: the tree's tip. crown_top_y : Camera.Upright -> Pixels crown_top_y = |outline| outline.foot.y.minus(outline.height_on_screen) ## How far the crown reaches either side of the trunk at its widest, on the ## screen. crown_half_width : Camera.Upright -> Pixels crown_half_width = |outline| outline.height_on_screen.scaled_by(crown_half_width_share) ## One tier of the crown: where its top and its bottom are, as fractions of ## the crown's height down from its top, and how wide its bottom is, as a ## fraction of the crown's width. Tier : { top : Fraction, bottom : Fraction, width : Fraction, } ## What every tier of one tree needs. `base` is the middle of the tree's foot, ## and `height` how far its tip stands above that. `outline` is a cache: the ## tree's outline through `focal_length`, worked out once per tree from `base` ## and `height` for all eight tiers. TierInputs : { base : RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead, height : Distance, focal_length : Pixels, outline : Camera.Upright, foliage_color : RgbColor, } ## What every tier of the tree at `spot` needs, its base and outline worked ## out from the rest. tier_inputs_of : Spot, { height : Distance, focal_length : Pixels, foliage_color : RgbColor, } -> TierInputs tier_inputs_of = |spot, { height, focal_length, foliage_color }| { base = spot.base() { base, height, focal_length, outline: TreeShapes.tree_outline(base, { height, focal_length }), foliage_color, } } ## How wide each tier's bottom is, top tier first, as a fraction of the crown's ## width, chosen by eye. tier_widths : List(Fraction) tier_widths = [0.35, 0.44, 0.53, 0.63, 0.72, 0.81, 0.91, 1.0].map(Fraction.of) ## The tiers, top to bottom. Each starts a tenth of the crown lower than the ## one above and runs three tenths down, so each overlaps the next. tiers : List(Tier) tiers = tier_widths.map_with_index( |width, index| { top: Fraction.of(index.to_f64() / 10.0), bottom: Fraction.of((index.to_f64() + 3.0) / 10.0), width, }, ) # Each tier's top, bottom and width, top tier first. expect tiers.map(|tier| [tier.top.to_f64(), tier.bottom.to_f64(), tier.width.to_f64()]) == [ [0.0, 0.3, 0.35], [0.1, 0.4, 0.44], [0.2, 0.5, 0.53], [0.3, 0.6, 0.63], [0.4, 0.7, 0.72], [0.5, 0.8, 0.81], [0.6, 0.9, 0.91], [0.7, 1.0, 1.0], ] trunk_color : RgbColor trunk_color = RgbColor.of(0x5A3E22) ## Of the tree's parts, 55 are trunk below the crown, chosen by eye. trunk_height_share : Fraction trunk_height_share = Fraction.of(55.0 / tree_parts.to_f64()) ## The crown is the rest of the tree, so its tip is the tree's height. crown_height_share : Fraction crown_height_share = trunk_height_share.complement() ## The crown's widest half-width, as a fraction of the tree's height: 36 ## parts, chosen by eye. crown_half_width_share : Fraction crown_half_width_share = Fraction.of(36.0 / tree_parts.to_f64()) ## The trunk's width, as a fraction of the tree's height: 10 parts, chosen by ## eye. trunk_width_share : Fraction trunk_width_share = Fraction.of(10.0 / tree_parts.to_f64()) ## However far off a tree is, its trunk is this wide. min_trunk_width : Pixels min_trunk_width = Pixels.of(1.0) ## How far the trunk runs up inside the crown, as a fraction of the tree's ## height, so that no sky shows between them: 6.25 parts, chosen by eye. trunk_overlap_share : Fraction trunk_overlap_share = Fraction.of(6.25 / tree_parts.to_f64()) ## A cone's base is a ring of this many points. ring_point_count : U64 ring_point_count = 16 ## How much a crown is shaded at distance `forward`: fully at the camera, ## falling evenly to none at crown_shade_reach. crown_shade : Distance -> Fraction crown_shade = |forward| Fraction.clamp(forward.ratio_to(crown_shade_reach)).complement() ## A trunk of `color` under the crown of the tree whose outline is `outline`. trunk_shape : Camera.Upright, { finish : TrunkFinish, color : RgbColor } -> Shapes.Shape trunk_shape = |outline, { finish, color }| { width = outline.height_on_screen.scaled_by(trunk_width_share).max(min_trunk_width) below_crown = outline.height_on_screen.scaled_by(trunk_height_share) height = below_crown.plus(outline.height_on_screen.scaled_by(trunk_overlap_share)) left = outline.foot.x.minus(width.divided_by(2.0)) fill = match finish { Shaded => Brush.width_shade( { min_x: left, max_x: left.plus(width) }, { color, strength: Fraction.whole }, ) Flat => Brush.flat(color) } Shapes.rectangle({ top_left: { x: left, y: outline.foot.y.minus(height) }, width, height, fill, }) } ## A tier as a flat triangle: its apex at the tier's top, its base across its ## bottom. tier_triangle : Camera.Upright, { tier : Tier, foliage_color : RgbColor } -> Shapes.Shape tier_triangle = |outline, { tier, foliage_color }| { crown_top = crown_top_y(outline) bottom_y = crown_top.plus(crown_height(outline).scaled_by(tier.bottom)) top_y = crown_top.plus(crown_height(outline).scaled_by(tier.top)) half_base = crown_half_width(outline).scaled_by(tier.width) Triangle({ first: { x: outline.foot.x, y: top_y }, second: { x: outline.foot.x.plus(half_base), y: bottom_y }, third: { x: outline.foot.x.minus(half_base), y: bottom_y }, fill: Brush.flat(foliage_color), }) } ## The angles of a cone's ring, from 0 round a whole turn. Each is the one ## before plus a step, not a multiple of the step: the two round differently. ring_angles : List(F64) ring_angles = { step = F64.tau / ring_point_count.to_f64() var $angle = 0.0 var $angles = [] for _ in 0..<ring_point_count { $angles = $angles.append($angle) $angle = $angle + step } $angles } ## The cosine and sine of each of the ring's angles, worked out once rather ## than for every tier of every tree. ring_units : List({ cos : F64, sin : F64 }) ring_units = ring_angles.map(|angle| { cos: angle.cos(), sin: angle.sin() }) ## A tier, as a cone when the tree's `crown` is cones and the ring round the ## cone's base is at or past the near plane, else as a triangle. tier_shape : Tier, { inputs : TierInputs, crown : TreeShapes.Crown } -> Shapes.Shape tier_shape = |tier, { inputs, crown }| { colored_tier = { tier, foliage_color: inputs.foliage_color } match crown { Cones({ shade }) => { radius_share = crown_half_width_share.to_f64() * tier.width.to_f64() cone_radius = inputs.height.times(radius_share) match cone_ring_points(tier, { inputs, cone_radius }) { Ok(ring_points) => tier_cone(tier, { inputs, ring_points, shade }) Err(BehindCamera) => tier_triangle(inputs.outline, colored_tier) } } Triangles => tier_triangle(inputs.outline, colored_tier) } } ## How high above the ground a point `down` the crown is, as a fraction of the ## crown's height down from its tip: the tree's base, then the trunk's share of ## its height, then the crown's share less the part above the point. height_down_crown : TierInputs, Fraction -> Distance height_down_crown = |inputs, down| { trunk_part = trunk_height_share.to_f64() crown_part = crown_height_share.to_f64() inputs.base.height().plus(inputs.height.times(trunk_part + crown_part * (1.0 - down.to_f64()))) } ## The ring of points round a tier's base, `cone_radius` out from the tree's ## middle, if every one of them is at or past the near plane. cone_ring_points : Tier, { inputs : TierInputs, cone_radius : Distance, } -> Try(List(RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead), [BehindCamera]) cone_ring_points = |tier, { inputs, cone_radius }| { base = inputs.base ring_height = height_down_crown(inputs, tier.bottom) RiderView.points_at_height_ahead( ring_units.map( |unit| { right: base.right().plus(cone_radius.times(unit.cos)), forward: base.forward().plus(cone_radius.times(unit.sin)), height: ring_height, }, ), ) } ## A tier as a cone: the hull of the ring round its base and its apex. tier_cone : Tier, { inputs : TierInputs, ring_points : List(RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead), shade : Fraction, } -> Shapes.Shape tier_cone = |tier, { inputs, ring_points, shade }| { apex_height = height_down_crown(inputs, tier.top) apex = Camera.project(inputs.base.at_height(apex_height), inputs.focal_length) ring_on_screen = Camera.projected_points(ring_points, inputs.focal_length) corners = ConvexHull.cone_hull_points(ring_on_screen, apex) fill = Brush.corners_shade(corners, { color: inputs.foliage_color, strength: shade }) Shapes.region_from_corners(corners, fill) } expect crown_shade(Distance.metres(0.0)).to_f64() == 1.0 expect crown_shade(Distance.metres(20.0)).to_f64() == 0.75 expect crown_shade(Distance.metres(40.0)).to_f64() == 0.5 expect crown_shade(Distance.metres(80.0)).to_f64() == 0.0 expect crown_shade(Distance.metres(200.0)).to_f64() == 0.0 expect crown_shade(Distance.metres(-50.0)).to_f64() == 1.0 expect TreeShapes.crown_of(Distance.metres(40.0)) == Cones({ shade: Fraction.of(0.5) }) expect TreeShapes.crown_of(Distance.metres(199.0)) == Cones({ shade: Fraction.zero }) expect TreeShapes.crown_of(Distance.metres(200.0)) == Triangles expect [0.0, 59.9].all(|metres| trunk_finish_of(Distance.metres(metres)) == Shaded) expect [60.0, 60.1].all(|metres| trunk_finish_of(Distance.metres(metres)) == Flat) ## The sample tree's base, the middle of its foot, at `lift` off the ground. sample_base : Distance -> RiderView.PointAtHeightAhead sample_base = |lift| RiderView.point_at_height_ahead({ right: Distance.metres(0.0), forward: Distance.metres(2.0), height: lift, }) ?? crash "the sample tree is past the near plane" sample_height : Distance sample_height = Distance.metres(4.352) sample_outline : Camera.Upright sample_outline = Camera.upright_on_screen( sample_base(Distance.zero), { height: sample_height, focal_length: Pixels.of(500.0) }, ) # A lifted tree's cones measure from its foot: the ring under the bottom tier # sits the trunk's share of the height above the foot, which here is 2 m up. expect { base = sample_base(Distance.metres(2.0)) height = sample_height focal_length = Pixels.of(500.0) inputs = { base, height, focal_length, outline: TreeShapes.tree_outline(base, { height, focal_length }), foliage_color: RgbColor.of(7), } bottom_tier = tiers.last() ?? crash "a tree has tiers" want = 2.0 + 4.352 * 55.0 / 136.0 is_at_want = |point| (point.height().to_metres() - want).abs() <= 0.000000001 match cone_ring_points(bottom_tier, { inputs, cone_radius: Distance.metres(1.0) }) { Ok(ring_points) => ring_points.len() == ring_point_count and ring_points.all(is_at_want) Err(BehindCamera) => False } } ## Whether two lists of coordinates agree, past rounding. is_near : List(F64), List(F64) -> Bool is_near = |got, expected| got.len() == expected.len() and got.map2( expected, |x, y| (x - y).abs(), ).all(|miss| miss <= 0.000000001) expect is_near( [ sample_outline.foot.x.to_f64(), sample_outline.foot.y.to_f64(), sample_outline.height_on_screen.to_f64(), crown_height(sample_outline).to_f64(), crown_half_width(sample_outline).to_f64(), ], [480.0, 600.0, 1088.0, 648.0, 288.0], ) ## A quad's four corners in order, each as its x and its y, as plain numbers. quad_numbers : { first : Point, second : Point, third : Point, fourth : Point, .., } -> List(F64) quad_numbers = |{ first, second, third, fourth, .. }| [first, second, third, fourth].join_map(|corner| [corner.x.to_f64(), corner.y.to_f64()]) ## The sample trunk's corners, clockwise from its top left: 80 px wide from 440 ## px across, and 490 px tall from 110 px down. sample_trunk_numbers : List(F64) sample_trunk_numbers = [440.0, 110.0, 520.0, 110.0, 520.0, 600.0, 440.0, 600.0] expect { trunk_brown = { r: 0x5A, g: 0x3E, b: 0x22, a: 1.0, } match trunk_shape(sample_outline, { finish: Flat, color: trunk_color }) { Quad(trunk) => trunk.fill == Flat(trunk_brown) and is_near(quad_numbers(trunk), sample_trunk_numbers) _ => False } } # A shaded trunk is the same colour, lighter in the middle of its width. expect { edge_brown = { r: 0x36, g: 0x25, b: 0x14, a: 1.0, } middle_brown = { r: 0x71, g: 0x4E, b: 0x2B, a: 1.0, } match trunk_shape(sample_outline, { finish: Shaded, color: trunk_color }) { Quad(trunk) => match trunk.fill { Span({ edge_color, middle_color, left_x, right_x }) => edge_color == edge_brown and middle_color == middle_brown and is_near([left_x, right_x].map(Pixels.to_f64), [440.0, 520.0]) and is_near(quad_numbers(trunk), sample_trunk_numbers) _ => False } _ => False } } expect { corners_of = |tier| match tier_triangle(sample_outline, { tier, foliage_color: RgbColor.of(7) }) { Triangle(t) => [t.first, t.second, t.third].join_map( |corner| [corner.x.to_f64(), corner.y.to_f64()], ) _ => crash "a tier is one triangle" } top_tier = tiers.first() ?? crash "a tree has tiers" bottom_tier = tiers.last() ?? crash "a tree has tiers" [ (top_tier, [480.0, -488.0, 580.8, -293.6, 379.2, -293.6]), (bottom_tier, [480.0, -34.4, 768.0, 160.0, 192.0, 160.0]), ].all(|(tier, want)| is_near(corners_of(tier), want)) }

name: canvas_apps/safari/TreeSighting.roc
html: ## TreeSighting finds the roadside trees the rider can see in a frame: those ## placed along the segments in view that stand in front of the camera and are ## tall enough on screen to draw. They are worked out each frame from the ## rider's camera and the route. import Conifer import RoadAhead import Pipeline TreeSighting :: [].{ ## The trees in view, segment by segment in the order of ## `RoadAhead.segments_in_view`, and each segment's in the order `Trees` ## places them. trees_in_view : RoadAhead.RoadView, Pipeline.SightingCamera -> List(Pipeline.Sighted(Conifer)) trees_in_view = |road, camera| RoadAhead.segments_in_view(road).join_map( |in_view| segment_trees(road, { camera, in_view }), ) } ## The trees in view on a segment in view. segment_trees : RoadAhead.RoadView, { camera : Pipeline.SightingCamera, in_view : RoadAhead.SegmentInView, } -> List(Pipeline.Sighted(Conifer)) segment_trees = |road, { camera, in_view }| in_view.segment.trees.keep_oks( |tree| Pipeline.scenery_sighting_of(tree, { road, camera, from_rider: in_view.from_rider }), )

name: canvas_apps/safari/Truck.roc
html: ## Truck is the truck as the scene draws it this frame: its lights' states, and ## its sprite. Its sprite is its headlight beams first, then its body, then ## its brake lights, so each paints over the one before. It is worked out each ## frame from the clock and the truck's progress. import Sprite import TruckBody import TruckBrakeLights import TruckHeadlights ## Which of the truck's lights are on. Truck := { headlights : TruckHeadlights, brake_lights : TruckBrakeLights }.{ is_eq : _ ## How the truck looks in `setting`: its beams, its body, then its brake ## lights. scenery_sprite : Truck, Sprite.Setting -> Sprite scenery_sprite = |truck, setting| Sprite.composite([ truck.headlights.sprite(setting), TruckBody.body_sprite(setting), truck.brake_lights.sprite(setting), ]) }

name: canvas_apps/safari/TruckBody.roc
html: ## TruckBody gives the sprite of the truck's body: every face of its shape, ## placed at its spot, dimmed as far as the sky has darkened, and projected. ## The shapes come sorted far to near, so a nearer face drawn later covers a ## farther one. import Camera import DepthSort import Distance import Sky import Sprite import TruckPlacement import TruckShape TruckBody :: [].{ ## The truck's body in `setting`, its farthest faces first. body_sprite : Sprite.Setting -> Sprite body_sprite = |setting| { placed_faces = TruckShape.truck_faces.map( |face| TruckPlacement.placed_face(setting.spot, face), ) faces_far_to_near = DepthSort.sort_by(placed_faces, face_depth) dimmed_faces = faces_far_to_near.map( |face| { ..face, color: Sky.color_at_darkness(face.color, setting.darkness) }, ) Sprite.from_shapes( dimmed_faces.keep_oks(|face| Camera.clipped_polygon(face, setting.focal_length)), ) } } ## How far ahead a placed face is, for the sort: the mean of its corners' ## distances ahead. face_depth : Camera.FlatPolygon -> Distance face_depth = |face| DepthSort.mean_depth(face.corners.map(|corner| corner.forward))

name: canvas_apps/safari/TruckBrakeLights.roc
html: ## TruckBrakeLights is whether the truck's brake lights are on, and how they ## look: two lamps on the back of the trailer, each with a glow around it. They ## are worked out each frame from the truck's progress, which says whether its ## last step slowed it. import Distance import Sprite import lib.Point import lib.Pixels import RiderView import Camera import Screen import TruckJourney import TruckPlacement import TruckShape import lib.ArgbColor import lib.Brush import lib.RgbColor import lib.Shapes ## Whether the truck's brake lights are lit. TruckBrakeLights := [On, Off].{ is_eq : _ ## The brake lights of a truck going at `pace`: on while its last step ## slowed it. at : TruckJourney.Pace -> TruckBrakeLights at = |pace| match pace { Slowing => On NotSlowing => Off } ## How the brake lights look: the two lamps and their glows while they are ## on, and nothing while they are off. sprite : TruckBrakeLights, Sprite.Setting -> Sprite sprite = |brake_lights, setting| match brake_lights { On => Sprite.from_shapes(lamp_pair_shapes(setting)) Off => Sprite.from_shapes([]) } } ## A brake lamp sits near a side of the trailer's back, in its lower half, ## where a real trailer carries its lamps. Its edges are set as shares of ## the truck's size, chosen by eye, so the lamps keep their place on the ## back as the truck's measurements change. brake_lamp_outer_edge : Distance brake_lamp_outer_edge = TruckShape.truck_width.times(0.1) brake_lamp_inner_edge : Distance brake_lamp_inner_edge = TruckShape.truck_width.times(0.36) brake_lamp_bottom : Distance brake_lamp_bottom = TruckShape.trailer_bottom.plus(TruckShape.trailer_height.times(0.2)) brake_lamp_top : Distance brake_lamp_top = TruckShape.trailer_bottom.plus(TruckShape.trailer_height.times(0.5)) brake_color : RgbColor brake_color = RgbColor.of(0xFF2A18) glow_core : ArgbColor glow_core = ArgbColor.of(0xE6FF503C) ## The glow fades out to the brake lamp's own colour at no opacity. glow_edge : ArgbColor glow_edge = ArgbColor.from_rgb(brake_color, { alpha: 0 }) ## A glow reaches this many times as far as its lamp's farthest corner, a ## reach chosen by eye. glow_reach : F64 glow_reach = 3.2 ## The two brake lights, one in from each side of the trailer's back. lamp_pair_shapes : Sprite.Setting -> List(Shapes.Shape) lamp_pair_shapes = |setting| { box = TruckShape.truck_box left_lamp_sides = { left: box.left.plus(brake_lamp_outer_edge), right: box.left.plus(brake_lamp_inner_edge), } right_lamp_sides = { left: box.right.minus(brake_lamp_inner_edge), right: box.right.minus(brake_lamp_outer_edge), } brake_shapes(setting, left_lamp_sides).concat(brake_shapes(setting, right_lamp_sides)) } ## The center of a polygon on screen: the mean of its corners. Each sum ## runs from the last corner to the first; a float sum's rounding depends ## on its order, and another order can move a pixel. center_of : List(Point) -> Point center_of = |corners| { count = corners.len().to_f64() { x: corners.fold_rev(Pixels.zero, |corner, sum| corner.x.plus(sum)).divided_by(count), y: corners.fold_rev(Pixels.zero, |corner, sum| corner.y.plus(sum)).divided_by(count), } } ## How far a brake light's glow reaches from `center`, the lamp's ## center. glow_radius : List(Point), Point -> Pixels glow_radius = |lamp_points, center| Screen.farthest_distance(lamp_points, center).times(glow_reach) ## A brake light on the back of the trailer, its sides `left` and `right` ## measured rightward of the truck's centre line: its glow, then the lamp ## over the glow. brake_shapes : Sprite.Setting, { left : Distance, right : Distance } -> List(Shapes.Shape) brake_shapes = |setting, lamp_sides| { rear = TruckShape.truck_box.rear lamp = TruckShape.strip_corners( lamp_sides, { near: { ahead: rear, height: brake_lamp_bottom }, far: { ahead: rear, height: brake_lamp_top }, }, ).map(|corner| TruckPlacement.point_at_height(setting.spot, corner)) glow_shapes = match brake_glow(setting, lamp) { Ok(glow) => [glow] Err(BehindCamera) | Err(TooSmall) => [] } match Camera.clipped_polygon({ color: brake_color, corners: lamp }, setting.focal_length) { Ok(lamp_polygon) => glow_shapes.append(lamp_polygon) Err(BehindCamera) => glow_shapes } } ## The glow round a brake lamp. A lamp with a corner behind the camera has ## no glow; the lamp itself is cut at the near plane like the body's faces. brake_glow : Sprite.Setting, List(RiderView.PointAtHeight) -> Try( Shapes.Shape, [BehindCamera, TooSmall], ) brake_glow = |setting, lamp_points| { lamp_ahead = RiderView.points_at_height_ahead(lamp_points)? on_screen = Camera.projected_points(lamp_ahead, setting.focal_length) center = center_of(on_screen) radius = glow_radius(on_screen, center) fill = Brush.circular_gradient({ center_color: glow_core, edge_color: glow_edge, center, radius, })? Ok(Disc({ center, radius, fill })) } expect TruckBrakeLights.at(Slowing) == On expect TruckBrakeLights.at(NotSlowing) == Off panel_points : List(Point) panel_points = [ Point.at(3.0, 4.0), Point.at(6.0, 8.0), Point.at(0.0, 0.0), Point.at(7.0, 4.0), ] triangle_points : List(Point) triangle_points = [ Point.at(0.0, 0.0), Point.at(3.0, 0.0), Point.at(0.0, 6.0), ] expect center_of(panel_points) == Point.at(4.0, 4.0) expect center_of(triangle_points) == Point.at(1.0, 2.0)

name: canvas_apps/safari/TruckHeadlights.roc
html: ## TruckHeadlights is whether the truck's headlights are on, and how they look: ## two beams reaching along the road ahead of the cab, each a little in from ## its side. They are worked out each frame from the clock, by way of the sky's ## darkness. import Camera import Distance import lib.Fraction import Sprite import RiderView import Screen import TruckPlacement import TruckShape import lib.ArgbColor import lib.Brush import lib.Shapes ## Whether the truck's headlights are lit. TruckHeadlights := [On, Off].{ is_eq : _ ## The headlights under a sky of `darkness`: on once the sky is dark ## enough, like a light sensor on the lamps. at : Fraction -> TruckHeadlights at = |darkness| if darkness >= headlights_on_darkness { On } else { Off } ## How the headlights look: their two beams while they are on, and nothing ## while they are off. sprite : TruckHeadlights, Sprite.Setting -> Sprite sprite = |headlights, setting| match headlights { On => Sprite.from_shapes(beam_shapes(setting)) Off => Sprite.from_shapes([]) } } ## The headlights come on once the sky is 41.2% dark, about when the sun sinks ## behind the west range. The value was measured once, on this ride; ## gates/expects/RideExpects.roc pins the step. headlights_on_darkness : Fraction headlights_on_darkness = Fraction.of(0.412) ## How high the headlights are, and how far in from the truck's sides. headlight_height : Distance headlight_height = Distance.metres(1.0) headlight_inset : Distance headlight_inset = Distance.metres(0.3) ## A beam is a vertical wedge from its lamp, widening to where it ends ## `beam_length` ahead of the cab's nose. beam_half_height_at_lamp : Distance beam_half_height_at_lamp = Distance.metres(0.25) beam_length : Distance beam_length = Distance.metres(20.4) beam_far_center : Distance beam_far_center = Distance.metres(0.7) beam_far_half_height : Distance beam_far_half_height = Distance.metres(0.9) ## The beam is one warm white, more opaque at the lamp than at its edge. beam_core : ArgbColor beam_core = ArgbColor.of(0xC3FFF8D6) beam_edge : ArgbColor beam_edge = ArgbColor.of(0x45FFF8D6) ## The two headlight beams, each a little in from its side. beam_shapes : Sprite.Setting -> List(Shapes.Shape) beam_shapes = |setting| { box = TruckShape.truck_box [ headlight_beam(setting, box.left.plus(headlight_inset)), headlight_beam(setting, box.right.minus(headlight_inset)), ].keep_oks(|beam| beam) } ## The beam of the headlight `rightward` of the truck's centre line, ## brightest at the lamp. A beam with a corner behind the camera is not ## drawn. headlight_beam : Sprite.Setting, Distance -> Try(Shapes.Shape, [BehindCamera, TooSmall]) headlight_beam = |setting, rightward| { nose = TruckShape.truck_box.nose on_truck = |ahead, height| TruckPlacement.point_at_height( setting.spot, { ahead, rightward, height }, ) at_lamp = |height| on_truck(nose, height) at_far_end = |height| on_truck(nose.plus(beam_length), height) lamp_bottom = at_lamp(headlight_height.minus(beam_half_height_at_lamp)) lamp_top = at_lamp(headlight_height.plus(beam_half_height_at_lamp)) far_top = at_far_end(beam_far_center.plus(beam_far_half_height)) far_bottom = at_far_end(beam_far_center.minus(beam_far_half_height)) corners = RiderView.points_at_height_ahead([lamp_bottom, lamp_top, far_top, far_bottom])? lamp = RiderView.point_at_height_ahead(at_lamp(headlight_height))? on_screen = Camera.projected_points(corners, setting.focal_length) lamp_on_screen = Camera.project(lamp, setting.focal_length) fill = Brush.circular_gradient({ center_color: beam_core, edge_color: beam_edge, center: lamp_on_screen, radius: Screen.farthest_distance(on_screen, lamp_on_screen), })? Ok(Shapes.region_from_corners(on_screen, fill)) } expect TruckHeadlights.at(Fraction.of(0.4119)) == Off expect TruckHeadlights.at(headlights_on_darkness) == On expect TruckHeadlights.at(Fraction.of(0.4121)) == On expect TruckHeadlights.at(Fraction.zero) == Off expect TruckHeadlights.at(Fraction.whole) == On # The headlight's lamp lies on the cab's nose face, above the cab's floor and # below its hood. expect headlight_height.minus(beam_half_height_at_lamp) >= TruckShape.cab_bottom expect headlight_height.plus(beam_half_height_at_lamp) <= TruckShape.hood_height

name: canvas_apps/safari/TruckJourney.roc
html: ## TruckJourney is the truck's travel along the route, as the rider chases it. ## The truck teases him: it starts well ahead and lets him close in over the ## whole route, unevenly, as if the driver saw him. The tease is ## `tease_position`, and plain physics carries it out: the truck speeds up while ## it is short of the tease, holds its speed otherwise, and slows for a turn when ## one is close. Its `TruckJourney.TruckProgress` is kept from one step to the ## next, one of the four things the ride remembers. import Acceleration import Angle import Distance import lib.Fraction import Route import Speed import VehicleLimits TruckJourney :: [].{ ## How far along the route the truck is, how fast it is going, and whether ## its last step slowed it. Nominal, not opaque: other modules read its ## fields. TruckProgress := { route_position : Distance, speed : Speed, pace : TruckJourney.Pace, } ## Whether the truck's last step slowed it. Pace := [Slowing, NotSlowing].{ is_eq : _ } initial : TruckJourney.TruckProgress initial = { route_position: tease_start_lead, speed: VehicleLimits.starting_speed, pace: NotSlowing, } ## The truck's progress one step on: where the rider is along the route, ## and the route itself, decide its pace. truck_progress_at_next_step : TruckJourney.TruckProgress, { rider_distance : Distance, route : Route, } -> TruckJourney.TruckProgress truck_progress_at_next_step = |progress, { rider_distance, route }| { tease = tease_position({ rider_distance, route_length: route.route_length() }) match next_bend(route, progress.route_position) { BendAhead(bend) => if bend.distance <= brake_distance { progress_braking_for(progress, bend) } else { progress_toward_tease(progress, tease) } NoBendAhead => progress_toward_tease(progress, tease) } } } ## A bend ahead of the truck: how far off it is, and how sharply it turns. ComingBend : { distance : Distance, turn : Angle.Turn } ## The next bend of the route past a point, or none: the route ends first. NextBend : [BendAhead(ComingBend), NoBendAhead] ## How far ahead of the rider the tease puts the truck at the route's start. tease_start_lead : Distance tease_start_lead = Distance.metres(500.0) ## How far ahead of the rider the tease puts the truck at the route's end. tease_finish_lead : Distance tease_finish_lead = Distance.metres(100.0) ## The truck takes a bend at this fraction of the speed the bend allows, to ## leave a margin. turn_caution : Fraction turn_caution = Fraction.of(0.8) ## The truck starts to brake when a bend is this close. brake_distance : Distance brake_distance = Distance.metres(60.0) ## The truck outdoes the rider by 10%, in both its acceleration and its top ## speed. chase_margin : F64 chase_margin = 1.1 ## The rider's own cruise acceleration, outdone by `chase_margin`. chase_acceleration : Acceleration chase_acceleration = VehicleLimits.cruise_acceleration.times(chase_margin) ## The rider's own top speed, outdone by `chase_margin`. chase_top_speed : Speed chase_top_speed = VehicleLimits.top_speed.times(chase_margin) ## The next bend of `route` past `route_position`. next_bend : Route, Distance -> NextBend next_bend = |route, route_position| match route.segments_with_ends().find_first(|stretch| route_position < stretch.end) { Ok({ segment, end }) => match segment.ending { Bends({ turn, .. }) => BendAhead({ distance: end.minus(route_position), turn }) RouteEnds => NoBendAhead } Err(NotFound) => NoBendAhead } ## The tease: where the truck aims to be along the route when the rider is ## `rider_distance` along it, so that the rider closes in on it over the whole ## route. The lead it aims for shrinks from `tease_start_lead` to ## `tease_finish_lead` in step with the rider's progress. The truck only chases ## this mark, and never slows to keep to it, so the real gap closes unevenly: the ## truck can run past the mark on a straight, and it slows for the bends. tease_position : { rider_distance : Distance, route_length : Distance } -> Distance tease_position = |{ rider_distance, route_length }| { fraction_left = 1.0 - rider_distance.ratio_to(route_length) extra_lead = tease_start_lead.minus(tease_finish_lead).times(fraction_left) rider_distance.plus(tease_finish_lead).plus(extra_lead) } ## The truck's progress one step on, slowing for `bend`, so that it reaches the ## bend at a cautious speed. progress_braking_for : TruckJourney.TruckProgress, ComingBend -> TruckJourney.TruckProgress progress_braking_for = |progress, bend| { target_speed = VehicleLimits.turn_speed(bend.turn).scaled_by(turn_caution) acceleration = VehicleLimits.braking_to( progress.speed, { target: target_speed, within: bend.distance }, ) # The steady brake may land a little under its target; `VehicleLimits.braking_to` # says why. The truck alone keeps to the target here. speed = target_speed.max(progress.speed.accelerated_by(acceleration)) { route_position: progress.route_position.plus(speed.step_length()), speed, pace: if speed < progress.speed { Slowing } else { NotSlowing }, } } ## The truck's progress one step on with no bend close: it speeds up while it ## is short of `tease`, and otherwise holds its speed. progress_toward_tease : TruckJourney.TruckProgress, Distance -> TruckJourney.TruckProgress progress_toward_tease = |progress, tease| { speed = if progress.route_position < tease { chase_top_speed.min(progress.speed.accelerated_by(chase_acceleration)) } else { progress.speed } { route_position: progress.route_position.plus(speed.step_length()), speed, pace: NotSlowing, } } ## Where the tease puts the truck, with the rider this far along a route ## 1000 m long. tease_at : F64 -> F64 tease_at = |rider_distance| tease_position({ rider_distance: Distance.metres(rider_distance), route_length: Distance.metres(1000.0), }).to_metres() expect tease_at(0.0) == 500.0 expect tease_at(250.0) == 650.0 expect tease_at(500.0) == 800.0 expect tease_at(1000.0) == 1100.0

name: canvas_apps/safari/TruckPlacement.roc
html: ## TruckPlacement stands the truck's shape at its spot. The truck is a solid ## thing that faces along the road, so each of its points stands through ## `Spot.standing_point`, turned by nothing beyond the road's own heading. import Angle import Camera import RiderView import Spot import TruckShape TruckPlacement :: [].{ ## Where a point on the truck stands in the rider's view, for a truck at ## `spot` facing along the road. point_at_height : Spot, TruckShape.TruckPoint -> RiderView.PointAtHeight point_at_height = |spot, point| spot.standing_point({ facing: Angle.straight_ahead, offset: point }) ## A face of the truck in the rider's view, every corner placed. placed_face : Spot, TruckShape.TruckFace -> Camera.FlatPolygon placed_face = |spot, { color, corners }| { color, corners: corners.map(|corner| TruckPlacement.point_at_height(spot, corner)), } }

name: canvas_apps/safari/TruckShape.roc
html: ## What the truck looks like, in its own frame and nowhere in the world: its ## size, its colors and its faces. It's blue, a navy body with darker sides ## and a lighter roof, on near-black tires. TruckPlacement stands it at its ## spot, and TruckBody, TruckHeadlights and TruckBrakeLights draw from these. import Distance import lib.Fraction import lib.RgbColor TruckShape :: [].{ ## The box the truck fills, in the truck's own frame. Four offsets run ## ahead of the trailer's center, from the back of the trailer to the front ## of the cab, so `rear` is negative. The two sides are offsets to the ## right of the trailer's center line, so `left` is negative. The cab's flat ## roof ends at `roof_front`, where its windshield slopes down to the nose. TruckBox : { rear : Distance, trailer_front : Distance, roof_front : Distance, nose : Distance, left : Distance, right : Distance, } ## A point on the truck, in the truck's own frame: how far ahead of the ## trailer's center and how far to the right of it, each negative the other ## way, and how high above the road under the truck. TruckPoint : { ahead : Distance, rightward : Distance, height : Distance, } ## A face of the truck: a color and its corners, in the truck's own frame. TruckFace : { color : RgbColor, corners : List(TruckShape.TruckPoint) } ## The truck's body, its back, nose and windshield. body_color : RgbColor body_color = RgbColor.of(0x1C2E66) roof_color : RgbColor roof_color = RgbColor.of(0x3A52A8) side_color : RgbColor side_color = RgbColor.of(0x152150) tire_color : RgbColor tire_color = RgbColor.of(0x15151A) ## The whole truck as it is built: its two sides, the trailer's back, its ## roof, the cab's windshield and nose, then its tires. truck_faces : List(TruckShape.TruckFace) truck_faces = [ sides, [trailer_back, roof, windshield, nose], tires, ].join() ## The truck's two sides, left then right. Each side is one outline, the ## trailer and the cab together: up the back of the trailer, along its roof ## and the cab's, down the windshield's edge and the nose, back along the ## cab's floor, and down to the trailer's floor. sides : List(TruckShape.TruckFace) sides = { box = truck_box [box.left, box.right].map( |rightward| { color: side_color, corners: [ { ahead: box.rear, rightward, height: trailer_bottom }, { ahead: box.rear, rightward, height: truck_height }, { ahead: box.roof_front, rightward, height: truck_height }, { ahead: box.nose, rightward, height: hood_height }, { ahead: box.nose, rightward, height: cab_bottom }, { ahead: box.trailer_front, rightward, height: cab_bottom }, { ahead: box.trailer_front, rightward, height: trailer_bottom }, ], }, ) } ## The back of the trailer, from its floor to its roof. trailer_back : TruckShape.TruckFace trailer_back = across_truck( body_color, { near: { ahead: truck_box.rear, height: trailer_bottom }, far: { ahead: truck_box.rear, height: truck_height }, }, ) ## The roof of the trailer and the cab, one flat face. roof : TruckShape.TruckFace roof = across_truck( roof_color, { near: { ahead: truck_box.rear, height: truck_height }, far: { ahead: truck_box.roof_front, height: truck_height }, }, ) ## The cab's windshield, sloping down from the roof to the nose. It is ## the body's color: there is no glass. windshield : TruckShape.TruckFace windshield = across_truck( body_color, { near: { ahead: truck_box.roof_front, height: truck_height }, far: { ahead: truck_box.nose, height: hood_height }, }, ) ## The cab's nose, from the hood down to the cab's floor. nose : TruckShape.TruckFace nose = across_truck( body_color, { near: { ahead: truck_box.nose, height: hood_height }, far: { ahead: truck_box.nose, height: cab_bottom }, }, ) ## A tire on each side of each axle, the left side's and then the right's. ## A tire is a circle standing on the road. tires : List(TruckShape.TruckFace) tires = { box = truck_box tire = |{ axle, rightward }| { color: tire_color, corners: TruckShape.circle_angles(tire_sides).map( |angle| { ahead: axle.plus(tire_radius.times(angle.cos())), rightward, height: tire_radius.plus(tire_radius.times(angle.sin())), }, ), } [ axles.map(|axle| tire({ axle, rightward: box.left })), axles.map(|axle| tire({ axle, rightward: box.right })), ].join() } truck_width : Distance truck_width = Distance.metres(2.4) truck_height : Distance truck_height = Distance.metres(3.6) cab_length : Distance cab_length = Distance.metres(3.5) tire_radius : Distance tire_radius = Distance.metres(0.5) ## The trailer's floor clears the top of its tires by 12 cm. trailer_bottom : Distance trailer_bottom = tire_radius.times(2.0).plus(Distance.metres(0.12)) ## The cab's floor is level with its axle. cab_bottom : Distance cab_bottom = tire_radius ## Where the windshield meets the nose: half the truck's height. hood_height : Distance hood_height = truck_height.divided_by(2.0) ## How tall the trailer is, from its floor to its roof. trailer_height : Distance trailer_height = truck_height.minus(trailer_bottom) ## The box the truck fills, in its own frame, centered where its trailer ## is; the cab is ahead of the trailer. truck_box : TruckShape.TruckBox truck_box = { trailer_front = trailer_length.divided_by(2.0) { rear: trailer_length.divided_by(2.0).opposite(), trailer_front, roof_front: trailer_front.plus(cab_length.scaled_by(cab_roof_fraction)), nose: trailer_front.plus(cab_length), left: truck_width.divided_by(2.0).opposite(), right: truck_width.divided_by(2.0), } } ## The four corners of a strip across the truck from `left` to `right`, ## between its `near` edge and its `far` edge: near left, near right, far ## right, far left. strip_corners : { left : Distance, right : Distance }, { near : { ahead : Distance, height : Distance }, far : { ahead : Distance, height : Distance }, } -> List(TruckShape.TruckPoint) strip_corners = |{ left, right }, { near, far }| [ { ahead: near.ahead, rightward: left, height: near.height, }, { ahead: near.ahead, rightward: right, height: near.height, }, { ahead: far.ahead, rightward: right, height: far.height, }, { ahead: far.ahead, rightward: left, height: far.height, }, ] ## The angles of the corners of a circle drawn as a polygon with ## `corner_count` corners, going round from angle 0. circle_angles : I64 -> List(F64) circle_angles = |corner_count| List.from_iter( I64.until(0, corner_count), ).map(|corner| corner.to_f64() / corner_count.to_f64() * F64.tau) } ## A face of `color` across the whole width of the truck, between its `near` ## edge and its `far` edge. across_truck : RgbColor, { near : { ahead : Distance, height : Distance }, far : { ahead : Distance, height : Distance }, } -> TruckShape.TruckFace across_truck = |color, edges| { color, corners: TruckShape.strip_corners( { left: TruckShape.truck_box.left, right: TruckShape.truck_box.right }, edges, ), } trailer_length : Distance trailer_length = Distance.metres(8.4) ## How far forward of the trailer the cab's flat roof reaches, as a fraction ## of the cab's length, a proportion chosen by eye. cab_roof_fraction : Fraction cab_roof_fraction = Fraction.of(0.3) ## A tire is drawn as a polygon with this many corners. tire_sides : I64 tire_sides = 16 ## How far in from each end of the trailer the middle of its pair of axles is. trailer_axle_inset : Distance trailer_axle_inset = Distance.metres(1.6) ## The distance between the two axles of a pair. axle_pair_gap : Distance axle_pair_gap = Distance.metres(1.2) ## How far forward of the trailer the cab's axle is, as a fraction of the ## cab's length. cab_axle_fraction : Fraction cab_axle_fraction = Fraction.of(0.55) ## How far ahead of the trailer's centre each of the truck's axles is, back ## to front: a pair under the back of the trailer, a pair under its front, ## and one under the cab. axles : List(Distance) axles = { box = TruckShape.truck_box back_pair = box.rear.plus(trailer_axle_inset) front_pair = box.trailer_front.minus(trailer_axle_inset) half_gap = axle_pair_gap.divided_by(2.0) [ back_pair.minus(half_gap), back_pair.plus(half_gap), front_pair.minus(half_gap), front_pair.plus(half_gap), box.trailer_front.plus(TruckShape.cab_length.scaled_by(cab_axle_fraction)), ] } expect TruckShape.strip_corners( { left: Distance.metres(-1.0), right: Distance.metres(1.0) }, { near: { ahead: Distance.metres(2.0), height: Distance.metres(3.0) }, far: { ahead: Distance.metres(5.0), height: Distance.metres(7.0) }, }, ).map( |corner| ( corner.ahead.to_metres(), corner.rightward.to_metres(), corner.height.to_metres(), ), ) == [ (2.0, -1.0, 3.0), (2.0, 1.0, 3.0), (5.0, 1.0, 7.0), (5.0, -1.0, 7.0), ] # The truck is its two sides, its back, roof, windshield and nose, and a tire # on each side of each of its five axles. expect TruckShape.truck_faces.len() == 16

name: canvas_apps/safari/World.roc
html: ## The ride's world is its route, planned as a list of segments. Each plan says ## how long its segment is, what grows and grazes along it, what the rider meets ## on it, and how it turns into the next. The route makes some choices across ## its segments, such as which herds are big and which the rider finds ## distracting, and this module resolves them before each segment is built. ## ## The world is built once and never changes during the ride. It holds these. ## The route is a list of segments, each known by its place in the list, a ## `Route.SegmentIndex` counted from 0; `World.route` builds it from ## `World.segment_plans`, and `Route.from_segments` checks that every segment ## but the last bends. ## A segment's trees are a list, each tree known by where it stands on its ## segment, along and across the road; `Trees.roadside_trees` plants them from ## the segment's scheme and length. ## A segment has at most one herd of pigs, whose shape and whether it distracts ## the rider `built_segment` chooses here, and one herd of cows, led by a bull or ## not; each animal's place is worked out from its herd when it is asked for ## (`Segment.segment_pigs`, `Segment.segment_cows`), not kept. ## A segment has one encounter, a cat crossing, a bird's flight or a quiet road, ## and `Segment.from_choices` places the cat by one of its trees and the bird on ## another. ## A segment ends by bending into the next, with its turn and what lives at the ## bend (an animal and its baby, a pond with its ducks, or nothing), or by ending ## the route; a pond is known by the segment whose bend it lies at, and its ## ducks, like the animal, are placed from that bend. ## Towers aren't kept at all: each follows from its segment, one past the end of ## every segment and one halfway along a segment longer than a kilometre, so a ## tower is known by its segment and its place on it, a `Beacon.TowerKey`. import Angle import BirdFlight import CatCrossing import CowHerd import Distance import PigHerd import RoadAhead import Route import Segment import Trees World :: [].{ ## Whether the route plans pigs along a segment. PigPresence : [WithPigs, NoPigs] ## One segment of the route as planned: its length and scenery, and what ## lives along it. SegmentPlan : { length : Distance, scheme : Trees.Scheme, encounter : Segment.PlannedEncounter, pigs : World.PigPresence, bull : CowHerd.Bull, } ## A segment the route plans to bend into the next: the segment's own plan, ## its turn into the next (right is positive), and what lives at the bend. BendingPlan : { segment_plan : World.SegmentPlan, turn : Angle.Turn, bend_life : Segment.BendLife, } ## Every segment of the route but the last, in order, each with its bend. bending_plans : List(World.BendingPlan) bending_plans = [ { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(500.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: BirdHere, pigs: NoPigs, bull: NoBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(50.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(320.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: NoPigs, bull: NoBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(-70.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(400.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: BirdHere, pigs: WithPigs, bull: NoBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(20.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: GoldGreen, encounter: CatCrosses, pigs: NoPigs, bull: NoBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(20.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: NoPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(-70.0), bend_life: Animal(Giraffe), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: BirdHere, pigs: NoPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(-70.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(1200.0), scheme: RedGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: NoPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(80.0), bend_life: Animal(Rhino), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: NoPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(15.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: NoPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(-70.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(800.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: CatCrosses, pigs: NoPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(15.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: WithPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(15.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: WithPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(15.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: RedGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: WithPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(15.0), bend_life: DuckPond, }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(400.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: WithPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(-50.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: BirdHere, pigs: WithPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(50.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: RedGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: NoPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(-50.0), bend_life: Animal(Zebra), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: WithPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(50.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, { segment_plan: { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: AllGreen, encounter: QuietRoad, pigs: WithPigs, bull: WithBull, }, turn: Angle.Turn.degrees(-50.0), bend_life: Animal(Elephant), }, ] ## Every segment's plan, in order. segment_plans : List(World.SegmentPlan) segment_plans = bending_plans.map(|bending| bending.segment_plan).append(last_plan) ## The route, built from its plans. Each segment but the last bends as its ## plan says, and the last ends the route. route : Route route = { bending_segments = bending_plans.map_with_index( |{ segment_plan, turn, bend_life }, at| { index = Route.SegmentIndex.from_count_before(at) built_segment(segment_plan, { index, ending: Bends({ turn, bend_life }) }) }, ) last_index = Route.SegmentIndex.from_count_before(bending_plans.len()) last_segment = built_segment(last_plan, { index: last_index, ending: RouteEnds }) Route.from_segments(bending_segments.append(last_segment)) } ## The road ahead of a rider on the route's first segment. What stands on ## that segment has no bend between it and the rider. road_at_start : RoadAhead.RoadView road_at_start = RoadAhead.RoadView.ahead_of(World.route, Route.SegmentIndex.first) ## The route's first segment with a cat. first_cat_segment : Segment first_cat_segment = World.route.route_segments().find_first( |segment| match segment.encounter { CatCrosses(_) => True BirdHere(_) | QuietRoad => False }, ) ?? crash "World.first_cat_segment: the route has a cat" ## The cat crossing on the route's first segment with a cat. first_cat_crossing : CatCrossing first_cat_crossing = match World.first_cat_segment.encounter { CatCrosses(crossing) => crossing BirdHere(_) | QuietRoad => crash "World.first_cat_crossing: the first cat segment has a cat" } ## The bird's flight on the route's first segment with a bird. first_bird_flight : BirdFlight first_bird_flight = match first_bird_segment.encounter { BirdHere(flight) => flight CatCrosses(_) | QuietRoad => crash "World.first_bird_flight: the first bird segment has a bird" } ## The route's first segment whose pigs draw the rider's eye. first_distracting_segment : Segment first_distracting_segment = World.route.route_segments().find_first(Segment.has_distracting_pigs) ?? crash "World.first_distracting_segment: the route has a distracting herd" } ## The route's last segment, which ends it. last_plan : World.SegmentPlan last_plan = { length: Distance.metres(300.0), scheme: RedGreen, encounter: CatCrosses, pigs: WithPigs, bull: WithBull, } ## The route's first segment with a bird. first_bird_segment : Segment first_bird_segment = World.route.route_segments().find_first( |segment| match segment.encounter { BirdHere(_) => True CatCrosses(_) | QuietRoad => False }, ) ?? crash "World.first_bird_segment: the route has a bird" ## The segment at `index` of the route, built from its plan once the route's ## choices for it are made: the shape of its herd and whether the rider finds it ## distracting, both from how many herds come before it, and how it ends, from ## its place in the route. built_segment : World.SegmentPlan, { index : Route.SegmentIndex, ending : Segment.Ending, } -> Segment built_segment = |plan, { index, ending }| { earlier_herd_count = herd_count_before(index) pigs = match plan.pigs { WithPigs => { herd = if earlier_herd_count < big_herd_count { PigHerd.BigHerd(big_pig_herd) } else { PigHerd.TwoRows } interest = if earlier_herd_count < pig_novelty_count { Distracting } else { Unnoticed } Herd({ herd, interest }) } NoPigs => NoPigs } Segment.from_choices({ length: plan.length, scheme: plan.scheme, pigs, cows: { herd: cow_herd, bull: plan.bull }, encounter: plan.encounter, ending, }) } ## How many of the route's herds, from its first, are big. The rest stand in ## two rows. big_herd_count : U64 big_herd_count = 2 ## How many of the route's herds, from its first, the rider finds distracting. ## The rider passes the rest by. pig_novelty_count : U64 pig_novelty_count = 2 ## The route's big herd, seven rows of seven.
